Title: The Road Ahead: A Tesla Car for the Masses?
Summary: During the Detroit Auto Show, Tesla's VP of engineering, Peter Rawlinson, discussed the company's "emphasis on process" and the engineering prowess behind the upcoming Model S. He explained that the Model S would serve as an affordable platform for future Tesla vehicles, designed to appeal to a broader market beyond current high-end models. Rawlinson believes that their unique engineering approach, focusing on integrated teamwork, will overcome skepticism despite the Model S's initial $57,000 base price.

Title: Five Questions: Peter Rawlinson, Tesla Motors Chief Engineer
Summary: Peter Rawlinson, Tesla Motors' chief engineer, discusses the company's message at the 2011 Detroit Auto Show, emphasizing its status as a real car company. He elaborates on the Model S's aluminum-intensive structure, the "alpha" and "beta" design phases, and the challenges of developing a new car and team simultaneously, particularly highlighting the innovative battery pack integration. Rawlinson expresses confidence in the Model S's development, with crash tests scheduled to begin soon.

Title: 2012 Tesla Model S moves toward production
Summary: New video of the 2012 Tesla Model S sedan shows it moving towards production, with an expected market arrival next year. The car boasts a 300-mile range, 0-60 mph in 5.6 seconds, seating for seven, and a 17-inch touchscreen. It is currently in alpha testing.

Title: Tesla’s Model S Alpha Takes to the Streets [VIDEO]
Summary: Fast Company shares a video of Tesla's Model S Alpha, an electric sedan priced at $57,000, performing on the streets. This alpha version precedes a beta version and a full release scheduled for mid-2012. The article highlights the car's performance capabilities and provides an update from Tesla's VP of engineering, Peter Rawlinson.

Title: Tesla Model S Update: Alpha Testing On Track, Deliveries Mid-2012
Summary: The Tesla Model S alpha testing is progressing as planned, with beta model assembly starting later this year and North American deliveries expected by mid-2012. The first 1,000 units will be a special Signature Series with a 300-mile range, followed by regular production which includes 230- and 160-mile battery options later in 2012. Pricing starts at $49,900 for the 160-mile version (after tax credit), with European and right-hand-drive markets receiving deliveries later.

Title: An Inside Look at Tesla’s Model S
Summary: Fast Company visited Tesla Motors headquarters to observe the development of their mass-market vehicle, the Model S electric sedan. The article details features like its ultra-light, swap-compatible battery pack with a 300-mile range and 45-minute recharge time, and also mentions executives such as JB Straubel and Peter Rawlinson.

Title: Update: Tesla, Top Gear Continue Verbal Spat Over Libel Suit
Summary: Tesla Motors and Top Gear are engaged in a libel suit stemming from an episode featuring the Tesla Roadster. Top Gear's executive producer, Andy Wilman, released a blog post refuting Tesla's claims of false and exaggerated criticisms regarding the car's range, overheating engine, and brakes. Tesla responded, asserting that Top Gear needs to provide straightforward answers and that Tesla wants to correct public misperceptions of its electric two-seater.

Title: Exclusive Tour Of Tesla’s Showroom With Apple’s Retail Guru [Video]
Summary: George Blankenship, Apple's former retail guru, has designed Tesla Motors' first showroom in San Jose, California, aiming to replicate the Apple Store's success. The showroom features sleek design, interactive touchscreens for car customization, and is strategically located in an upscale shopping district to attract wealthy buyers. Blankenship's goal is to make buying an expensive electric car as appealing and accessible as Apple products.

Title: Tesla Motors Opens Showroom On San Jose's Santana Row
Summary: Tesla Motors has opened a new showroom on San Jose's Santana Row, aiming to redefine the car buying experience. The store features interactive displays and the all-electric Roadster, which sells for about $100,000. This move is part of the company's strategy to make car shopping as appealing as visiting an Apple Store.

Title: Elon Musk Says Tesla Won't Be Sold, But Elon Musk Is Wrong
Summary: Despite Elon Musk's assertions that Tesla would not be sold, the company announced a new share offering, with Musk himself and Daimler subsidiary Blackstar Investco buying significant shares. Industry analysts largely dismiss the idea of Tesla remaining independent long-term, citing the capital-intensive nature of carmaking and the strength of global giants. Many suggest Tesla's best chance for longevity is through partnerships, with Toyota and possibly Daimler vying for influence.

Title: New photos of Tesla Model S show more aggressive style
Summary: New photos of the Tesla Model S Alpha sedan reveal a more aggressive design with a sharper front fascia and vents, moving closer to its production look. The first Model S Alpha vehicles are scheduled for delivery in mid-2012 at an estimated price of $57,000, with over 4,600 reservations already taken.

Title: CEO Musk: 2011 Tesla Roadster Electric Sports Cars Are Gone, Almost
Summary: Tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, announced that production of the 2011 Tesla Roadster is winding down, with only a "handful of cars" left for U.S. buyers and a few more months for European and Japanese orders. The company is shifting its focus to the upcoming Model S sedan and a new crossover concept, Model X. The Roadster, which started at $109,000, was crucial in demonstrating the viability of high-performance electric vehicles.

Title: The End Of An Era: Roadster To Be Discontinued, But Tesla Not Done With Electric Supercars
Summary: Tesla is discontinuing its Roadster model after selling 1,650 units worldwide, shifting its focus to the more affordable Model S set to launch in 2012. Despite this, Tesla assures that it plans to release another electric supercar in the future, emphasizing the Roadster's role in proving the viability of high-performance EVs. The company's next challenge is to appeal to a mass market with the Model S, which is still considered pricey.

Title: 2012 Tesla Model S Spied Testing In Palo Alto
Summary: A prototype of the 2012 Tesla Model S was spotted testing in Palo Alto, California, showing what appears to be the most production-ready version yet. Key changes from the Alpha build include more realistic tail lights, recessed door handles, and enlarged side mirrors. Production of the Model S is anticipated to begin in mid-2012.

Title: Tesla Model S Customer Blog: Regenerative Braking And Its Discontents
Summary: A Tesla Model S reservation holder discusses a preview event where new technical details about the Model S were revealed, focusing on regenerative braking and battery specifications. The author expresses concerns about the strong, non-adjustable regenerative braking reminiscent of the Roadster and details the pricing and effective range of the different battery pack options. The article also touches on cosmetic options like wheel sizes and anticipates beta prototype test drives.

Title: Toyota RAV4 EV production set for Ontario, Canada
Summary: Toyota Motor North America senior vice-president Ray Tanguay has confirmed that all 2012 RAV4 EV models for the U.S. will be manufactured in Woodstock, Ontario, Canada, sharing a production line with the gasoline-powered RAV4. Tesla will supply the electric powertrains from its facility in Palo Alto, California, to the Canadian plant for final assembly. This move streamlines production and ensures quality control for the jointly developed electric vehicle.

Title: 2012 Tesla Model S: Photo Gallery
Summary: This article presents a photo gallery of the 2012 Tesla Model S beta vehicle, taken at the Fremont, California factory. Tesla Motors opened its factory to a select group of customers, reservation holders, and journalists to showcase and offer rides in the upcoming all-electric sport sedan. The Model S beta vehicles were presented ahead of the first "Signature Edition" deliveries expected in nine months.

Title: Can Tesla become a bigger company with Model S electric car? That's Elon Musk's gamble
Summary: Tesla Motors is making a significant gamble with its upcoming Model S electric car, aiming for mass production and profitability despite skepticism from Wall Street and the challenges of the EV market. CEO Elon Musk is confident in the Model S's superiority and is transforming the former NUMMI plant into a state-of-the-art facility for its production. The company is strategically acquiring assets and leveraging expertise to overcome past production issues and cost concerns.

Title: An Electric Car Drives an Industry’s Change (Published 2011)
Summary: Chris Paine's documentary "Revenge of the Electric Car" explores the resurgence of electric vehicles and the industry's shift towards electrification. The film follows various key figures, including Elon Musk, Carlos Ghosn, and Bob Lutz, as they navigate the challenges and triumphs of bringing electric cars to the mass market. It presents an optimistic view of the automotive industry's retooling towards an electric future.

Title: Elon Musk Owes Customers 6,500 Cars, So Why Is He Smiling?
Summary: Despite having 6,500 unfulfilled reservations for the Model S, Elon Musk remains optimistic about Tesla's future. The article highlights recent strategic partnerships with Daimler, Toyota, and Panasonic, along with Musk's perspective on building companies around new technologies. Musk discusses the unique dashboard of the Model S and his role in SolarCity, attributing its success to Peter and Lyndon Rive.

Title: East Palo Alto plane crash pilot's fault, feds say
Summary: A federal investigation concluded that the pilot of a small plane that crashed in East Palo Alto in 2010, killing himself and two Tesla Motors colleagues, was at fault. The pilot, Doug Bourn, failed to heed warnings about heavy fog and did not follow standard instrument departure procedures, leading the twin-engine Cessna 310 to hit a transmission tower. The crash killed Bourn, Brian Finn, and Andrew Ingram, all employees of Tesla Motors, though no one on the ground was injured.

Title: Exclusive Tour Of Tesla’s Showroom With Apple’s Retail Guru [Video]
Summary: George Blankenship, Apple's former retail guru, is applying his expertise to Tesla Motors with a new showroom design in San Jose, California. The showroom aims to offer an Apple-store-like experience for buying luxury electric cars, emphasizing cleanliness, approachability, and excitement, despite Tesla currently only selling one high-priced model. Located on a high-traffic street alongside upscale retailers, the design intends to attract affluent pedestrians and allows for easy updates for future Tesla models.

Title: Top Analyst Upgrades & Downgrades (AMGN, AON, EQT, EXEL, IPI, ERIC, MDVN, NKE, NIHD, NYX, POT, RAX, RRC, SYMC, TSLA, UA, UNH)
Summary: This article lists top analyst upgrades, downgrades, and initiations from Wall Street firms on January 31, 2012. Several prominent companies including Amgen, Nike, and Tesla Motors received upgrades or new "Buy" ratings, while others like Intrepid Potash and Potash Corp. of Saskatchewan were downgraded. The report highlights key changes in analyst sentiment and price targets for a variety of stocks.

Title: Tesla Motors Teases Model X Electric SUV
Summary: Tesla Motors is planning to launch a new all-electric SUV called the Model X, which will be revealed on February 9th in California. Based on a teaser image, the Model X is expected to have a curved hood, sloping roofline, and oval front grille, reminiscent of the forthcoming Model S. The company's CEO, Elon Musk, has stated that this new vehicle will not be "blah" and will likely utilize Tesla's proprietary all-electric powertrain.

Title: SolarCity IPO expected in third quarter: source
Summary: SolarCity is expected to launch its IPO in the third quarter of 2012, hiring Goldman Sachs to underwrite the offering which could value the company at $1.5 billion. The company, founded by brothers Lyndon and Peter Rive and chaired by Elon Musk, has rapidly become a leader in residential solar systems due to its successful solar leasing business model. This IPO could help revitalize a struggling clean technology market, following delays for other energy startups.

Title: TESLA MOTORS, INC. FOURTH QUARTER AND FULL YEAR 2011 SHAREHOLDER LETTER
Summary: Tesla Motors, Inc. released its Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2011 Shareholder Letter, highlighting planned Model S deliveries by July 2012, the premiere of the new Model X, and a new Mercedes-Benz EV powertrain program. The company reported $204 million in revenue for 2011 and anticipates $550-600 million in 2012, while continuing planned investments in R&D and infrastructure, expecting net losses until Model S volume sales in 2013. The letter also details store expansion, growing Model S reservations exceeding 8,000, and deepening partnerships with Daimler and Toyota.

Title: Tesla Model X, And The Curse Of Gull-Wing Doors
Summary: This article discusses the design choice of Tesla's Model X, specifically its "Falcon doors," which closely resemble gull-wing doors. The author argues that while Tesla attempts to differentiate them and highlight their functionality, the association with previous cars featuring gull-wing doors, particularly in a family vehicle context, pushes the Model X into self-parody. The author contends that a minivan (in terms of functionality) will never be a sports car, despite Tesla's attempts to blend styles.

Title: Tesla Battery 'Bricking': The Real Story Behind The Scare
Summary: This article debunks a sensational blog post claiming that Tesla Roadster batteries were "bricking" due to a design flaw. It clarifies that battery "bricking" is a known risk for EVs if not charged, and Tesla explicitly warns owners to keep their cars plugged in, stating damage from not doing so is not covered under warranty. The article also highlights that the original blogger had a business relationship with the aggrieved Tesla owner.

Title: Why Tesla Motors Is Betting On The Model S
Summary: This article details Tesla Motors' strategy, as primarily articulated by CEO Elon Musk, focusing on the launch of the Model S sedan as a pivotal step in the company's long-term plan to produce increasingly affordable electric vehicles. It highlights Musk's vision to move away from fossil fuels and addresses criticisms of Tesla being an "elitist" company by emphasizing future plans for a mass-market electric car. The piece also notes the financial skepticism surrounding Tesla, with Musk confidently dismissing short-sellers.

Title: Toyota Unveils 'RAV4 EV' Jointly Developed with Tesla
Summary: Toyota Motor Corporation announced the unveiling of the Toyota "RAV4 EV," an all-electric compact SUV developed in collaboration with Tesla Motors, Inc. This vehicle, featuring a Tesla electric powertrain, boasts a cruising range of approximately 100 miles and is set to launch in California in late summer 2012. Toyota plans to sell about 2,600 units over three years, continuing its efforts to promote alternative energy sources in vehicles.
Source: トヨタ自動車株式会社 公式企業サイト

Title: Elon Musk: Is he the real-life Tony Stark?
Summary: This article draws parallels between Elon Musk and the fictional character Tony Stark (Iron Man), highlighting Musk's entrepreneurial ventures in electric vehicles, space exploration, and solar energy. It discusses his past successes, such as PayPal, and acknowledges the "Tony Stark" comparisons made by the public and even an Iron Man movie director. However, it also touches upon the personal and financial challenges Musk has faced despite his outward success.

Title: Inside The Tesla Model S
Summary: This article reviews the Tesla Model S upon its debut, highlighting its features, driving experience, and market positioning. It praises the car's performance, range, and technological innovations like the large touchscreen and remote updates, while also addressing concerns about charging infrastructure and its luxury price point. The author concludes that the Model S aims to compete with high-end sedans and demonstrates Tesla's ambition to revolutionize the electric vehicle industry.

Title: First Tesla electric sedans hit the road
Summary: Tesla's first mass-market sedans, the Model S, began rolling out of its Fremont factory on June 22, 2012, marking a crucial moment for the electric car maker. With over 10,000 refundable deposits, the company aims to sell 5,000 units this year, hoping the Model S will drive them toward profitability after previous losses. The base model is priced at $49,900 after federal tax credits and boasts a 160-mile range on a single charge.

Title: Tesla Model S Electric Car Uses Panasonic Lithium Ion Batteries
Summary: The article announces that the new Tesla Model S electric car utilizes lithium-ion batteries supplied by Panasonic. Tesla plans significant production numbers for 2012 and 2013, highlighting the Model S's advanced design, impressive range, and zero emissions. The collaboration between Tesla and Panasonic emphasizes the development of next-generation battery cells specifically optimized for electric vehicle performance and longevity.

Title: Tesla Model S 2013 Review - International
Summary: This article reviews the 2013 Tesla Model S, highlighting its performance, efficiency, and advanced technology as a distinctive electric vehicle. It discusses Tesla's vision to prove EVs can be superior to petrol cars, detailing the Model S's unique features, impressive acceleration, and long range. The review also touches upon initial production challenges, pricing for different variants, and the car's dynamic driving experience despite being electric.

Title: Tesla produces its 1st 50 Model S sedans
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. announced it has produced its first 50 Model S luxury sedans and plans to accelerate production to meet a yearly target of 5,000 deliveries. The company also reported having 12,200 orders for the Model S. The article also touches on a copyright infringement settlement between SAP AG and Oracle Corp., and LinkedIn's stock performance after exceeding sales forecasts.

Title: Tesla's Musk gets option for 5.27 million shares as incentive
Summary: Elon Musk has been granted an option to purchase 5.27 million shares in Tesla as an incentive. He can exercise this option at a price of $31.17 per share. The article was published on August 17, 2012.

Title: California DMV - Plates & HOV Stickers | Page 59
Summary: This discussion from the Tesla Motors Club forum addresses common questions and concerns among California Tesla owners regarding Clean Air Vehicle (CAV) decals and HOV lane access. Topics include applying for CAV decals with temporary license plates, the varying instructions for sticker placement from the DMV, and practical advice for applying the decals to preserve vehicle paint. The conversation highlights the confusion caused by inconsistent information from the California DMV on decal placement over time.

Title: 2012 Tesla Model S [w/video]
Summary: This article provides a first-drive review of the 2012 Tesla Model S, highlighting its revolutionary design as the world's first practical, no-compromise electric vehicle. It details the Signature Performance model's specifications, driving dynamics, and innovative interior features like the 17-inch touchscreen, concluding that the Model S is an impressive and engaging sport sedan that will be considered a pioneering automobile.

Title: Tesla's Model S coming soon, Elon Musk says
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk confirmed that the Model S electric sedan is almost ready for customer deliveries, with the first two units already delivered to a board member and Musk himself for final quality control. The company expects to begin customer deliveries on June 22, 2012, with basic versions selling for $57,400 before incentives. Tesla aims to produce over 5,000 Model S sedans this year and 20,000 in 2013, forecasting a profit after selling approximately 8,000 units despite an $89.9 million loss in Q1.

Title: Tesla’s First Electric-Car 'Supercharger' Stations Now Live
Summary: Tesla has launched its first "Supercharger" fast-charging stations, promising to add up to 150 miles of range to a Model S in 30 minutes. These proprietary stations are twice as powerful as other rapid charging standards and will initially serve 85-kWh Model S owners, with future expansion plans across the U.S. and solar-powered facilities. The initiative aims to dramatically improve long-distance electric car travel for Tesla owners.

Title: Tesla unveils faster electric car-charging station
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. unveiled a new solar-powered Supercharger station designed to quickly charge electric vehicles, making long-distance travel as convenient as stopping for gas. CEO Elon Musk stated these stations address key concerns about electric vehicles' range and convenience. The company plans to expand these charging stations across the US, with the first six already deployed in California.

Title: Tesla chief Elon Musk reaches for stars
Summary: This article profiles Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, highlighting his demanding leadership style and ambitious vision spanning electric cars, space exploration, and solar energy. It details his entrepreneurial journey, from PayPal to his current ventures, and his personal sacrifices in pursuit of groundbreaking innovations. The piece emphasizes his long-term goals of sustainable energy and multi-planetary existence, portraying him as a modern-day industrialist charting a course beyond incremental advancements.

Title: Romney Calls Tesla Electric Vehicles A 'Loser'
Summary: Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney publicly labeled electric car makers Tesla and Fisker as "losers," grouping them with bankrupt companies Ener1 and Solyndra. He criticized the Obama administration for providing $90 billion in loans and grants to green energy companies, implying that many were failing or politically connected. The article questions whether these claims are justified, noting that Fisker was still shipping cars and Tesla [NSDQ:TSLA] was delivering its Model S to thousands of depositors.

Title: Tesla starts delivery out of former Nummi plant
Summary: Tesla Motors began delivering its all-electric Model S luxury sedan from its Fremont factory, formerly the NUMMI plant. The reopening of the plant by Tesla, which now employs 850 people with plans to reach 1,000, has revitalized Fremont's economy after the closure of NUMMI and the bankruptcy of Solyndra. The article highlights the personal impact on former NUMMI employees now working for Tesla and the broader economic recovery of the city.

Title: Tesla & Fisker: The Game of Favorites
Summary: This article contrasts the public reception and financial challenges of electric car manufacturers Tesla and Fisker. Despite similar struggles with government loans and developing affordable vehicles, Tesla, led by Elon Musk, consistently receives more favorable treatment and press compared to Fisker. The piece highlights their common issues with DOE loans, targeting millionaires, and difficulties in a challenging market for electric vehicles.

Title: Tesla co-founder Elon Musk defends retail strategy
Summary: Tesla co-founder Elon Musk defended the company's retail strategy, emphasizing the need to create a business model that promotes electric vehicle knowledge in a convenient and accessible way. This statement highlights Tesla's focus on an innovative approach to EV sales and customer education.

Title: Telsa Model S Is Car of the Year?
Summary: Automobile magazine named the Tesla Model S its Car of the Year, despite the vehicle's high price tag and limited sales. The article expresses skepticism about Tesla's viability, noting the company's potential financial issues and the limited availability of charging stations. While praising the car's performance and technology, the author highlights the practical challenges faced by potential owners.

Title: Model S Photo Gallery | Page 72
Summary: This page from the Tesla Motors Club discussion forum's "Model S Photo Gallery" thread features user posts discussing modifications and appearances of their Tesla Model S vehicles. Discussions include satin wraps for Deep Blue Metallic Plaid models, chrome deletes, PPF wraps, wheel setups, and questions about rare Tesla paint colors like the Signature Red. Users share photos and details of their customizations, providing a visual and technical exchange among Tesla enthusiasts.

Title: Tesla Supercharger Network Expands Into East Coast
Summary: Tesla has expanded its Supercharger network to the East Coast, with new stations in Milford, Connecticut, and Wilmington, Delaware. These stations aim to enable long-distance travel for Tesla Model S owners by providing rapid charging, making a Boston-to-Washington D.C. trip feasible. The company plans to continue expanding the network, with a long-term goal of powering stations with solar energy.

Title: Tesla Electric SUV Is Pretty, But Looks Aren’t Everything
Summary: Tesla Motors unveiled the Model X prototype at the 2013 North American International Auto Show in Detroit, an electric SUV with gull-wing doors and a 17-inch touchscreen. Despite its innovative design, the article questions the viability of electric vehicles for average consumers due to challenges with range, cost, and charging infrastructure. The success of the Model X is seen as dependent on the sales performance of the Model S sedan and Tesla's ability to overcome financial losses and expand its charging network.

Title: At what voltage does the Model S motor work ?
Summary: A Tesla Motors Club discussion thread asks about the operating voltage of the Model S motor, with a user questioning how 320KW at 320 volts would lead to 1000 amps and the implications for wiring. Another user suggests looking at Roadster battery discussions for clues and explains the Model S inverter's integration with the motor.

Title: Tesla Calls NYT Electric Car Review a 'Fake'
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk criticized a New York Times review of the Tesla Model S, calling it "fake" and alleging the reviewer did not fully charge the car and took an unreported detour. The NYT stood by its review, which highlighted concerns about the car's range in cold weather and the scarcity of charging stations, issues that deter many drivers from electric vehicles. Musk argued the article was a "set up and is unreasonable," while the newspaper maintained its account was "completely factual."
Source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

Title: Tesla posts revenue of $306 million, larger-than-expected loss
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. reported a larger-than-expected loss of $90 million in the fourth quarter, or 79 cents a share, though its revenue of $306 million surpassed expectations. Despite the financial performance, the company plans to deliver 20,000 Model S units in the current year and aims for profitability. However, challenges persist with production delays for future models and consumer skepticism regarding electric vehicle range and cost competitiveness.

Title: Tesla Motors focused on improving image after negative New York Times review
Summary: Tesla Motors is strategizing to recover market value and demand after a critical New York Times review of its Model S sedan. CEO Elon Musk estimates the review caused $100 million in lost sales and canceled orders, and the company's shares fell 13 percent since the article's publication. Tesla plans to address the misperception around the Model S's cold weather performance, as its success is crucial for achieving its first adjusted profit since going public.

Title: Case Law: Tesla Motors v BBC, Top Gear up before Top Judges – Rosalind English
Summary: This article discusses the Court of Appeal's decision to refuse Tesla Motors' appeal against the strike-out of a libel claim against the BBC's "Top Gear" programme. The court determined that there was no sufficient prospect of Tesla recovering substantial damages to justify continuing the case to trial, upholding the earlier ruling that the show's review of the Tesla Roadster did not imply malicious falsehood or intentional misleading by Tesla. The judgment emphasizes the principle of proportionality in legal actions, particularly concerning libel claims, and the balance between freedom of speech and protection of reputation.

Title: Tesla repaying Obama admin loan 5 years early
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. is repaying its $465 million loan from the U.S. Energy Department five years ahead of schedule, with repayment planned by December 2017. This development highlights the success of the Obama administration's investment in the innovative car company, a move that was heavily criticized by Mitt Romney and Paul Ryan during the 2012 presidential election. The article questions whether critics will now reconsider their stance given Tesla's early repayment.

Title: Tesla Now Making, Delivering 500 Model S Electric Cars Weekly
Summary: Tesla Motors is reportedly producing and delivering a record average of over 500 Model S electric luxury sedans weekly, a significant increase from its previous target of 400 cars per week. This production rate, confirmed by Tesla's VP George Blankenship and an upstate New York newspaper, suggests the company is now making 2,000 Model S vehicles or more per month, potentially contributing to profitability in the first quarter of the year.

Title: Tesla Motors Pats Itself on the Back
Summary: Tesla Motors announced that its Model S sales exceeded targets, leading to an amendment in its Q1 guidance to full profitability. CEO Elon Musk expressed pride in the team and gratitude to customers, emphasizing that profitability validates the company's place in the electric car revolution. Despite the positive outlook, the article notes skepticism regarding the impressiveness of 4,750 sales.

Title: Tesla Motors Partners With Wells Fargo And US Bank To Finance Model S Electric Cars
Summary: Tesla Motors has partnered with Wells Fargo and US Bank to offer a new financing product for its Model S Electric cars, blending ownership with lease-like advantages. This program, personally guaranteed by Elon Musk, aims to make the Model S more accessible by reducing the net out-of-pocket cost to under $500 per month after accounting for tax credits and electricity savings, and offers a guaranteed resale value after three years.

Title: Tesla Q1 2013: Electric Car Maker Profitable For The Very First Time
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. reported its first-ever quarterly profit in Q1 2013, exceeding Wall Street expectations by delivering nearly 5,000 Model S electric cars. The company also raised its annual delivery target for the Model S to 21,000 vehicles and saw its shares jump significantly after the announcement. This milestone highlights Tesla's success in a challenging market for other "green" car startups.

Title: Tesla Motors Turns A Profit For The First Time
Summary: Tesla Motors reported its first-ever profit in the first quarter of 2013, making $11 million after 10 years without profitability. This turnaround follows better-than-expected sales of its Model S. The company sold 4,900 cars in Q1 2013 and aims to sell 45,000 vehicles annually.

Title: Electric-Car Maker Tesla Posts Its First Quarterly Profit
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. announced its first quarterly profit in the first quarter of 2013, reporting earnings of $11.2 million. This significant milestone was driven by strong deliveries of its Model S electric vehicles. The company recognized revenue from 4,900 Model S units, surpassing its previous forecast of 4,500 cars for the quarter.

Title: Tesla Model S gets Consumer Reports' top score
Summary: The Tesla Model S electric car achieved the highest score ever recorded in Consumer Reports magazine's automotive testing, tying an older Lexus model. Despite its exceptional performance in acceleration, handling, and quietness, it did not receive a "Recommended Buy" rating due to insufficient reliability data from the new company and some identified drawbacks like limited range and long charging times. The magazine praised its sports car-like performance and luxury car quietness, highlighting its energy efficiency.

Title: PHOTOS: Consumer Reports Calls Tesla 'Best Car Ever Tested'
Summary: Consumer Reports has declared the Tesla Model S the "Best Ever" product they have tested, giving it an unprecedented score of 99 out of 100. The electric car outperformed competitors like the Porsche Panamera and Fisker Karma due to its "off the charts" performance. The author expresses a personal desire for the car and encourages readers to view a photo gallery and read more about the test from CNN Money.

Title: Model S boosts Tesla,but mass market electric cars still elusive
Summary: The Tesla Model S has boosted the company's financial performance and reputation, with its first quarterly profit and a near-perfect rating from Consumer Reports. Despite this success, the article highlights that mass-market adoption of electric cars remains elusive, with the Model S catering primarily to affluent consumers due to its high price. Tesla is challenged to deliver more affordable models to reach a broader market and solidify its position as a major car manufacturer.

Title: Tesla Motors Inc (TSLA): Is a ‘Commoner’ Electric Car Possible?
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc (TSLA) has experienced a significant bull run following its first quarterly profit and a near-perfect Consumer Reports score. Despite this success, bears argue that Tesla's focus on the luxury market for electric cars may limit its long-term sustainability. CEO Elon Musk has indicated plans for a more affordable, mid-range electric car retailing for about $30,000 within four years.

Title: 2003-2013:10 Years of Tesla Motors
Summary: This article looks back at Tesla Motors' first ten years (2003-2013), highlighting its journey from the Roadster to the successful Model S. It covers the company's first profitable year, future plans for new models like a 3-series competitor and the Model X, and a next-generation Roadster. Founder Elon Musk also teased an electric supercar within the next four to five years.

Title: Tesla reaches new milestone as stock tops $100 for the first time
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. reached a new milestone as its stock topped $100 a share for the first time on Tuesday, May 28, 2013. This event was seen as significant for Tesla and the electric car industry, with analysts highlighting the company's momentum and future potential. Despite the achievement, analysts also noted the importance of Tesla introducing a more affordable car to sustain its stock value in the long term.

Title: Tesla Is No Success Story
Summary: This article argues that Tesla's financial success is primarily due to political favoritism, government subsidies, and tax credits rather than its ability to create value for customers. It highlights the company's reliance on a $465 million federal loan, state tax incentives, and the sale of special credits in California's zero-emission vehicle program to achieve profitability. The author suggests that without these forms of government assistance, Tesla would not be a success story.

Title: Tesla Motors Inc (TSLA) News: Elon Musk’s Uneasiness, Affordable EV, Buzz without Ads & More
Summary: This article from June 2013 discusses several key aspects of Tesla Motors Inc (TSLA), including Elon Musk's goal to produce an affordable electric vehicle by 2016, the company's valuation following a surprise first-quarter profit, and the expansion of its Supercharger network. It also touches on Musk's reaction to a reporter's question about battery costs.

Title: Drag Race a Tesla Electric Car for $.06 Per 1/4 Mile
Summary: A drag racing website, Drag Times, tested a Tesla Model S with the 85 kWh battery and Performance Package to determine its cost per quarter-mile race. They found that thanks to regenerative braking and California's electricity prices, a quarter-mile drag race costing just 6 cents compared favorably to gas-guzzling sports cars. The test highlighted the Model S's performance, achieving 0-60 mph in 3.9 seconds and covering a quarter-mile in 12.4 seconds at 111.3 mph.

Title: Tesla Motors added to Nasdaq-100 index
Summary: Tesla Motors is being added to the Nasdaq-100 stock index, replacing Oracle Corporation, which is moving to the New York Stock Exchange. This move highlights Tesla's strong performance, with its stock price soaring and its Model S sedan receiving top ratings. The inclusion makes Tesla the only U.S. car company in the index and underscores the increasing competition between Nasdaq and NYSE for listings.

Title: Tesla Being Eyed by Big General Motors (GM)
Summary: General Motors (GM) has formed a task force to study Tesla Motors, viewing the smaller electric car manufacturer as a potential "disrupter." Despite GM's significantly larger sales and profits, the company is wary of repeating past mistakes where it underestimated emerging threats like Japanese automakers. Tesla's Model S has garnered significant attention and its stock has tripled, giving it a market value of $14 billion compared to GM's $50.6 billion at the time of the article.

Title: GM Is Feeling Threatened By Tesla
Summary: General Motors CEO Dan Akerson is reportedly concerned about Tesla's disruptive potential, despite the electric vehicle industry's small market share compared to gas-powered vehicles. GM has formed a team to study the Silicon Valley startup, especially as Tesla's Model S has outsold GM's Chevrolet Volt in early 2013, highlighting Tesla's innovative approach and rapid deployment of new technologies. This shows a shift in the automotive industry where traditional giants are starting to view EV innovators as significant threats.

Title: Tesla Misses On Q2 Earnings, But Margins Grew
Summary: Tesla (TSLA) reported a loss in its second quarter of 2013, missing profit forecasts, but exceeded revenue and profit margin expectations. Despite the net loss, the company delivered a record number of Model S sedans and saw its stock climb in after-hours trading due to strong sales and margin growth. Analysts highlighted the increasing production rate and growing margins as more compelling than the overall revenue and profit numbers.

Title: Tesla Motors earns $26 million in the 2nd quarter — thanks to the government
Summary: Tesla Motors reported a surprise second-quarter profit of $26 million, largely attributed to government support initiatives such as zero-emission-vehicle (ZEV) credits and a Department of Energy loan. The article highlights how government subsidies were crucial in Tesla's path to profitability and development, despite CEO Elon Musk's public criticisms of such support. It details Tesla's financial milestones and its reliance on these programs to bring its ambitious electric vehicles to market.

Title: Musk awarded $4.3 million in Tesla shares for advance Model X work
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk received $4.3 million in stock compensation during the second quarter of 2013. This award was for his work on the Model X, specifically completing vehicle and engineering prototypes, and the first production vehicle of the Model X.

Title: Tesla co-founder gets $4.3m for SUV work-in-progress
Summary: Elon Musk, Tesla's CEO and co-founder, received $4.3 million in stock-based compensation for his work on the Model X SUV, which the company expects to complete later. This compensation was part of the $19.3 million in stock-based pay reported by Tesla for the second quarter and contributed to an adjusted profit figure that defied analyst expectations for a loss. The payment structure and the stock's significant appreciation highlight Tesla's unique approach to compensation and its growing status as a technology company rather than a traditional automaker.

Title: China - The World's Top Car Market Where Tesla Can't Use Its Trademark
Summary: Tesla Motors is facing a significant trademark dispute in China with entrepreneur Zhan Baosheng, who registered the "Tesla" name and domain names. This conflict is hindering Tesla's expansion into the critical Chinese auto market, despite the company's efforts to negotiate and acquire trademark rights for certain vehicle types. The situation highlights the challenges foreign companies face with trademark squatting in China, similar to Apple's past experience with the "iPad" name.

Title: Here Are Other Companies Tesla’s ‘Trademark Troll’ Tried To Claim
Summary: The article details how "trademark troll" Zhan Baosheng, who attempted to claim the "Tesla" trademark in China, has a history of trying to register trademarks for other companies. This pattern of behavior could potentially help Tesla Motors in its legal battle to reclaim its own trademark rights in China, as it might demonstrate bad faith on Zhan's part. The dispute highlights China's "first to file" trademark principle and the challenges it poses for mid-tier companies expanding into new markets.

Title: Tesla Model S Scores Better Than Perfect On Safety Tests
Summary: The Tesla Model S has achieved top safety ratings from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), scoring five stars across all crash tests and even a "better than perfect" overall Vehicle Safety Score of 5.4 stars. The electric car outperformed other categories, including minivans and SUVs, attributed partly to its design without a large gasoline engine block, which allows for a longer crumple zone. Despite an enthusiastic statement from Tesla about its safety scores, the NHTSA clarified it does not rate vehicles beyond 5 stars or rank vehicles within starred categories.

Title: A Gasoline-Powered Tesla
Summary: The article argues that for Tesla Motors Inc. to achieve significant sales, it needs to introduce a hybrid or gasoline-powered car due to the limited market for electric vehicles. It highlights hurdles such as price, range anxiety, and charging times, suggesting that current electric car demand is insufficient for Tesla's long-term success without broadening its appeal. The author proposes that Tesla consider integrating gasoline engines to expand its market beyond a niche given the premium price of its vehicles.

Title: Agency Pushes Back on Tesla 5.4 Star Safety Rating Claim
Summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is challenging Tesla Motors' claim that its Model S car achieved a crash test rating greater than five stars. While acknowledging the car's stellar performance with a five-star rating in all categories, NHTSA clarified that it does not rate vehicles beyond five stars. Tesla reportedly combined various safety measurements to arrive at its 5.4-star figure, a methodology criticized as misleading by an auto safety expert.

Title: Tesla's market value tops $20 billion on EV optimism
Summary: Tesla's market value has exceeded $20 billion, driven by optimism surrounding electric vehicles. The company's shares reached a new record high, highlighting investor confidence in its future in the EV market.

Title: Chipotle Mexican Grill names Kimbal Musk to board
Summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc. has appointed entrepreneur and restaurateur Kimbal Musk, brother of Elon Musk, to its board of directors, effective September 1. As an outside director, Musk will receive an annual compensation package including cash and restricted stock units, along with additional fees for attending board and committee meetings. Musk, based in Boulder, also serves on the board of Tesla and co-founded The Kitchen restaurants.

Title: 'Teslanaires' put all their eggs in one electric car
Summary: The article highlights individual investors, dubbed "Teslanaires," who have made significant profits from investing heavily in Tesla Motors Inc. stock, often through risky options trading. Despite advice to diversify, these investors show strong confidence in Tesla, citing its successes and CEO Elon Musk's vision. Financial experts warn against putting disproportionate wealth into a single volatile stock due to high risks involved.

Title: Green Mountain Coffee Roasters Inc. (GMCR), Tesla Motors Inc (TSLA), Bazaarvoice Inc (BV): Three Predictions for the New Week
Summary: This article presents three predictions for the upcoming week from The Motley Fool. The predictions include Green Mountain Coffee Roasters Inc. (NASDAQ:GMCR) closing higher, the Nasdaq Composite outperforming the Dow Jones Industrial Average (INDEXDJX:^DJI), and Lululemon Athletica inc. (NASDAQ: LULU) beating Wall Street's earnings estimates. The author provides rationale and historical data to support these predictions.

Title: How the Tesla Model S Works
Summary: This article details the workings and impact of the Tesla Model S, highlighting its innovative all-electric design, high safety ratings, and its role in challenging traditional automotive manufacturing and sales models. It covers the car's performance specifications, charging infrastructure, and the vision of co-founder Elon Musk in pushing electric vehicle technology forward. The piece also touches on criticisms and the car's influence on the perception of EVs.

Title: Silverthorne the first Colorado town tapped for Tesla Motors supercharging station
Summary: Silverthorne, Colorado, has been chosen as the location for Tesla Motors' first supercharging station in the state. This move is part of Tesla's effort to enable cross-country road trips for its customers by building supercharging stations along major highways and in metropolitan areas across the U.S. and Canada. The station, located at the Outlets at Silverthorne, will provide free and fast charging for Tesla vehicles, benefiting both Tesla owners and local economic development.

Title: In brief: Oil giant is cross about use of XX
Summary: Exxon Mobil Corp. has sued FX Networks and its affiliates to block their use of a logo featuring interlocking XXs, claiming it infringes on its own XX logo. Separately, Wall Street is urging Congress to end the government shutdown, Oracle is defending CEO Larry Ellison's pay packages against a shareholder rebellion, and Tesla Motors shares dropped after a video showed one of its vehicles on fire. Other business news includes an advertising agency renaming, Monsanto's acquisition of a farming software firm, and financial results from Phillips 66 and Walgreen Co.

Title: Musk defends Tesla Model S safety after review of fire
Summary: Elon Musk is defending the safety of the Tesla Model S after a fire incident. The fire was caused by an impact to the front battery module, according to Tesla. This article also includes other automotive news regarding U.S. sales figures for October and dealer disputes.

Title: Tesla in talks with Samsung SDI for battery supply deal
Summary: Tesla Motors is reportedly in advanced talks with South Korean battery producer Samsung SDI to become an additional battery supplier, aiming to diversify its supply chain ahead of new model introductions like the Model X. While both companies confirmed ongoing discussions, sources indicate complexities remain, such as Samsung SDI's desire for Tesla to purchase other components from Samsung Group. This potential deal comes as Tesla seeks to reduce its reliance on a single battery supplier, Panasonic, and as Samsung Group looks to expand its electric battery business.

Title: Mainland China has its first Tesla owner
Summary: The first Tesla owner in Mainland China has been identified as a 24-year-old from Dongyang city. He purchased the Model S through Hong Kong, as Tesla Motors Inc. had not yet opened a store in mainland China. Due to the lack of local service, the owner stated he bought the car mainly for fun and does not expect to drive it long distances.

Title: Tesla hires Apple Product Design and Development VP and Segway veteran Doug Field
Summary: Tesla has hired Doug Field, former VP of Product Design and Development at Apple Inc. and veteran of Segway, as its Vice President of Vehicle Programs. Field will be responsible for leading the development of new vehicles, bringing his extensive experience in consumer electronics and automotive engineering to Tesla. This move highlights Tesla's commitment to attracting top talent for innovative vehicle design and production.

Title: BASF Recieves Tesla Motors Supplier Award
Summary: BASF was honored with a Supplier Award by Tesla Motors for its excellence in delivery performance. The company was recognized for exceeding Tesla's expectations in new color introductions, vehicle painting efficiencies, product quality, and customer service. This award highlights the collaborative relationship between BASF and Tesla.

Title: How Tesla Protects The Romance Of Driving While Disrupting The Industry
Summary: This article details how Tesla's chief designer, Franz von Holzhausen, approaches car design to create emotional engagement while disrupting the automobile industry. It highlights the inspiration behind the Model S and the upcoming Model X, focusing on innovative features, user experience, and the company's long-term vision to move away from fossil fuels.

Title: 3 Workers Injured In Accident At Fremont Tesla Factory, CEO Speaks Out
Summary: Three workers were hospitalized with burns after an industrial accident involving a low-pressure aluminum casting press at the Tesla Motors factory in Fremont. CEO Elon Musk visited the injured employees, identifying them as Jorge, Kevin, and Jesus, and stated that the company would ensure they receive the best possible care, particularly for Jesus who suffered severe hand burns. The incident, where molten aluminum spilled, comes amidst recent safety questions surrounding Tesla's Model S vehicles.

Title: Tesla Model S probed by U.S. after three fires in five weeks
Summary: The U.S. government is investigating the Tesla Model S after three battery fires occurred in five weeks. This heightened scrutiny comes amidst concerns about the lithium-ion batteries used in the vehicles.

Title: Tesla GAAP Gap: Are Tesla’s Accounting Practices A Risk?
Summary: Tesla's accounting practices are under scrutiny due to a widening gap between its GAAP and non-GAAP financial reporting, particularly concerning how it books future revenue from the sale of post-lease Model S sedans. This has led to potential federal securities law claims and concerns among investors and critics about the company's valuation of used vehicles and its stock performance following recent events.

Title: Elon Musk and Tesla Fight Back After Feds Probe Model S
Summary: Elon Musk and Tesla are defending the Model S after the NHTSA began an investigation into two vehicle fires. Musk argues that gasoline cars have a significantly higher risk of fire, stating that Model S fires occurred only after high-speed collisions without serious injuries. Analysts weigh in on the potential outcomes of the investigation, ranging from no inherent flaw to a forced recall.

Title: How Tesla found itself on the defense
Summary: This article examines how electric-car maker Tesla, once a media darling due to its innovative CEO Elon Musk and highly-rated Model S, found itself defending against negative press. This shift was largely due to a series of battery fires in its Model S vehicles and a subsequent disappointing earnings report, leading to a significant stock dip and questions about safety. Tesla's response included Musk's detailed explanations, software updates, and an amended warranty, alongside an ongoing discussion with the NHTSA.

Title: Elon Musk Puts a Satellite into Orbit
Summary: Tech entrepreneur Elon Musk and his private space flight company SpaceX successfully launched their first major commercial satellite into high orbit on Tuesday aboard SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket. This marks a significant milestone as previous launches were test runs or for NASA. SpaceX has over 50 upcoming launches planned, with more than half designated for commercial customers.

Title: Whatever Happened to Tesla?
Summary: This article from December 2013 discusses Tesla's fluctuating fortunes. Despite strong sales growth and positive reviews, recent car fires and a looming U.S. investigation caused its stock to drop and public sentiment to sour, making it difficult for the company to regain positive media attention.

Title: The Shops at Mission Viejo Revs Up for Two New Additions This Winter
Summary: The Shops at Mission Viejo announced the upcoming opening of two new tenants, a Tesla Motors store and Magellan’s Travel Supplies, just in time for the winter travel season. Tesla Motors is expected to open mid-December, offering test drives and a design studio for their Model S sedan, while Magellan's Travel Supplies will open early next year, providing a wide range of travel gear. These additions aim to diversify the mall's offerings and enhance the shopping experience for the community.

Title: Tesla To Add Production Capacity For 35,000 More Electric Cars
Summary: Tesla Motors is set to expand its annual production capacity by 35,000 electric vehicles, aided by $34.7 million in tax breaks from California. This expansion, costing $415 million for new manufacturing equipment, will support not only the Model S but also the upcoming Model X and a future lower-priced sedan, along with powertrains for partners Daimler and Toyota. The move is expected to create 112 new jobs and provide a net benefit of $24.4 million to the state.

Title: Tesla's global sales top 22,000 in 2013, stock rises 16%
Summary: Tesla announced its global sales topped 22,000 vehicles in 2013, which contributed to a 16% rise in its stock price. Despite not introducing new vehicles at the 2014 Detroit auto show, the company confirmed it is on track to begin production of the Model X SUV by year-end.

Title: How Many Tesla Model S Electric Cars Have Been Built So Far?
Summary: This article discusses the estimated production numbers for the Tesla Model S electric car as of January 2014. Despite Tesla Motors not releasing exact production figures, the author uses various pieces of information, including Tesla's Q4 2013 delivery numbers, comments from executives, and car serial numbers, to estimate that Tesla had built around 30,000 Model S vehicles. The article highlights Tesla's rapid production compared to other plug-in vehicle startups.

Title: Whiplash: Trading SPY, GOOG, AAPL, TSLA, And ISRG
Summary: The article discusses the "whiplash" experienced in the stock market during the week, particularly focusing on the S&P 500 and individual stocks like GOOG, AAPL, TSLA, and ISRG. The author describes switching between bullish and bearish biases, noting significant price movements and technical indicators for these companies. The piece highlights surprising rallies and reversals, suggesting a period of high volatility and potential for significant moves in the market.

Title: Tesla Motors Inc, the youngest U.S. automaker, ranks in top 5 car brands in Consumer Reports survey
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. has ranked in the top five brands in a Consumer Reports survey, an improvement from its 11th position last year. The electric car company, known for its innovation and performance, saw its shares triple since May due to positive reviews and financial reports. This survey highlights growing consumer perception of quality and technology among car brands.

Title: Why A Used Tesla Model S Can Cost More Than A New One (TSLA)
Summary: A study by iSeeCars found that used Tesla Model S vehicles can cost more than new ones, sometimes up to 20 percent over the average new MSRP. This unusual trend is attributed to federal tax incentives for new buyers and Tesla's production constraints, which create a supply/demand imbalance in the aftermarket. The analysis also revealed very low average mileage on used Model S cars, suggesting some early adopters are profitably reselling nearly new vehicles.

Title: Tesla Motors closes at record after Apple merger rumor surfaces
Summary: Shares of Tesla Motors reached a new closing high of $203.70, a 3% gain, fueled by rumors of a potential acquisition by Apple and anticipation of strong fourth-quarter results. The rumors stemmed from a reported meeting in early 2013 between Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Apple's mergers-and-acquisitions head, Adrian Perica. However, analysts expressed skepticism about a full merger due to Apple's acquisition history and the differing profit margins between the auto and consumer electronics industries.

Title: Tesla Motors Reports $74 Million Net Loss in 2013
Summary: Tesla Motors reported a GAAP net loss of $74 million for the full year 2013, despite moving 6,892 Model S vehicles in Q4 2013. The company also announced plans to deliver 35,000 Model S vehicles in 2014, launch the Model X crossover by spring 2015, and develop a "Gigafactory" for battery production.

Title: Elon Musk Made $1.1 Billion Yesterday
Summary: Elon Musk's net worth increased by $1.1 billion in one day as Tesla Motors shares rose by nearly 14 percent. This surge brought his total net worth to $11.7 billion, representing a 47.8 percent increase since the beginning of the year. The article highlights the rapid growth in Musk's net worth, particularly since late 2013.

Title: The Real Reason Elon Musk Became an Entrepreneur
Summary: Elon Musk became an entrepreneur not for financial gain but to positively impact the future, as he explained at the 36th annual ENCORE Award reception honoring Tesla Motors. He focused on sustainable energy, the Internet, and making life multi-planetary, while steering clear of AI and genetics due to potential negative outcomes. His first venture, Zip2 Corporation, was driven by a desire to be part of the Internet rather than by wealth accumulation, showcasing his commitment to impactful innovation over monetary rewards.

Title: Snap-on Introduces New Parking Brake Tool For Toyota Vehicles
Summary: Snap-on has introduced a new Parking Brake Tool (BT20) designed to save service technicians at least 20 minutes when working on rear parking brake springs on many Toyota vehicles. This specialized tool addresses the difficulty of accessing and manipulating the spring cup, aiming to increase productivity and profitability for automotive service and repair businesses. It is compatible with model year 2000 and newer Tacoma, Tundra, FJ Cruiser, 4Runner, Land Cruiser, and Camry vehicles.

Title: Kandi: China’s Non-Tesla Electric Car Maker
Summary: Kandi Technologies Group Inc. and Tesla Motors Inc. have both seen significant stock price increases, though Kandi produces smaller, more affordable electric cars primarily for the Chinese market. Kandi's strategy involves government-subsidized hourly rentals and aims to provide vehicles at a fraction of Tesla's price. The Chinese market is large enough to support both companies' business models, and Kandi recently reported strong revenue and net income growth.

Title: Labor unions saved Ford in our 'darkest' hour: Bill Ford
Summary: Bill Ford, executive chairman of Ford Motor Company, credited labor unions with saving the company from bankruptcy during its "darkest hour," highlighting their role in helping Ford avoid a federal bailout. He contrasted Ford's experience with that of competitors like General Motors, which went bankrupt, and discussed Ford's stance on unionization in the South and Tesla's direct sales model.

Title: Tesla to install high-strength battery shields to reduce fire risk
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. announced plans to reinforce the undercarriage of approximately 16,000 cars with high-strength shields to mitigate fire risk stemming from crash damage. This voluntary action, which mirrors a recall in scope, comes after the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) closed its probe into two Tesla Model S fires, finding no safety defect trend warranting a recall. Tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, detailed a triple underbody shield design that will be installed free of charge to existing owners to enhance safety and peace of mind.

Title: How Tesla Is Driving The New Purpose Economy
Summary: This article examines how Tesla is driving the new purpose economy by applying the diffusion of innovations theory. Tesla's strategy of targeting innovators and early adopters with luxury electric cars is explained as a model for social entrepreneurs to build markets for world-changing products. The author, Aaron Hurst, uses Tesla's approach to illustrate how to create meaningful impact and human-centered markets.

Title: Tesla hopes to sell cars in Arizona
Summary: Tesla is pushing to change Arizona state law to allow direct sales of its electric cars, bypassing traditional dealerships. This effort is intertwined with the company's search for a location for a massive battery factory, with Arizona being one of the four states considered. The move faces opposition from car dealers and other automakers, who argue Tesla's business model doesn't conform to established industry rules.

Title: Wall Street slips as biotech, momentum stocks lead decline
Summary: U.S. stocks, particularly in the biotech and momentum sectors, experienced a decline on Thursday, led by drops in companies like Facebook, Tesla, and Netflix. Investors were taking profits ahead of the nonfarm payrolls report and showed anxiety over the economic outlook. Despite some value-oriented stocks rising, the Dow and S&P 500 slipped from intraday record highs.

Title: Tesla Model S: The hot car everyone is talking about
Summary: This article showcases the Tesla Model S, highlighting its popularity and acclaim as a top car. It includes various images of the vehicle and mentions Tesla's plans for a battery factory. The piece also briefly touches on regulatory challenges Tesla faces regarding direct sales in some states.

Title: Tesla Gigafactory Seeks North American Raw Materials To Cut Pollution
Summary: Tesla Motors has announced that its new $5 billion battery gigafactory will source all raw battery materials from North America to reduce pollution and increase supply chain transparency. This strategic move aims to minimize environmental impact and significantly cut battery costs, despite potential challenges in sourcing materials like graphite locally. The company seeks to reduce the vast pollution footprint typically associated with the global supply chain of lithium-ion battery components.

Title: Tesla's Elon Musk paid $70,000 in 2013
Summary: In 2013, Tesla Motors CEO Elon Musk was paid just under $70,000, consisting of a base salary of $33,280 and $36,709 in company bonuses. Although he only accepts $1 of his salary, he holds a compensation package from 2012 awarding him options to buy nearly 5.3 million shares of Tesla stock. The full value of these options, exceeding $1 billion, is contingent on the company meeting specific performance goals, including share value and production milestones for future vehicles like the Model X and Generation Three.

Title: Stock Market Crash Indicators: Three More Warning Signs
Summary: This article discusses three stock market crash indicators that suggest the current bull market may be losing steam and susceptible to a significant correction. These indicators include the S&P 500 being excessively above its 150-day moving average, weakness in the housing sector, and underperformance of the consumer discretionary sector. Analysts provide recommendations for investors to prepare for a potential correction, such as adjusting trailing stops, adding inverse funds like Rydex Series Trust Inverse S&P 500 Strategy Fund Class Investor (MUTF: RYURX) or ProShares Short S&P 500 (NYSE ARCA: SH), and preparing a buy list for good stocks that become cheap (e.g. Tesla Motors Inc. (Nasdaq: TSLA) and Amazon.com Inc. (Nasdaq: AMZN)).

Title: Tesla Suppliers List: These 26 Companies Help Make a Model S Sedan
Summary: This article identifies 26 known suppliers that contribute parts to Tesla Motors Inc.'s Model S sedan. Despite Tesla keeping its full list of suppliers classified, the piece highlights several companies, some publicly traded, that play a role in the production of the luxury electric vehicle. The article also notes Tesla's significant stock performance and mentions a secretive project called "BlueStar."

Title: The Logic of Tesla's Gigafactory: 'The Economics Are a No-Brainer'
Summary: Elon Musk discussed Tesla's planned "gigafactory" for electric car batteries, emphasizing its economic necessity for the company's growth. He stated that building a $5 billion factory in the U.S. is crucial for Tesla to cut costs and boost sales volume. However, he did not disclose the factory's location or funding sources.

Title: Tesla CEO Says Sacramento A 'Long-Shot' For Gigafactory Expansion
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. is considering Sacramento as a potential site for its massive $5 billion Gigafactory battery plant, which could create 6,500 jobs. However, CEO Elon Musk views California as an "improbable" location due to complex and lengthy approval processes for greenfield sites. Nevada, Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas are considered more likely candidates, with Musk aiming to break ground next month.

Title: China's Xinzhi buys stake in Tesla's Taiwanese motor supplier
Summary: China's Xinzhi has acquired a stake in a Taiwanese motor supplier that works with Tesla. This acquisition highlights the growing interest and investment from Chinese companies in the electric vehicle supply chain.

Title: Tesla’s Musk: ‘It is quite difficult to be CEO at two companies’
Summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla Motors and SpaceX, stated that being a CEO of two companies is difficult and committed to staying at Tesla for at least another four to five years. He plans to oversee the volume production of the third-generation car, set for late 2016. Additionally, Musk noted that Tesla would decide on the location for its battery “gigafactory” by the end of the year, a project estimated to cost up to $5 billion and employ 6,500 people.

Title: Why Tesla's Elon Musk Must Sell 6 Million Electric Cars To Make History
Summary: This article argues that for Tesla CEO Elon Musk to make history as the most successful startup automaker in 90 years, his company must produce and sell roughly 6 million electric cars. This benchmark is set by comparing Tesla's current production to the historical output of industrialist Henry J. Kaiser, whose company, Kaiser-Frazer, sold 750,000 cars in a post-war market significantly smaller than today's. The piece highlights the immense challenges of breaking into the automotive industry and emphasizes the scale of achievement needed to rival past successes when accounting for market growth.

Title: BMW launches i8 plug-in hybrid as Tesla shakes up green supercar segment
Summary: BMW has launched its i8 plug-in hybrid, featuring laser headlights, entering a green supercar market segment increasingly influenced by Tesla. The article also mentions current automotive news regarding U.S. sales figures for various brands in October and dealer disputes for Nissan and Stellantis.

Title: Tesla Motors offers all its patents for good faith use
Summary: Tesla Motors CEO Elon Musk has announced that the company will make all of its patented technology available for use by competitors in a bid to boost the electric vehicle industry. Musk stated that Tesla would not sue other automakers for using its patents, including technologies like the Supercharger network and battery pack construction, and expects similar reciprocal behavior. The move aims to accelerate the adoption of electric cars, which currently make up less than 1 percent of total vehicle production.

Title: Elon Musk opens up Tesla patents; it ‘isn’t entirely altruistic’
Summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla Motors is opening up its patents to all challengers, aiming to accelerate the adoption of electric cars. While seemingly altruistic, analysts suggest the move helps Tesla by expanding the electric vehicle market, allowing it to potentially sell batteries and maintain a competitive lead. The decision is also influenced by Musk's belief that the patent system stifles innovation and his desire to address global warming.

Title: Tesla Will Allow Others To Use Its Patents
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. is offering its proprietary technology, including patents related to its Model S electric car, to other companies. CEO Elon Musk stated this move is aimed at spurring wider development of electric vehicles. He also mentioned discussions with BMW AG about sharing technology for rapidly recharging batteries.

Title: Free For All: Tesla Motors Makes Electric Car Patents Open Source
Summary: Tesla Motors has announced that it is making all of its electric car technology patents open source, allowing anyone to use them. CEO Elon Musk stated this decision was made to accelerate the advent of sustainable transport and foster growth in the electric vehicle industry. Musk believes that technology leadership is defined by attracting talented engineers rather than by patents, and hopes this move will help combat the dominance of gasoline-powered cars.

Title: Elon Musk offers Tesla’s patents to everyone
Summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla (TSLA) will not initiate patent lawsuits against anyone who uses their technology in good faith, in an effort to advance electric car development. This decision marks a significant reversal of his previous strategy to patent technology, which he now believes stifles progress in the electric vehicle field. Musk hopes this open-source approach will accelerate innovation and help combat climate change.

Title: Elon Musk opens up Tesla patents to everyone
Summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla Motors is opening up its patents to all companies, aiming to accelerate the adoption of electric cars. This unconventional move is intended to help the U.S. auto industry and counter the dominance of gasoline-powered vehicles, rather than to gain a competitive advantage over other electric car manufacturers. While analysts see it as a smart move that demonstrates confidence, some warn of potential risks in sharing core technology.

Title: Elon Musk: 'All Our Patent Are Belong To You'
Summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla Motors Inc., announced a groundbreaking decision to give away the company's patents. This move is expected to permanently alter the automotive industry landscape.

Title: Tesla Motors to share patents to spur electric car development
Summary: Tesla Motors announced it will allow others to use its intellectual property, including all current and future patents, to accelerate the development of electric cars across the industry. CEO Elon Musk stated the company would not pursue legal action against those who use their technology in good faith, believing an open-source approach benefits the entire electric vehicle market without harming Tesla's bottom line. The move aims to attract skilled talent and promote sustainable transport, though Tesla will continue to file patents to prevent others from monopolizing information.

Title: Tesla hands over the keys to its electric car technology
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced a groundbreaking decision to open-source the company's entire patent portfolio to encourage the broader adoption of electric vehicles. This move aims to foster collaboration within the automotive industry and accelerate the development of compelling electric cars, acknowledging Tesla cannot achieve widespread market transformation alone. While giving up a long-term advantage, Tesla hopes this strategy will solidify its leadership and expand the overall electric car market.

Title: Elon Musk opens up all of Tesla Motors’ patents
Summary: Elon Musk has announced that Tesla Motors is making all of its electric vehicle and charger technology patents available to the public domain. The company's CEO stated that Tesla will not pursue legal action against anyone using their patented technology in "good faith," hoping this open-source approach will accelerate EV production and adoption in the U.S. Musk believes that the primary competition is gasoline-powered cars, not other electric vehicles, aligning with Tesla's mission to advance sustainable transport.

Title: 8 unforgettable quotes from Tesla/SolarCity founder Elon Musk
Summary: This article compiles eight memorable quotes from Elon Musk, founder of Tesla and SolarCity, highlighting his vision for a sustainable energy future. The quotes cover his beliefs on the necessity of renewable energy, the mission of Tesla, the need for competition in electric vehicles, the role of stationary battery packs for solar, and the significance of solar power as a primary energy source. Musk's perspective on opening up Tesla's patents to accelerate EV adoption is also included.

Title: Nikola Tesla museum gets $1 million boost from Elon Musk
Summary: Elon Musk has pledged an additional $1 million and a Tesla charging station to the Nikola Tesla museum project, celebrating the inventor's 158th birthday. This comes after an initial $2,500 donation and a successful online campaign that raised $1.3 million. The effort to convert Tesla's Wardenclyffe lab into a museum is spearheaded by Matthew Inman of The Oatmeal.

Title: Tesla names small car to be launched in 2017 'Model 3'
Summary: Tesla Motors announced its new small car, intended for a broader consumer segment, will be named Model 3 and launch in 2017. Priced at $35,000, it aims to compete with BMW's 3 Series sedans, offering a driving range of about 200 miles. This vehicle represents the third generation of Tesla cars, following the Model S and the upcoming Model X.

Title: Why Tesla Motors can't sell cars in most of the United States
Summary: Tesla Motors faces significant hurdles in selling its electric cars directly to consumers in the United States due to state laws protecting traditional car dealerships. These laws, established to safeguard car dealers from manufacturers, prevent Tesla from adopting its preferred direct-to-consumer sales model, similar to Apple stores. The conflict highlights an ongoing battle between Tesla's innovative sales approach and the established automotive dealership system, primarily driven by financial interests and political lobbying from auto dealer associations.

Title: Fremont approves new 'innovation district' plan around BART station, Tesla Motors
Summary: Fremont City Council has approved a new "innovation district" plan around the Warm Springs BART station and the Tesla Motors Inc. factory. This plan outlines land-use and design guidelines for the 879-acre zone. The goal is to transform the area into a mixed-use district with housing, offices, and industrial facilities.

Title: 10 Questions: Mike Nefkens, EVP of Enterprise Services, Hewlett-Packard
Summary: Mike Nefkens, EVP of Enterprise Services at Hewlett-Packard, discusses his career, influences, and the challenges facing the IT services sector. He shares his admiration for innovators like Elon Musk and Mark Benioff, and his goal to reinvent HP Enterprise Services. Nefkens also emphasizes the importance of international experience and work-life balance for career success.

Title: Will Tesla 'Gigafactory' answer come today for Nevada?
Summary: Nevada is eagerly anticipating an announcement from Tesla Motors, Inc. today regarding the location of its much-anticipated lithium-ion battery "gigafactory." Tesla executives are scheduled to hold a conference call with Wall Street analysts after reporting second-quarter earnings, where further details about the factory are expected, though it remains uncertain if CEO Elon Musk will reveal the chosen state. The factory, a $5 billion investment, is projected to create 6,500 jobs and significantly impact the chosen region.

Title: Panasonic and Tesla Sign Agreement for the Gigafactory
Summary: Panasonic Corporation and Tesla Motors, Inc. have signed an agreement for the construction of a large-scale battery manufacturing plant in the United States, known as the Gigafactory. Panasonic will manufacture and supply cylindrical lithium-ion cells and invest in associated equipment, while Tesla will manage the facility and assemble battery modules and packs. This collaboration aims to significantly reduce the cost of long-range battery packs and enable mass-market electric vehicles by achieving economies of scale and optimizing manufacturing processes.

Title: Tesla Breaks Ground on 'Potential' Nevada Site for Battery Factory
Summary: Tesla has broken ground on a potential Gigafactory site in Nevada, partnering with Panasonic for battery production. However, Nevada is only one of several states, including Arizona, California, New Mexico, and Texas, vying for the $5 billion facility. The final location will be chosen based on incentives and operational readiness to support the upcoming Model 3.

Title: Tesla Motors Inc (TSLA) Stock Price: Time To Buy Shares? [VIDEO]
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. (TSLA) shares rose following strong Q2 2014 earnings, exceeding analyst expectations, and the announcement of a $5 billion "Gigafactory" deal with Panasonic. The company detailed plans for increased production of Model S vehicles, development of the Model X SUV, and expansion into international markets like Europe and China, alongside an increased capital expenditure forecast. Analysts suggest the stock is poised for a breakout given its recent consolidation and volatility.

Title: Tesla bringing plant to Central Valley, but it’s not the big one
Summary: Tesla Motors Inc. is opening a 430,000-square-foot facility in Lathrop, San Joaquin Valley, which was formerly a DaimlerChrysler distribution center. This new plant is likely for parts manufacturing and will employ 125 workers to start, but it is not the 6,500-job battery Gigafactory Tesla is considering for other states. California is still attempting to convince Tesla to build the larger factory in the state despite being absent from the list of finalists, while Tesla also expanded operations in China.

Title: Customized Tesla Model S: Mod-Shop Will Begin Making Tesla Motors Cars Convertible In California, Barcelona, Dubai
Summary: Newport Convertible Engineering, a luxury car mod-shop, announced plans to convert Tesla Model S sedans into convertibles and coupes. These customized vehicles will be sold worldwide from locations in Huntington Beach, Barcelona, and Dubai. The conversions will cost Model S owners significantly extra, with soft tops priced above a Nissan Leaf and hard tops around the cost of a BMW i3.

Title: How Tesla Can Drop The Price Of Its Cars
Summary: This article discusses how Tesla Motors plans to reduce the price of its upcoming Model 3 electric car to make it more affordable for the mass market. Key strategies include lowering battery costs through the "gigafactory" and potentially reducing some luxury features, while still aiming for a practical range. The challenge lies in balancing price reduction with maintaining Tesla's high-tech appeal and performance expectations.

Title: Tesla Motors Looks To Install Massive Sign Near Fremont Plant
Summary: Tesla Motors is seeking to install a massive 40-foot tall, 200-foot wide illuminated sign near its Fremont factory, which would feature a rendering of a Tesla car. Despite Fremont's strict sign regulations, Mayor Bill Harrison supports granting an exception, citing Tesla's economic contributions to the city. The planning commission is slated to vote on the proposal.
