The appointment raises concerns among some analysts about Denholm's independence, given her long tenure on the board with Musk. Denholm will leave her current role as CFO of Telstra Corp. to assume the full-time chairman position at Tesla.

Title: A user’s guide to Tesla’s worker safety problems
Summary: This article details Tesla's ongoing worker safety issues and alleged efforts to conceal injuries. It provides a timeline of key events, reports, and investigations, highlighting concerns about the company's injury reporting practices, medical care for workers, and regulatory responses.
Source: Reveal from The Center for Investigative Reporting

Title: California officials grill Tesla on safety problems exposed in Reveal investigation
Summary: California officials questioned Tesla Inc. representatives about the company's treatment of injured workers following a Reveal investigation and have expressed serious concerns over safety practices. The state board is considering further action and referrals to Cal/OSHA, while Tesla disputes the reporting, claiming its safety protocols are sound and injury rates are declining.
Source: Reveal from The Center for Investigative Reporting

Title: RJ Scaringe
Summary: RJ Scaringe, CEO of Rivian Automotive, discusses his third attempt at car manufacturing, focusing on battery-electric vehicles set to launch in 2020. He details the challenges of building a company, brand, tech platform, and organization simultaneously, and outlines Rivian's strategy regarding profitability, capital, automation, and direct sales, contrasting it with Tesla's approach.

Title: How Morgan Stanley's 'mad scientist' became the top Wall Street analyst on the space industry
Summary: Adam Jonas, Morgan Stanley's auto analyst, has become the firm's leading expert on the space industry, a shift driven by his interest in Elon Musk's ventures. Initially met with skepticism, Jonas and his team have built a comprehensive research effort on space, anticipating significant growth, akin to the self-driving car market. He believes catalysts like a Chinese lunar mission or a major tech company's satellite launch could rapidly accelerate market appreciation for space investments.

Title: J.B. Hunt reveals its first all-electric truck, 5 to haul bulky items to homes
Summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services has introduced its first five all-electric Mitsubishi Fuso eCanter trucks into its fleet, which will be used for home delivery of bulky items in Houston and California. The company anticipates significant carbon emission reductions and lower operating costs compared to traditional diesel trucks. J.B. Hunt also announced plans to purchase 40 Tesla Semi all-electric trucks, further expanding its commitment to electric vehicles.

Title: Corporate Governance Case Study: Tesla, Twitter, and the Good Weed
Summary: This article examines the corporate governance implications of Elon Musk's tweets regarding taking Tesla private, focusing on Regulation FD issues. It details the SEC enforcement action against Musk and Tesla, resulting in fines, Musk's removal as chairman, and new governance requirements for the company. The authors analyze why Twitter was an unsuitable platform for such disclosures, highlighting the lack of context and clarity in Musk's statements and the ongoing fallout from the incident.
Source: The Harvard Law School Forum on Corporate Governance

Title: More charging stations for Tesla cars likely means more customers for Bibb businesses
Summary: Macon, Georgia, is seeing an increase in Tesla charging stations, which is expected to bring more customers to local businesses. While existing stations downtown are popular with both locals and travelers, new stations are being installed in north Macon to meet growing demand. Tesla declined to comment on the exact timing or location of these new stations.

Title: Saudi wealth fund invests in Tesla rival
Summary: Lucid Motors, a Bay Area electric car startup, has secured over a billion dollars in investment from Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. This funding is expected to enable Lucid to finalize the engineering of its high-end Lucid Air sedan and begin manufacturing in Arizona by 2020. The Saudi fund is also an investor in Tesla, placing it in a unique position of backing both a leading electric luxury car maker and one of its competitors.

Title: Tesla names close Musk friend Larry Ellison to board
Summary: Tesla appointed Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson to its board, aiming to satisfy U.S. regulators' demands for independent oversight following Elon Musk's tweets about taking the company private. Ellison, a close friend and shareholder of Musk, and Wilson-Thompson, Walgreens Boots Alliance's global head of HR, join the board amidst investor concerns about corporate governance. This move follows an SEC settlement requiring Tesla to add independent directors and control Musk's communications.

Title: Tesla names Oracle’s Ellison to board, ending US charges
Summary: Tesla has appointed Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison and Walgreens Boots Alliance’s Kathleen Wilson-Thompson to its board of directors, fulfilling a requirement from a September deal with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. This move resolves federal charges against CEO Elon Musk related to his tweets about taking the company private. Analysts view Ellison's addition positively due to his experience and understanding of maverick CEOs like Musk, which could help channel Musk's energy constructively.

Title: Tesloop, Goodyear Map out the Digital Future of Tires on Teslas Today
Summary: Goodyear and Tesloop Inc. have entered a technology agreement to study and model tire performance using data from Tesloop's fleet of semi-autonomous Tesla vehicles. This collaboration aims to leverage machine learning and predictive analytics to optimize tire maintenance and performance for the next generation of connected passenger mobility fleets, addressing the increasing miles driven by electric, autonomous vehicles. The partnership highlights the focus on creating a real-time digital framework to enhance safety, range, and lower operational costs in future transportation.

Title: 2017 Chevrolet Bolt EV Review: First Drive
Summary: This article reviews the 2017 Chevrolet Bolt EV, highlighting its 238-mile EPA-estimated range, 9.5-hour charging time, and a $37,495 price before tax credits. The author praises its quick acceleration, regenerative braking, and spacious interior, while noting minor drawbacks like uncomfortable seats and a potentially disorienting rearview camera display. The review also touches on the uncertainty surrounding electric car incentives under the incoming Trump administration and compares the Bolt's market entry to the Tesla Model 3.

Title: The curious partnership of Elon Musk and Donald Trump
Summary: This article explores the evolving and "curious partnership" between Elon Musk and Donald Trump. It delves into their initial disagreements and subsequent growing ties, examining what each leader stands to gain from the relationship, particularly concerning technology, clean energy, manufacturing jobs, and Space exploration. Various industry experts and commentators weigh in on what they believe the two should or are discussing.

Title: Tesla Motors, Inc. is now officially Tesla, Inc.
Summary: Tesla Motors, Inc. has officially changed its corporate name to Tesla, Inc., reflecting its expanded business scope beyond just automobile manufacturing. This change acknowledges its acquisition of SolarCity, its ventures into battery storage solutions like Powerwall and Powerpack 2.0, and plans for solar roof tiles. The company's rebranding aligns with its self-description as a technology and design company focused on energy innovation, a shift that has been anticipated since its website URL change last year.

Title: Tesla Removes ‘Motors’ From Its Name
Summary: Tesla Motors officially changed its name to Tesla Inc. on February 1st, reflecting CEO Elon Musk's broader focus on energy products beyond just electric vehicles. This change highlights the company's significant investments in battery production at its Gigafactories and its acquisition of SolarCity, emphasizing its transformation into a comprehensive energy provider. Despite the name change, electric cars remain central to its website for now.

Title: Tesla drops ‘Motors,’ cementing its energy evolution
Summary: Tesla Inc. has officially removed "Motors" from its name, signaling its evolution beyond just an electric car company into a diversified energy firm. This change reflects its acquisitions like SolarCity and its expansion into solar power, energy storage, and battery production for homes and grids, solidifying its ambition to become a vertically integrated energy company. The article highlights Tesla's expanding influence and CEO Elon Musk's broader initiatives in the energy sector.

Title: Meet Lucid, An Aspiring Tesla Competitor Selling A $100K “Private Jet On Wheels”
Summary: Lucid Motors, an electric car startup, unveiled its prototype vehicle, the Lucid Air, a high-end electric car aimed at competing with Tesla. The Lucid Air, with a starting price above $100,000, boasts impressive features like 1,000 horsepower, rapid acceleration, and advanced autonomous driving sensors. While facing the challenge of establishing itself in a market dominated by Tesla, Lucid plans to begin customer deliveries in 2019 and build a manufacturing plant in Arizona.

Title: Tesla wants to open store in Cherry Hill
Summary: Tesla Inc. is seeking approval to convert a furniture store in Cherry Hill, New Jersey, into a sales and service center for its electric vehicles. This proposed facility, located on Route 70, would serve as a "build-to-order" delivery and service hub, differing significantly from traditional car dealerships. If approved, this would be Tesla's fourth sales outlet in New Jersey, following a 2015 law that allowed direct sales of no-emission cars in the state.

Title: Tesla's 'Vision' and Autopilot chip efforts validated by Intel's $15 billion acquisition of Mobileye
Summary: Intel's $15 billion acquisition of Mobileye for its autonomous driving capabilities validates Tesla's in-house approach to developing its own vision system and chip efforts for Autopilot. Tesla had previously discontinued using Mobileye's system and is working on its own SoC, with a world-class team and rumors of a partnership with Samsung. While Tesla's current vision system isn't yet on par with Mobileye's, a software update is expected to bring parity, and future self-driving capabilities could even surpass Mobileye's timeline.

Title: Tesla Model Y will follow Model 3
Summary: Tesla is reportedly developing a compact crossover called the Model Y, which will follow the Model 3. The Model Y is expected to share much of the Model 3's engineering and architecture, incorporating features like gullwing rear doors and full autonomous driving capabilities. It will likely be priced slightly above the Model 3's $37,000 starting price and is anticipated to be unveiled in 2018 with production commencing later that year.

Title: Tesla seeks $1.15B for Model 3 rollout
Summary: Tesla announced a plan to raise $1.15 billion through new stock and convertible securities sales to fund the Model 3 rollout, despite typically burning through cash. The market reacted positively, with Tesla's stock climbing, as investors back Elon Musk's vision for the mass-market electric vehicle. The capital raise is intended to strengthen the balance sheet and mitigate risks associated with the Model 3's production and delivery schedule.

Title: Uber suspends self-driving car program after Arizona crash
Summary: Uber suspended its self-driving car pilot program in Arizona, Pittsburgh, and San Francisco after one of its autonomous vehicles was involved in a crash in Tempe, Arizona. The accident, which caused no serious injuries, occurred when another driver failed to yield to the Uber vehicle. This incident follows other collisions involving self-driving cars, including a fatal accident with a Tesla in 2016.

Title: Tesla closes in on General Motors as most valuable US carmaker
Summary: Tesla is rapidly closing in on General Motors to become the most valuable US carmaker after its market value surpassed Ford's. The electric car manufacturer's shares rose significantly after it announced record deliveries in the first quarter of 2017, and investors are betting on its future growth, especially with the upcoming Model 3 sedan and battery production expansion.

Title: Hyperloop in Texas? Dallas-led AECOM Group is Making the Case
Summary: A Dallas-led AECOM group is proposing a 640-mile Hyperloop route connecting major Texas cities, including Dallas-Fort Worth, Austin, Houston, San Antonio, and Laredo. This team is a semifinalist in the Hyperloop One Global Challenge, aiming to demonstrate Texas as an ideal location for the high-speed transportation system. The technology, still in development by Hyperloop One and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, promises to revolutionize travel times and freight transport.

Title: Tesla, Inc. Stock Is Far Too Risky to Buy … Or Short (TSLA)
Summary: This article discusses the dilemma for investors regarding Tesla (TSLA) stock, noting its rapid appreciation makes it both too risky to short due to valuation disconnection and short-squeeze potential, and too dangerous to buy due to its extended rally and high valuation. The author concludes that TSLA is currently a stock for spectators, recommending patience for potential buyers to wait for a pullback.

Title: All eyes on Tesla as it faces its biggest hurdle yet
Summary: Tesla briefly surpassed General Motors to become the most valuable U.S. automaker, driven by investor optimism despite financial losses and a reliance on future profitability. Analysts highlight Tesla's unique market position and brand loyalty, while questions remain about electric car adoption rates and Tesla's ability to scale production for its new Model 3. The article contrasts Tesla's soaring stock and "cult-like brand" with the frustrations of traditional automakers like GM and Ford, whose stocks have declined.

Title: Tesla rival Lucid rises on home turf
Summary: Lucid Motors, led by former Tesla chief engineer Peter Rawlinson, is positioning its Air sedan as "EV 2.0," aiming to challenge Tesla's Model S. The company is fundraising $240 million for 2019 production in Arizona, with a starting price similar to the Model S, and boasts advanced features and a longer battery range. Despite facing skepticism about the profitability of EV startups, Lucid leans on its experienced team, several of whom previously worked at Tesla, and investments from firms like Venrock and Mitsui Group.

Title: Elon Musk: Robot software will make Tesla worth as much as Apple
Summary: Elon Musk believes that the key to Tesla achieving a $700 billion market capitalization comparable to Apple Inc. lies in its robot manufacturing software. With new production lines for Model 3, batteries, and solar panels launching soon, Musk has the opportunity to prove Tesla's advanced automated manufacturing capabilities. If successful, Tesla's manufacturing prowess could give it a significant advantage in the market.

Title: Tesla battery patents further proof of Elon Musk’s duplicitous views on patents
Summary: This article discusses the perceived hypocrisy of Elon Musk regarding patents, highlighting how Tesla continues to secure patents for battery technology despite Musk's public statements about avoiding patents. It points out that high-ranking Tesla officials are listed as inventors on these patents, suggesting that these actions are known to Musk. The author concludes that Musk's words on patents often contradict the actions of his companies.

Title: Tesla factory workers reveal pain, injury and stress: 'Everything feels like the future but us'
Summary: Tesla factory workers are reporting pain, injuries, and stress despite CEO Elon Musk's defense of workplace conditions and claims of improved safety. The Guardian's exclusive report highlights accounts of grueling pressure, long hours, and numerous ambulance calls, contrasting with Musk's ambitious production goals and his view that the company's $50bn valuation is overvalued. Workers express pride in Tesla's mission but also "mass disappointment" over the human cost of reaching production targets.

Title: Tesla had worse safety records than slaughterhouses and sawmills, but says it’s improving
Summary: Tesla faced criticism for its workplace safety record in 2015, with incident rates significantly higher than the auto industry average and even topping some industries commonly associated with risky work like sawmills and slaughterhouses. While Tesla acknowledged past challenges, the company stated it has since made improvements, claiming the lowest injury rate in the industry and dramatically improved safety scores for early 2017. The report, released by union-connected Worksafe, emphasized that one quarter's statistics aren't enough to prove a trend, raising concerns as Tesla prepared for the launch of its mid-market Model 3.

Title: A new rival for Elon Musk has just blasted off in the space race
Summary: Rocket Lab, a Silicon Valley-funded space company, successfully launched a battery-powered, 3-D printed rocket into space from New Zealand, marking a new competitor in the race for cheap space access. This successful test is the first of three trial flights before planned commercial take-offs later in the year, distinguishing itself by focusing on cheap, disposable rockets rather than reusable ones like those pursued by Elon Musk's SpaceX and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin. Rocket Lab aims for over 50 launches annually, positioning New Zealand as a significant player in the global satellite launch industry.

Title: Tesla Workers Get Seriously Injured Almost Twice as Much as Industry Average
Summary: A non-profit study by Worksafe indicates that workers at Tesla's Fremont plant experienced serious injuries at nearly double the auto industry average. While Tesla acknowledges past challenges, it claims significant improvements have been made, leading to a much lower injury rate. This study emerges as some workers push for unionization and Tesla prepares for critical Model 3 production.

Title: Watch Morgan Stanley Takes a Pause on Tesla With Downgrade
Summary: Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas explains the firm's downgrade of Tesla, citing competitive pressure in AI applications for driving from major tech companies like Amazon, Apple, and Alphabet. He emphasizes that Tesla is viewed as more than just a car company, focusing on sustainable transport energy infrastructure. Jonas discusses how traditional auto manufacturers are struggling to adapt to this new model, which values miles traveled and data monetization.

Title: Toyota sells all shares in Tesla as their tie-up ends
Summary: Toyota Motor Corp announced it sold all its shares in Tesla Inc by the end of 2016, marking the conclusion of their joint electric vehicle development tie-up. The Japanese automaker had initially invested $50 million for a roughly 3 percent stake in Tesla, and the sale is part of a regular review of investments after their partnership ended. Toyota is now stepping up its own electric car development efforts.

Title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk Signals New Factory for Model Y SUV
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced plans for a new factory to produce the Model Y SUV, citing space limitations at their current Fremont plant. This announcement comes even before the Model 3 sedan has begun production. Tesla Inc. is already looking ahead to its next vehicle and the manufacturing capacity required.

Title: Ride-hailing Ucar invests in China Tesla-challenger startup
Summary: Ucar, a ride-hailing app, has led a 2.2 billion yuan (US$324 million) investment into Chinese electric vehicle start-up Xpeng Motors, marking its entry into automobile manufacturing. The company also announced a 10 billion yuan fund focused on future automobile technology, with Xpeng Motors being its first investment. Ucar plans to support Xpeng in manufacturing, sales, after-sales networks, and big-data-enabled marketing.

Title: Electric moment
Summary: Shashank Reddy Goli, a graduate student at Wright State University, is interning at Tesla's manufacturing facility in Fremont, California. He works with the Lean Manufacturing and Operational Excellence team, focusing on optimizing processes, and had the opportunity to meet Elon Musk. Goli, who hopes to work at Tesla full-time after graduation, credits Wright State's faculty and diverse community for his academic success.

Title: Driver killed in Tesla Autopilot crash ignored repeated warnings, NTSB says
Summary: The NTSB has released its initial findings on a fatal 2016 Tesla Autopilot crash, stating that the driver, Joshua Brown, ignored repeated warnings to retake control of the car. The Autopilot system failed to apply brakes when a tractor-trailer turned in front of the Tesla Model S. Tesla has since updated its Autopilot system to prevent drivers from using it if they do not respond to warnings, and emphasizes that Autopilot is a "public beta" and not a "self-driving car."

Title: Yes, you can buy a Tesla electric car at its Scottsdale store
Summary: Tesla Inc. has begun selling cars from its Scottsdale Fashion Square store after winning a lengthy legal battle over its right to conduct direct sales in Arizona. The company obtained a dealer license on September 15, allowing sales from its store and ending challenges that started in 2012 when the Arizona Department of Transportation stated state law prevented automakers from competing with dealerships. Despite previous unsuccessful attempts to change state law, Tesla’s legal victory now allows direct sales in Arizona, a move opposed by the Arizona Automobile Dealers Association.

Title: Why won’t Tesla participate in the J.D. Power quality survey?
Summary: The article discusses why Tesla does not participate in J.D. Power's annual Initial Quality Study. Tesla does not allow J.D. Power access to its customer registration data, which is necessary for the survey, despite other automakers cooperating. J.D. Power acknowledges Tesla's quality but notes their non-participation prevents inclusion in the industry benchmark study.

Title: Tesla, Inc. Starts Selling Tesla-Branded Solar Panels in Its Stores
Summary: Tesla, Inc. has begun selling its newly launched Tesla-branded solar panels in its stores, following a successful pilot program. This move signifies the company's full integration of solar products into its brand after the SolarCity acquisition and aims to leverage Tesla's retail footprint for sales and cost synergies. The company anticipates energy product sales to become a larger share of its revenue.

Title: Elon Musk Teases Sunday Announcement About Tesla Model 3 Timing
Summary: Elon Musk announced via Twitter that an update on the Tesla Model 3 timing would be provided on Sunday. The Model 3, priced at $35,000, is set to begin production next month. This anticipation has significantly boosted Tesla's shares, elevating its market capitalization above competitors like General Motors Co. and Ford Motor Co.

Title: Model 3 launch could signal the beginning -- or end -- for Tesla
Summary: The launch of Tesla's Model 3 is a pivotal moment for the company, signaling a move from niche luxury carmaker to a mass-market electric vehicle provider. While Tesla has surprised some by starting production on time, the company faces immense pressure to meet ambitious production targets and overcome challenges in distribution and service infrastructure. Analysts have varying expectations for Tesla's ability to scale production and maintain customer satisfaction, especially given past issues with other models and the high expectations set by Elon Musk.

Title: Musk Tweets Pictures of First Model 3 to Roll Off the Line
Summary: Elon Musk tweeted pictures of the first Tesla Model 3 sedan to roll off the assembly line. The car was a gift from board member Ira Ehrenpreis for Musk's 46th birthday. Tesla anticipates exponential production increases for the Model 3, despite recent concerns about weakening demand for its Model S and a drop in registrations in key markets like California and Hong Kong.
Source: VOA - Voice of America English News

Title: US Stock Market — Live Quotes, News, Ideas
Summary: This page provides a comprehensive overview of the US stock market, featuring live quotes, news, and trading ideas. It includes market summaries, sector performance data, earnings calendars, and lists of most active and unusual volume stocks. The article also showcases various trading ideas and analyses from experts on specific stocks like NKE, RACE, NVIDIA, and TSLA.

Title: Southern Company launches Tesla Powerpack demo project
Summary: Southern Company and its Gulf Power subsidiary have initiated a two-year research project in Florida using a Tesla Powerpack to better understand the operational aspects of commercial and industrial energy storage systems. The project, in collaboration with the Electric Power Research Institute and Tesla, aims to evaluate the benefits of storage for services like peak shaving, demand management, and backup power. This marks Southern Company's first Tesla Powerpack project and Gulf Power's first storage project, signaling a potentially significant step in energy storage for a major utility operating beyond high-penetration renewable energy areas.

Title: XLY Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:XLY
Summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY), including its price performance, key statistics like AUM and expense ratio, and classification. It also shares various trading ideas and technical analyses from the TradingView community. The fund invests in US large-cap consumer discretionary stocks, with significant concentration in companies like Amazon and Tesla.

Title: Over-the-air software updates coming to GM cars and trucks
Summary: General Motors announced plans to introduce a new electrical vehicle architecture and infotainment system capable of over-the-air (OTA) updates before 2020. This move will bring GM closer to competitors like Tesla, which has been utilizing OTA updates for years, and is expected to save automakers billions and alter their relationship with drivers and dealerships. GM also recently hired a chief data officer to strengthen data analytics for customer experience and business-to-business opportunities.

Title: Tesla’s Big Reveal Shows a Rough Road Ahead
Summary: Tesla unveiled its Model 3 sedan, with CEO Elon Musk delivering the first 30 vehicles. While the company holds over 500,000 refundable deposits, investors are cautioned against expecting a similar stock market reaction. The article suggests that despite the fanfare, the Model 3 might struggle to meet the mass-market hype surrounding it.

Title: Tesla, Inc.'s Model 3: What We Know So Far
Summary: Ahead of its final unveiling, Tesla had already revealed significant details about the Model 3, including its $35,000 starting price, over 215 miles of range, and sub-six-second 0-60 mph acceleration. The vehicle, smaller than the Model S, features a 15-inch display and will utilize Autopilot sensors, though Supercharging will not be free. Investors were watching closely for additional information at the launch event.

Title: Tesla delivers first lower-cost Model 3 cars
Summary: Tesla Inc. has delivered its first 30 Model 3 electric cars to employees, marking the release of its long-anticipated affordable vehicle with a $35,000 starting price and 220-mile range. CEO Elon Musk expects "manufacturing hell" for at least six months to meet the goal of producing 500,000 cars next year, with 500,000 people already having placed deposits. The Model 3 aims to transition Tesla from a luxury brand to the mainstream, despite potential production challenges and a global market shift towards SUVs.

Title: Industry Focus: Manufacturing
Summary: This article discusses the growth spurt in Nevada's manufacturing industry, highlighting challenges and opportunities identified by industry leaders. Key issues include workforce shortages due to rapid expansion and competition from large companies like Tesla and Panasonic, as well as regulatory hurdles. Automation is presented as a significant factor in increasing efficiency and enabling companies to remain competitive in the US.

Title: Tesla 3 official launch depends on suppliers
Summary: Tesla's ambitious Model 3 launch timeline is heavily reliant on its suppliers' ability to meet high production demands, with CEO Elon Musk stating the company needs to produce 10,000 cars per week. The article highlights the critical role of strong supplier relationships for manufacturers with tight deadlines, citing issues faced by Apple due to supply chain delays. Despite past production struggles and what Musk calls "manufacturing hell," Tesla's proximity to suppliers in Fremont, California, is expected to help them achieve their Model 3 production goals.

Title: Tesla to Sell $1.5 Billion in Debt to Fuel Aggressive Expansion
Summary: Tesla Inc. is planning to sell $1.5 billion in its first-ever traditional bond offering to finance its aggressive expansion, particularly with the launch of its lower-priced Model 3 sedan. This move signifies the company's shift from a luxury car manufacturer to a mass-market competitor. The bonds are expected to be sold as early as Friday, with Goldman Sachs Group Inc. underwriting the deal.

Title: Exclusive: Tesla developing self-driving tech for semi-truck, wants to test in Nevada
Summary: Tesla Inc. is developing a self-driving, long-haul electric semi-truck capable of platooning and is seeking to test prototypes in Nevada and California, as revealed through correspondence with the Nevada DMV. This initiative places Tesla in a competitive realm of commercial transport, alongside companies like Uber and Alphabet's Waymo, despite skepticism regarding the economic feasibility of long-haul electric trucking due to battery range limitations. Tesla has been a leader in developing self-driving technology for its luxury cars, including the lower-priced Model 3.

Title: Tesla's first junk bond offering is a hit, but now Elon Musk must deliver: 'No more room for excuses'
Summary: Tesla successfully raised $1.8 billion, $300 million more than planned, in its first high-yield junk bond offering, indicating strong demand despite a recent drop in high-yield bonds. The company must now deliver on profitability, particularly with its new Model 3, as it has burned through billions of dollars in recent years. Analysts believe this offering shows investor confidence in Tesla's long-term growth story, but emphasize the need for results.

Title: Bond investors give Tesla a $1.8 billion endorsement
Summary: Bond investors backed Tesla Inc.'s first foray into the U.S. junk bond market, providing a $1.8 billion boost for the electric car maker. The strong demand allowed Tesla to increase its offering from an initial $1.5 billion, with the proceeds intended to finance production of the mass-market Model 3. This successful debt issuance highlights robust investor appetite in the high-yield market, despite some analysts considering it pricey.

Title: Merck CEO Resigns from Trump Council after Charlottesville
Summary: Merck CEO Kenneth Frazier resigned from President Trump's American Manufacturing Council, citing intolerance and extremism after the Charlottesville violence. Frazier stated his responsibility to take a stand against hatred and bigotry, which prompted a response from Trump regarding drug prices. Other executives, including Elon Musk and Robert Iger, had previously left advisory councils due to disagreements with Trump's policies.

Title: Why the Texas lawyer who started Southwest Airlines in 1967 never gave himself a raise or a bonus
Summary: Herb Kelleher, co-founder of Southwest Airlines, famously never took a pay raise or bonus to set a good example for employees, instead receiving compensation in stock options. He maintained that this decision aligned with his philosophy of fiscal conservatism for the airline. Kelleher's approach is mirrored by other prominent CEOs like Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg, who also take minimal or no salaries.

Title: SCE’s Wind Energy, Energy Storage Featured in CNBC World TV Show
Summary: Southern California Edison's (SCE) leadership in clean energy, particularly its use of wind power and battery storage, was featured in a CNBC World TV series episode titled "Wind." The episode highlighted SCE's Mira Loma battery storage facility, which uses 396 Tesla Powerpacks to store energy, and its connection to the Tehachapi Renewable Transmission Project. Edison International's president and CEO, Pedro Pizarro, also discussed the importance of renewable energy and storage for SCE's future.

Title: Why this Tesla fan thinks the company is losing its way
Summary: An early Tesla adopter and owner of three vehicles criticizes the company for perceived loss of focus on consumer satisfaction, citing numerous product issues and a lack of responsiveness from customer service. Despite his belief in Tesla's mission and Elon Musk's vision, the author, who is now suing the company, fears that poor customer service and faulty design could jeopardize Tesla's future success. He emphasizes that being innovative should not excuse a company from being responsive to its customers.

Title: Novonix secures Canadian funding for its lithium battery technology
Summary: Novonix Limited (ASX:NVX) has secured C$500,000 in funding from the Government of Canada to advance its innovative battery testing technologies. The company, a developer and supplier for the lithium-ion battery industry, will use the funds for research and development of battery chargers and cell testing, aiming to expand its international marketing efforts. This investment is timely as Novonix expects growing demand for energy-efficient batteries, with its expertise already sought by major companies like Apple and Tesla Motors.

Title: LG Group rules out producing its own electric cars
Summary: LG Group has clarified that it is not planning to enter the electric vehicle manufacturing business, despite aggressively expanding its presence in the vehicle components sector. An official stated that the company is not considering manufacturing complete vehicles. Industry observers believe LG Group aims to be a comprehensive automotive parts firm, similar to Bosch, rather than an EV manufacturer like Tesla.

Title: Tesla's head of business development leaves after 11 years
Summary: Diarmuid O'Connell, Tesla's vice president of business development, has left the electric car company after more than 11 years. His responsibilities, including government relations, will be taken over by Jon McNeill, president of global sales and service. O'Connell stated he felt it was the right time to move on and spend more time with his family after seeing Tesla grow from a startup through the launch of the Model 3.

Title: This is the $50,000 electric pickup truck that will take on Tesla
Summary: Workhorse Group is introducing the W-15, an electric pickup truck with a range-extending gas motor, priced at just over $50,000, aiming to compete with Tesla. CEO Stephen Burns highlights its performance claims and notes significant consumer interest, with production for individual consumers set to begin in 2019. The company also anticipates strong demand from fleet users, with initial production vehicles expected in late 2018.

Title: Tesla’s China Dream Edges Closer to Reality
Summary: China is reportedly considering relaxing rules requiring foreign automakers to have a local partner, a change that could significantly benefit Tesla Inc. This move would allow Tesla to manufacture vehicles in China, a goal the company has pursued due to the country being the world's largest market for electric vehicles. This regulatory shift could address a major hurdle for Tesla, which has struggled to find a suitable local partner.

Title: Tesla continues to rack up patents despite Elon Musk’s supposed distaste for patents
Summary: Despite Elon Musk's public aversion to patents, Tesla Inc. continues to actively pursue and obtain new patents, including a recent application for a robotic battery swapping system. The article highlights the perceived hypocrisy in Musk's stance, arguing that his companies' patenting activities contradict his claims that patents stifle progress and primarily lead to lawsuits. It suggests that Tesla's ongoing patenting efforts are strategic business decisions, essential for protecting innovations and gaining market advantage, rather than an altruistic move.

Title: Tesla is said to shift to Intel from Nvidia for infotainment
Summary: Tesla is reportedly switching its infotainment system chip supplier from Nvidia Corp to Intel Corp for its Model 3 and upcoming vehicle versions. This move highlights the growing importance of the automotive market for chipmakers and Intel's strategy to diversify beyond personal computers. While Tesla is a smaller automaker, its adoption of new technology makes such supplier changes significant in the tech industry.

Title: Behind Tesla’s Production Delays: Parts of Model 3 Were Being Made by Hand
Summary: Tesla's production of its Model 3 sedan has been significantly hampered by "production bottlenecks," leading to far fewer vehicles than promised. Unknown to most, major parts of the Model 3 were being assembled by hand as recently as early September, away from the automated production line. Experts deem this method highly unusual for mass production, likening it to outdated manufacturing techniques.

Title: Tesla Model 3 production falls short of targets in Q3
Summary: Tesla Inc. missed its third-quarter production goals for the new Model 3 sedan, delivering only 220 cars and producing a total of 260, far short of CEO Elon Musk's initial projections. The company attributed the shortfall to "production bottlenecks" but stated there are no fundamental issues and expressed confidence in addressing them. This performance raises concerns among analysts about Tesla's ability to transition from a luxury car manufacturer to a mainstream automaker, although the company did report record overall vehicle deliveries for the quarter.

Title: Tesla Recalling 11,000 Model X SUVs for Seat Issue
Summary: Tesla Inc. is recalling 11,000 Model X SUVs globally due to a potential issue where rear seats might not lock into place. The recall affects vehicles manufactured between October 28, 2016, and August 16, 2017, and Tesla estimates only about 3 percent of those have the defect. The company discovered the problem during internal testing and has not received any reports of injuries.
Source: VOA - Voice of America English News

Title: Tesla fires hundreds of employees, 400 to 700 may have lost their jobs
Summary: Tesla fired hundreds of employees, estimated to be between 400 and 700, as part of its annual performance reviews. This comes as the company is under pressure to ramp up production of its new Model 3 sedan and despite still looking to hire more workers. Tesla denies that union activities played a role in the firings, even though some pro-union employees were among those dismissed.

Title: Volvo Unveils a Direct Challenge to Tesla
Summary: Volvo has unveiled its first high-performance electric-car model in Shanghai, directly challenging Tesla Inc. This move reinforces Volvo's commitment to exclusively produce electric or hybrid vehicles starting in 2019. Its new stand-alone premium electric-vehicle company, Polestar, will launch its first two vehicles in 2019, backed by a $755 million investment from Volvo and Zhejiang Geely Holding Group Co.

Title: Tesla reaches deal to set up a factory in China
Summary: Electric-car maker Tesla Inc. has reached an agreement to establish a manufacturing facility in Shanghai, China. This deal, allowing for a wholly-owned factory in the city's free-trade zone, could significantly reduce production costs for Tesla. However, the company would still face China’s 25% import tariff on its vehicles.

Title: Elon Musk Was Wrong About Self-Driving Teslas
Summary: This article discusses how Elon Musk's promises about Tesla's self-driving capabilities have not materialized as quickly as advertised. Tesla announced a plan for fully autonomous driving a year prior, but the feature is still not fully functional, despite being marketed to customers. The article highlights the discrepancy between the promised self-driving technology and its current implementation.

Title: A Tale of Tesla Seats Hints at Why So Few Cars Built
Summary: The article explains how Tesla's decision to insource the production of its car seats, driven by Elon Musk's pursuit of perfection and control, is contributing to the company's manufacturing bottlenecks and missed production targets for the Model 3. Industry experts question this vertical integration strategy, suggesting it detracts from Tesla's core competencies and causes production inefficiencies, despite Musk viewing it as an opportunity for innovation. The delays and recalls related to seating highlight the challenges Tesla faces in scaling from a niche luxury producer to a mass-market automaker.
Source: VOA - Voice of America English News

Title: Payne: First Tesla Michigan gallery opens at Somerset mall
Summary: Tesla Inc. has opened its first stand-alone gallery space in Michigan at the Somerset Collection mall in Troy. This gallery, similar to an Apple store and located next to one, allows customers to learn about Tesla vehicles and energy products but not purchase cars directly due to Michigan's direct-to-consumer sales ban. The opening comes as Tesla battles state laws restricting its direct sales model, showcasing Model S and Model X vehicles, and highlighting its maintenance approach for electric vehicles.

Title: Tesla Buys Minnesota-Based Manufacturer
Summary: Tesla Inc. has acquired Perbix, a Minnesota-based manufacturer of highly automated equipment that has supplied Tesla for three years. This acquisition is part of CEO Elon Musk's strategy to enhance factory efficiency, following previous acquisitions aimed at boosting manufacturing expertise. Perbix, currently employing 150 people, will remain based north of Minneapolis with plans to recruit more staff.

Title: Tesla racial discrimination class action gets 2025 trial date
Summary: A California judge has set a tentative pretrial date of August 29, 2025, for a class action lawsuit alleging racial discrimination against nearly 6,000 Black former Tesla workers at its Fremont plant. The class certification aims to establish common facts and determine if injunctive relief is necessary against Tesla, with individual cases to follow for damages. The lawsuit, originally filed in 2017 by Marcus Vaughn, claims Tesla's factory was a "hotbed for racist behavior" and failed to address complaints.

Title: Tesla, Elon Musk Unveil Electric Semi-Truck
Summary: Tesla Inc. unveiled its all-electric Class 8 tractor, marking its entry into the commercial truck business. The Tesla Semi, slated for 2019 production, is a day cab with a 500-mile range, designed for improved energy efficiency and lower operating costs compared to diesel trucks. It features a unique center driver's seat, dual touchscreens, enhanced autopilot, and advanced safety features, including jack-knife prevention and "armor glass" windshields.

Title: New Tesla Roadster upstages rollout of electric big-rig truck
Summary: Tesla Inc. CEO Elon Musk unveiled a new $200,000 Roadster, which he claimed would be the fastest production car ever, at an event that was primarily for the debut of an electric heavy-duty truck. The sports car can travel 620 miles on a single charge and accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in 1.9 seconds. This dual unveiling highlighted Tesla's ambitious projects while also drawing attention away from the company's struggles to roll out a more affordable sedan.

Title: Trucking company J.B. Hunt reserves Tesla trucks
Summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. has placed a reservation for Tesla Inc.'s new Semi trucks, following their launch. The trucking company did not specify the exact number of Tesla trucks it plans to acquire. Tesla's Semi trucks aim to compete with traditional diesel trucks by offering an affordable electric alternative with comparable range and cargo capacity.

Title: J.B. Hunt, Wal-Mart reserve Tesla electric big rig, analyst questions battery life, cost
Summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services and Wal-Mart Stores have reserved "multiple" Tesla Semi electric big rigs after their unveiling, with J.B. Hunt planning to use them in intermodal and dedicated segments on the West Coast, and Wal-Mart testing 15 trucks in the U.S. and Canada. However, analysts from Jefferies and Stifel are questioning the battery longevity, total cost of ownership compared to diesel, and Tesla's decision to enter a market segment they believe is not well-suited for electric vehicles. Despite Tesla's claims of 500-mile range and lower TCO, concerns remain regarding battery depreciation and the estimated higher upfront cost.

Title: J.B. Hunt, Wal-Mart climb aboard Tesla's electric truck
Summary: Wal-Mart Stores Inc and J.B. Hunt have placed high-profile orders for Tesla's new electric Semi trucks, though initial plans indicate testing rather than large-volume purchases. Customers are reserving trucks with $5,000 deposits, reflecting uncertainty in the electric commercial vehicle market. Tesla and other manufacturers are investing in electric trucks, anticipating a market shift driven by emissions regulations and government incentives.

Title: Tesla unveils ambitious electric semi-truck
Summary: Tesla unveiled its new electric semitractor-trailer, with CEO Elon Musk stating it can travel 500 miles on a single charge with a full 80,000-pound load and will be more cost-effective than diesel semis. Production is set to begin in 2019, with a $5,000 deposit required, but the semi's price was not disclosed. The announcement comes amidst Tesla's production struggles with the Model 3 and other ventures.

Title: J.B. Hunt Transport Services reserves Tesla electric Class 8 trucks
Summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services announced a reservation to purchase multiple Tesla Semi electric Class 8 trucks, unveiled by Tesla on November 16. The company plans to deploy these electric tractors to its Intermodal and Dedicated Contract Services divisions for West Coast operations, particularly for local and dray routes, aligning with its $500 million investment in technology and sustainable initiatives.

Title: Elon Musk’s fast route to more cash: A new Tesla Roadster
Summary: Elon Musk surprised attendees at a Tesla event by unveiling a new version of the Roadster, an expensive electric sports car that could quickly generate over $250 million. This comes as Tesla faces a cash drain, and the new Roadster is claimed to be the fastest production car ever. The introduction of the Roadster offers a potential fast route to additional funding for Tesla Inc.

Title: Major Fleets Line Up to Test Tesla Semi
Summary: Major trucking companies and retailers, including J.B. Hunt, NFI Industries, Wal-Mart, Meijer, and Loblaw Cos., have placed reservations for or plan to test the all-electric Tesla Semi, which is scheduled to enter production in 2019. These companies aim to evaluate the truck's performance in their supply chains, reduce their carbon footprint, and potentially realize cost savings through sustainable technology. While fleets are enthusiastic about the prospect of electric trucks, some key questions remain regarding the economic case, price, and battery pack weight.

Title: Retailers to Pilot New Tesla Electric Semi
Summary: Several major retailers, including Meijer, J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc., and Walmart, are partnering with Tesla to pilot its new electric semi-trucks. These partnerships aim to test the vehicles' performance, reduce carbon footprints, and achieve cost savings through improved fuel efficiency. Production for the semis is expected to begin in 2019, following their unveiling by Elon Musk.

Title: Lucid moves its electric car ambitions into a spacious new HQ
Summary: Lucid is relocating its headquarters to a new, larger facility in Newark, California, to accommodate growth as it prepares to launch its first vehicle, the Lucid Air. The Lucid Air is an all-electric luxury sport sedan aiming for a 2019 launch, designed to compete with Tesla's Model S, offering high performance and collaborative consumption features. The move signifies a critical phase for Lucid's product development and ambition in the electric vehicle market.

Title: Tesla Reveals Price Range for Electric Semi
Summary: Tesla Inc. has announced the expected price range for its all-electric Class 8 truck, the Tesla Semi, will be between $150,000 and $200,000. The truck will offer 300 or 500 miles of range and is anticipated to enter production in 2019, with a "founders series" option available for $200,000. Tesla projects significant fuel savings and a two-year payback period for the Semi.

Title: Build fast, fix later: speed hurts quality at Tesla, some workers say
Summary: A Reuters investigation, based on accounts from nine current and former Tesla employees, reveals that a significant percentage of Model S and Model X vehicles require fixes after rolling off the assembly line, with some exceeding 90% defect rates. This "build fast, fix later" approach, driven by pressure to maintain production speed, results in costly rework and raises concers about Tesla's ability to scale high-quality manufacturing for its mass-market Model 3. Despite Tesla's claims of rigorous quality control, experts and workers indicate that persistent defects and a lack of manufacturing experience hinder the company's quality standards compared to established luxury automakers.

Title: Tesla builds world’s largest battery in Australian outback
Summary: Tesla has officially plugged in the world's largest lithium-ion battery into Australia's state grid, fulfilling Elon Musk's 100-day guarantee. Located near Jamestown, Australia, the 100-megawatt battery stores energy from the Hornsdale Wind Farm and can power 30,000 homes for up to an hour. This initiative aims to stabilize South Australia's power grid, which has experienced blackouts, and makes the state a leader in dispatchable renewable energy.

Title: Tesla Wannabe Lucid Takes on the Auto Industry With an Electric Stunner
Summary: Lucid, a Silicon Valley-based electric vehicle startup, is positioning itself as a competitor to Tesla with its luxurious Air sedan. The company emphasizes a pragmatic approach to production, leveraging the experience of former Tesla Model S chief engineer Peter Rawlinson and planning to gradually scale up manufacturing to eventually produce 130,000 cars annually in Casa Grande, Arizona. Lucid aims to capitalize on the growing global demand for electric vehicles, particularly in markets like China that favor large, luxurious sedans.

Title: First Trust Nasdaq Transportation ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:FTXR)
Summary: The First Trust Nasdaq Transportation ETF (FTXR) tracks an index of 30 U.S. transportation companies, with major holdings including General Motors, Tesla, and Union Pacific. The ETF has seen its shares increase by 8.8% this year, trading at $42.20 as of February 27, 2026. Institutional investors like Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Maridea Wealth Management LLC are significant shareholders.

Title: Anheuser-Busch Orders 40 Tesla Semi Trucks
Summary: Anheuser-Busch has reserved 40 of Tesla Inc.'s all-electric Semi trucks to reduce fuel costs and vehicle emissions. The U.S. subsidiary plans to use these trucks for shipments to wholesalers within a 150 to 200-mile range of its breweries, aligning with Tesla's promised 500-mile range. These vehicles will be integrated into the brewer's dedicated fleets of approximately 750 trucks, which are managed by outside carriers.

Title: Industry leaders Rusty Rush & Michael McRoberts of Rush Enterprises talk electric trucks, the growing Tech Rodeo, domestic energy & market conditions
Summary: Rusty Rush, head of Rush Truck Centers, and Michael McRoberts discuss the future of electric trucks, anticipating their primary role in the medium-duty, last-mile delivery segment rather than heavy-duty, long-haul trucking. They express skepticism about Tesla's direct sales and service model for commercial vehicles and highlight challenges like infrastructure and payload. The article also touches on the expanding Tech Rodeo, the tech shortage, economic impact on trucking, and the outlook for 2018.

Title: PepsiCo makes biggest public pre-order of Tesla Semis: 100 trucks
Summary: PepsiCo Inc. has placed the largest known public pre-order for Tesla's electric Semi trucks, reserving 100 vehicles. This move aims to reduce fuel costs and fleet emissions, aligning with PepsiCo's goal to cut greenhouse gas emissions across its supply chain by 20 percent by 2030. The beverage and snack giant plans to use the Semis for shipments between manufacturing facilities, distribution centers, and retailers within the trucks' 500-mile range.

Title: Frito-Lay Parent Orders New Tesla Semi Electric Trucks
Summary: PepsiCo Inc., the parent company of Frito-Lay, has placed an order for 100 Tesla Semi electric trucks, marking the largest known order for the new long-haul vehicle. The company plans to use these trucks for shipping snack foods and beverages between facilities and to retailers to lower fuel costs and reduce fleet emissions. This move is part of PepsiCo's strategy to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 20 percent across its supply chain.

Title: NIO ES8 Challenges the Tesla Model X in China
Summary: NIO has launched its first production model, the ES8, an aluminum-bodied, seven-seat electric SUV, in China, positioning it as a competitor to the Tesla Model X. The ES8 features a 70-kWh battery, dual motors producing 644 hp, and advanced automated driving technology including Mobileye's EyeQ4 chip. It also offers a battery swapping service and starts at 448,000 RMB, roughly equivalent to $67,715 USD.

Title: Here's What Brown Can Do For Tesla Motors
Summary: UPS is purchasing 125 all-electric semi trucks from Tesla, making it the largest known order for the vehicle to date. This move is part of UPS's ongoing efforts to transition towards an electric fleet and reduce fuel expenditures, with plans to thoroughly test the Tesla trucks in real-world routes within the United States. Both companies are collaborating to ensure the success of this "introductory technology" and promote their leadership in green initiatives.

Title: Meet the NIO ES8: a Fully Electric, 7-Seat SUV With 220 Miles of Range
Summary: Chinese electric carmaker NIO has unveiled its first mass-market model, the ES8 SUV, a 7-seat electric vehicle with an estimated 220 miles of range and standard all-wheel drive, launching in early 2018. It features a swappable battery and is priced at 448,000 Chinese yuan (approx. $68,000 USD), offering a cheaper alternative to the Tesla Model X in China. NIO also announced plans for a second batch of its EP9 hypercar, known for its record-breaking Nürburgring lap time and 1,341 horsepower.

Title: Elon Musk Touts Tesla Pickup Plans, Though Light on Detail
Summary: Elon Musk has teased plans for a Tesla pickup truck, building on his previous "Master Plan, Part Deux." The Tesla CEO indicated on Twitter that the truck would be released after a new compact SUV, which he suggested could be available as early as 2019. Consistent with his style, Mr. Musk provided few specific details about the new vehicle.

Title: All-New Tesla Roadster: What You Need to Know
Summary: Tesla unveiled an all-electric second-generation Roadster with record-setting performance figures, including a 0-60 mph sprint in 1.9 seconds and a 620-mile range. The new Roadster, designed by Franz von Holzhausen, features all-wheel drive, a 200 kWh battery, a 2+2 seating configuration, and a removable glass roof. With a base price of $200,000, it aims to outperform existing supercars and will be released in 2020.

Title: For Tesla, Deliver, Don’t Promise, in 2018
Summary: In 2018, Tesla CEO Elon Musk needs to prioritize the production of the Model 3 mass-market sedan over promising new vehicles like electric semi-trucks or sports cars. Tesla delivered significantly fewer Model 3s than forecasted in the third quarter of 2017, highlighting the need for operational focus. The company's credibility with investors hinges on making its Model 3 dreams a reality and achieving profitable high-volume production.

Title: Ford plans $11 billion investment, 40 electrified vehicles by 2022
Summary: Ford Motor Co. announced a significant increase in its electric vehicle investment plan to $11 billion by 2022, aiming to introduce 40 hybrid and fully electric vehicles. This move is a sharp increase from a previous $4.5 billion target and reflects a broader industry trend towards electrification driven by regulatory pressures and the success of companies like Tesla. Ford also plans to electrify its mainstream and iconic vehicles, including a hybrid F-150 truck and a high-performance electric utility vehicle, and will cut $14 billion in costs over five years by shifting away from sedans and internal combustion engines.

Title: This ETF shows how you can pick stocks for rapid growth while doing good
Summary: The iShares MSCI USA ESG Select ETF demonstrates how to achieve rapid growth while adhering to ethical standards. This ETF, which tracks the MSCI USA ESG Select Index, has outperformed the stock market and includes companies with strong sales growth and positive environmental, social, and corporate governance (ESG) criteria. Tesla is highlighted as one of its stockholdings.

Title: UPS, Workhorse team up to develop all-electric Class 5 truck
Summary: UPS is partnering with Workhorse Group to develop all-electric Class 5 delivery trucks, with an initial deployment of 50 vehicles for real-world testing. These trucks are expected to offer a nearly 400 percent fuel efficiency improvement and a 100-mile range. This initiative is part of UPS's broader strategy to electrify its fleet, building on existing electric and hybrid vehicles and recent orders for Tesla Semi tractors and Fuso eCanter trucks.

Title: Axon CEO may make $1 billion in the next 10 years or nothing at all, but he's excited for the challenge
Summary: Axon CEO and co-founder Rick Smith's new performance plan is modeled after Tesla CEO Elon Musk's compensation plan, offering him the potential to earn $1 billion over the next decade or nothing at all. This ambitious compensation structure highlights a significant shift in executive incentives, directly tying leadership wealth to long-term company performance. The plan reflects a growing trend of incentivizing high-risk, high-reward leadership in the tech industry.

Title: For backup power, batteries join the mix as prices come down
Summary: Home battery systems are becoming a more affordable and popular alternative to traditional generators for backup power, especially in areas prone to storm outages. Sunrun Inc. has introduced its Brightbox system in Massachusetts at a competitive price, aiming to capitalize on consumer demand for reliable, clean backup energy. Other companies like Tesla are also expanding their home battery offerings as costs decline and incentives grow.

Title: Musk’s $2.6 billion award cheered on by big Tesla shareholders
Summary: Two of Tesla Inc.'s largest shareholders, Baillie Gifford & Co. and T. Rowe Price Group Inc., are supporting a plan to award Elon Musk a compensation package valued at $2.6 billion. This backing comes despite proxy adviser Glass Lewis & Co. recommending against the plan due to potential shareholder dilution. The shareholders believe Musk's vision is crucial for Tesla's continued growth not just in automotive but also in energy markets.

Title: Uber Crash Is Nightmare Driverless World Feared but Expected
Summary: A self-driving Uber test car struck and killed a pedestrian in Tempe, Arizona, on March 18, raising significant concerns about consumer confidence in autonomous vehicle technology. This incident, the first known fatality involving an autonomous test vehicle and a pedestrian, is prompting investigations and a call to slow down the industry's rapid march toward commercialization, especially in contrast to a previous Tesla fatality which involved a driver using an assistance system. The event is expected to have a broader impact on the future development and regulation of fully autonomous driving systems.

Title: Texas DMV seeks to clarify dealership law — as it tries to enforce it
Summary: The Texas Department of Motor Vehicles is seeking to clarify and simplify its dealership ownership laws, which currently prohibit motor vehicle manufacturers from owning dealerships, as it grapples with ongoing enforcement cases against Berkshire Hathaway Inc. and Cummins Inc. The proposed changes, which could impact these cases, aim to define "own" more precisely and limit prohibitions to manufacturers owning dealerships that sell their specific products. This initiative comes amidst pushback from the Texas Automobile Dealers Association, which has different stances on the enforcement against Berkshire Hathaway and Cummins, and highlights the contentious nature of current regulations for companies like Tesla Inc.

Title: FedEx Reserves 20 Tesla Semi Electric Trucks
Summary: FedEx Corp. announced it has reserved 20 Tesla Semi electric trucks, which are slated for production in 2019 and will be operated by FedEx Freight. This investment highlights FedEx's commitment to sustainability, improving road safety, and reducing its environmental impact. The Tesla Semi trucks are expected to offer advanced safety features and significant energy cost savings compared to diesel trucks.

Title: FedEx Orders 20 Tesla Semis
Summary: FedEx Corp has placed an order for 20 Tesla Semi electric trucks for its FedEx Freight less-than-truckload unit. This investment reflects FedEx's commitment to improving road safety and reducing its environmental impact. The Tesla Semi, unveiled in November, offers various range options and features designed for increased safety and fuel savings.

Title: Home Solar Dims as Tesla, Others Curb Aggressive Sales
Summary: The growth of residential solar installations in the U.S. declined last year for the first time in over a decade. This slowdown is attributed to leading installers, including Tesla Inc., curbing aggressive sales practices. Historically, residential solar had seen significant annual growth, averaging 49% between 2010 and 2016, making this decline a notable shift in the market.

Title: Twin-win venture: How Tarang Jain built a global automotive business
Summary: Tarang Jain, founder of Varroc Engineering, became India's newest auto billionaire after successfully acquiring Visteon's global lighting business in 2012. This strategic move transformed Varroc into a global automotive player, with customers like Ford and Tesla, and significantly improved its product margin profile. As Varroc prepares to go public, Jain aims for further growth, eyeing an ambitious sales target of ₹20,000 crore, potentially through another acquisition.

Title: Tesla says its factory is safer. But it left injuries off the books
Summary: An investigation by Reveal found that Tesla failed to report serious injuries on legally mandated reports, making its injury numbers appear better than they were. Former safety experts claimed Tesla prioritized production speed over worker safety, with CEO Elon Musk's preferences influencing safety protocols. The article details instances of undercounted injuries, inadequate training, and health issues faced by workers due to chemicals and repetitive tasks.
Source: Reveal from The Center for Investigative Reporting

Title: Tesla hit by government investigation after Reveal story
Summary: California’s workplace safety agency, Cal/OSHA, launched an investigation into Tesla Inc. following a Reveal investigation that alleged safety problems and underreported injuries at Tesla's Fremont factory. While Tesla maintains its injury records are accurate and criticizes Reveal's reporting as "baseless," Cal/OSHA stated it takes such reports seriously and will examine all aspects of workplace safety regulations at the company. Tesla has faced over 40 health and safety violations from Cal/OSHA since 2013, though it claims to have never been cited for inaccurate injury record-keeping.
Source: Reveal from The Center for Investigative Reporting

Title: iShares U.S. Consumer Discretionary ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:IYC) $IYC
Summary: The iShares U.S. Consumer Discretionary ETF (IYC) invests primarily in U.S. consumer discretionary equities, tracking a market-cap-weighted index. Launched in June 2000 and managed by BlackRock, IYC has assets under management of $1.29 billion and an expense ratio of 0.39%. The ETF's top holdings include major companies like Amazon, Tesla, and Netflix, and it has seen a slight increase in price this year.

Title: Jim Keller Joins Intel to Lead Silicon Engineering
Summary: Intel announced that Jim Keller will join the company as a senior vice president to lead silicon engineering, including system-on-chip (SoC) development and integration. Keller brings over two decades of experience in x86 and ARM-based microarchitecture design from companies like Tesla, AMD, and Apple, where he contributed to the Zen architecture and early A-series processors. His appointment is expected to accelerate Intel's transformation in heterogeneous process and architectures for the data-centric computing era.

Title: Iowa-based Winnebago is launching an all-electric RV platform
Summary: Winnebago Industries has unveiled an all-electric commercial vehicle platform, marking a significant step towards emissions-free RVs. This zero-emissions Class A vehicle, available in 33-foot and 38-foot lengths, is currently suited for urban and semi-urban short-range commercial applications like mobile clinics, with plans to extend the technology for retail use by increasing its range. The company anticipates future retail applications as battery technology improves and costs decrease.

Title: Injury at Tesla solar business draws company’s biggest safety fine
Summary: Federal safety officials levied a record fine of over $110,000 against Tesla Inc.'s solar business after an employee suffered a high-voltage electrical shock at a Massachusetts facility. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration cited Tesla for nine serious safety violations, including inadequate training and protective gear. While Tesla plans to appeal, this incident adds to a pattern of safety concerns at the company's various operations, including its Fremont car factory, which has faced numerous citations and investigations.
Source: Reveal from The Center for Investigative Reporting

Title: George Soros' fund bought $35 million of Tesla bonds while loading up on Amazon, Netflix stock
Summary: George Soros' investment firm, Soros Fund Management, purchased $35 million worth of Tesla convertible bonds in the first quarter of 2018, providing significant backing to the troubled electric carmaker. The fund also made substantial investments in Amazon and Netflix stock, acquiring 51,200 shares of Amazon and 148,500 shares of Netflix, while simultaneously divesting its holdings in Twitter. These moves offer insight into Soros Fund Management's investment strategy during a period of market volatility for some tech giants.

Title: Tesla belatedly adds injuries to its books, but it might not face penalties
Summary: Tesla Inc. has retroactively added 13 previously unrecorded 2017 employee injuries to its logs after questions were raised by Reveal. Despite this belated update, which slightly increases Tesla's injury rate, the company may avoid penalties due to a six-month statute of limitations for citing employers for unrecorded incidents under current regulations. This situation highlights a broader issue of injury undercounting and the challenges regulators face in enforcing workplace safety laws.
Source: Reveal from The Center for Investigative Reporting

Title: Salt River Project launches first standalone storage project
Summary: Salt River Project (SRP) has launched Arizona's first standalone battery storage project, a 10 MW, four-hour system purchased from Fluence Energy and operated by AES. This initiative aims to provide flexible peaking capacity and explore grid-scale battery storage, coming as the Arizona Corporation Commission considers state energy storage goals, including a potential 3 GW target by 2030. The project follows SRP's previous struggles with integrating renewables and a settlement with SolarCity that included plans for a 25 MW battery from Tesla and an incentive program for customer-installed storage.

Title: Kauai utility moves ahead with Tesla, AES storage on road to 70% renewables
Summary: Kauai Island Utility Cooperative (KIUC) is accelerating its renewable energy goals, aiming for 70% by the end of next year, largely due to large energy storage projects paired with solar. The Hawaii Public Utilities Commission approved a 19.3 MW solar facility and 70 MWh battery energy storage system by AES Distributed Energy, while KIUC and Tesla also opened a new 13 MW solar project and 52 MWh battery system. These projects are swiftly moving the island away from fossil fuels, with the AES project expected to displace 2.8 million gallons of diesel annually and provide power at a low cost of $0.1085/kWh under a 25-year power purchase agreement.

Title: Tesla: Tips On When To Go Long
Summary: This article provides a technical analysis of Tesla Inc. (TSLA) to identify optimal times for going long. It analyzes various technical indicators like moving averages, price channels, and the Average Directional Index (ADX), along with broader market indicators, to build a long-term bullish bias for TSLA. The report suggests strategies for entering a long position, including aggressive and conservative approaches.

Title: Tesla’s Mad Scramble to Meet Production Deadline Is Coming to an End
Summary: Tesla is nearing the end of another challenging quarter for its Model 3 rollout, aiming to meet its self-imposed production target of 5,000 cars per week by the end of June. Investors are keenly awaiting production figures to assess how many cars Tesla manufactured, sold, and stockpiled, and the final weekly production rate achieved. Analysts offer varied outlooks on Tesla's prospects, focusing on Model 3 deliveries, production rates, and the impact of the expiring U.S. electric vehicle tax credit.

Title: Tesla Reaches Production Goal for Making 5,000 Model 3s
Summary: Tesla Inc. has reached its long-delayed production goal of manufacturing 5,000 Model 3 sedans in about a single week, a target confirmed by CEO Elon Musk in a memo to employees. This achievement aims to alleviate scrutiny on the unprofitable automaker and marks a significant step in its efforts to become a mainstream electric vehicle provider. Workers at the Fremont, California, factory celebrated this milestone after working long shifts to meet the intensive production demands.

Title: Musk says Tesla pushed out 7,000 cars last week, meeting goal of 5,000 Model 3s
Summary: Tesla announced it produced 7,000 cars last week, successfully meeting its self-imposed goal of manufacturing 5,000 Model 3s before the close of the second quarter. This achievement, despite production hurdles and a reliance on manual labor, comes as the company faces investor scrutiny over its ability to sustain high production rates and profitability. The news could positively impact Tesla's stock as the company aims to prove its mass production capabilities.

Title: Exclusive: Tesla hits Model 3 manufacturing milestone, hours after deadline - factory sources
Summary: Tesla Inc nearly achieved its goal of producing 5,000 Model 3 electric sedans in the last week of its second quarter, hitting the milestone hours after CEO Elon Musk's deadline. Despite the tight deadline and previous production issues, the company also reached its production goal of 7,000 Model S and Model X vehicles in a week, and expects to produce 6,000 Model 3 sedans a week "next month." This achievement is crucial for the money-losing company as it aims to prove its mass production capabilities and sustain investor confidence.

Title: Vistra, Tesla and PG&E seeking world’s first 1 GWh+ batteries
Summary: PG&E is seeking regulatory approval for four energy storage projects in California totaling 567 MW / 2.27 GWh, including systems from Vistra Energy and Tesla that would be among the world's largest. The Vistra Energy project is 300 MW / 1200 MWh, while Tesla's project is 182.5 MW / 730 MWh with an option to expand to 1095 MWh, potentially confirming Elon Musk's reference to a 1 GW battery. These developments indicate a significant move towards larger battery storage solutions on the global electric grid.

Title: CEO Musk: Tesla reaches goal of making 5,000 Models 3s
Summary: Tesla Inc. announced it met CEO Elon Musk's goal of producing 5,000 Model 3s per week by the end of June, a critical milestone for the electric car maker. Musk celebrated the achievement but market analysts expressed caution, emphasizing the need for consistent production and resolution of financial and potential safety issues. The company faces challenges including never having posted a full-year profit, burning through over $1 billion in cash in the first quarter, and addressing a backlog of 450,000 orders.

Title: Shouting CEO, Changing Rules: Inside Tesla's Model 3-building Sprint
Summary: Tesla pushed hard in the final week of June to meet its goal of producing 5,000 Model 3s in a week, with CEO Elon Musk actively involved on the assembly line. This intense effort included mandatory weekend shifts, a new temporary assembly line, and pulling workers from Model S and X production, which led to concerns about employee burnout and the impact on other vehicle lines. Despite some investor skepticism regarding the sustainability of this pace, Tesla achieved its milestone, though questions remain about long-term production methods and employee welfare.
Source: VOA - Voice of America English News

Title: Even Tesla Inc (TSLA) Bulls Are Getting Uncomfortable
Summary: Tesla Inc. (TSLA) stock dropped 9.3 percent after reporting disappointing Q2 production numbers, missing analyst expectations. Analysts are questioning the sustainability of Model 3 production and Tesla's ability to achieve profitability amidst reports of mandatory weekend shifts and discontinuation of brake-and-roll testing. Concerns about Tesla's financial situation persist, with some analysts believing the company will need to raise capital again despite claims to the contrary.

Title: Tesla goes big in China with Shanghai plant
Summary: Tesla Inc. CEO Elon Musk secured a deal to build its first factory outside the U.S. in Shanghai, China, which is expected to double the electric car maker's global manufacturing capacity. This move comes as China pushes to attract more investment in advanced electric vehicle technology and despite new tariffs imposed by China on U.S.-made vehicles. The Shanghai plant aims to produce up to 500,000 vehicles annually, significantly boosting Tesla's presence in the world's largest EV market.

Title: Tesla whistleblower retains law firm famous for winning $22.5 million Monsanto suit
Summary: Tesla technician Martin Tripp, accused of sabotage by CEO Elon Musk, has filed a formal whistleblower complaint with the SEC and retained Meissner Associates, a law firm known for winning a $22.5 million Monsanto lawsuit. Tripp alleges that Tesla made material omissions and misstatements to investors, potentially compromising customer safety by overstating Model 3 production, using defective parts, and lowering vehicle specifications. Tesla has characterized Tripp as a disgruntled former employee seeking to harm the company.

Title: Tesla Got 7,000 New Orders Last Week: Elon Musk
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk publicly revealed the company's order book statistics, indicating 7,000 new net orders last week, including 5,000 for the Model 3 and over 2,000 for the Model S and X. This disclosure appears to be an effort to counter recent criticisms and downgrades from analysts regarding Model 3 demand and cancellation rates. The move is unusual as Tesla typically reports such numbers quarterly.

Title: Elon Musk Says Tesla May Go Private, and Its Stock Soars (Published 2018)
Summary: Elon Musk announced via Twitter that he was considering taking Tesla private at $420 per share, claiming "Funding secured." This cryptic declaration led to a frenzy in the stock market, especially after Tesla's stock had already risen due to reports of a sizable Saudi Arabian stake in the company. Investors were left to decipher the implications of Musk's tweet and its relationship to other news.

Title: Tesla CEO Drops Latest Bombshell With $72B Buyout Proposal
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced on Twitter his consideration of taking the electric car company private at $420 per share, estimating a buyout value of nearly $72 billion. This move would end Tesla's eight-year history as a publicly traded company and potentially allow it to focus on long-term goals away from quarterly investor scrutiny. The announcement came amid reports of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund building a stake in Tesla and raised questions due to Musk's controversial past tweets.
Source: VOA - Voice of America English News

Title: Elon Musk Tweets He Is Considering Taking Tesla Private
Summary: Elon Musk announced via Twitter that he is considering taking Tesla private at $420 a share, claiming that funding for the deal is secured. This potential move could represent the largest buyout in history, valuing the electric-car maker at over $70 billion. The announcement caused a jolt in financial markets.

Title: Elon Musk says he wants to take Tesla private at over $70 billion — here’s what that means
Summary: Elon Musk announced his intention to take Tesla private at a valuation of $70 billion, offering $420 per share, a premium of about 20% over recent stock prices. This move aims to free Tesla from the pressures of quarterly earnings cycles and public market scrutiny, which Musk believes distract from long-term strategy. The plan, though requiring shareholder approval and facing potential SEC scrutiny, reflects a growing trend among CEOs to privatize companies to focus on long-term goals without short-term market pressures.

Title: Tesla’s stock price falls, wiping out Elon Musk’s tweet-fueled rally in just two days
Summary: Tesla's stock price fell, wiping out gains from Elon Musk's tweet about taking the company private, as doubts mounted about the funding and feasibility of the $82-billion valuation. The SEC is reportedly examining whether Musk's tweet was factual, while financial institutions and large shareholders indicate they were not aware of secured financing.

Title: Saudi Interest in Tesla Could Help 'KSA' ETF
Summary: Elon Musk's consideration of taking Tesla private has drawn interest from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund.
