Title: Arent Fox Helps Tesla Bring Tesla Tequila to Market
Summary: Arent Fox advised Tesla on the legal aspects of launching its own brand of liquor, "Tesla Tequila," which sold out almost instantly. The product is described as a premium 100% agave añejo tequila aged in French oak barrels, packaged in a distinctive lightning bolt-shaped bottle. The Arent Fox team, led by Anthony V. Lupo, included Steven A. Cohen, Luna M. Samman, Michael T. Kelly, and Dan Jasnow.

Title: Can the Chinese-Built Xpeng P7 Hold Its Own on American Soil?
Summary: The article discusses the Xpeng P7, an all-electric sedan from China's Xpeng, and its potential entry into the American market. A test drive by InsideEVs suggests the car offers a premium interior and comfort-tuned performance that could rival Tesla models, especially given its competitive pricing. The Xpeng P7 is available with two drivetrain configurations, including a Performance model with 430 horsepower and a Super Long Range version offering over 430 miles per charge.

Title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk says he may have COVID-19
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced on November 13, 2020, that he believes he has contracted COVID-19. He reported experiencing symptoms similar to a common cold, including a "mild sniffles & cough & slight fever & aches." This news comes as the pandemic continued to affect global economies and public health.

Title: My Top 2 Battery Metal Miners For Lithium, Cobalt, Nickel; 1 For Graphite And Manganese
Summary: This article discusses the impending super-cycle for battery metal miners, driven by rapidly increasing EV sales and Tesla's aggressive battery production forecasts. The author identifies their top two preferred miners for lithium, cobalt, and nickel, and one each for graphite and manganese, based on quality and growth potential. The piece highlights predictions of an 86x increase in global battery production by 2030, necessitating a significant surge in demand for these key metals.

Title: |Tesla to Join S&P 500 Next Month as Largest-Ever New Member
Summary: |Tesla Inc. (TSLA) is set to join the S&P 500 index on December 21, becoming the largest company ever added to the gauge. This announcement follows months of speculation and a significant rally in the stock this year, elevating the electric vehicle pioneer's market value to nearly $390 billion. Tesla's inclusion is expected to greatly broaden its investor base and make it one of the index's most influential constituents.

Title: Tesla shares up 12 percent as automaker zooms to join S&P 500
Summary: Tesla Inc. is set to join the S&P 500 in December, triggering a massive $51 billion trade as index funds are forced to buy the electric car maker’s shares. The company's shares surged 12 percent after the announcement, marking a significant win for CEO Elon Musk and its shareholders. Tesla's inclusion will make it one of the largest weight additions to the S&P 500 in the last decade, with a market capitalization over $380 billion.

Title: Tesla to join the S&P 500 in December
Summary: Tesla's shares surged by over 10% after S&P Dow Jones Indices announced the electric car company would be added to the S&P 500 stock index. The inclusion is effective from December 21, and Tesla is expected to be one of the largest additions by market capitalization in the last decade. This follows a previous snub and comes after Tesla reported its fifth consecutive quarter of profit.

Title: Tesla to join S&P 500, spark epic index fund trade
Summary: Tesla Inc (TSLA.O) is set to join the S&P 500 in December, a decision that caused its shares to jump 14% and will trigger an estimated $51 billion trade by index funds. With a stock market value over $400 billion, Tesla will be one of the largest additions to the index in the last decade, requiring index funds to adjust their portfolios significantly. The inclusion comes despite concerns from some investors about Tesla's high valuation and corporate governance.

Title: Tesla Added to the S&P 500
Summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices announced that Tesla would be added to the S&P 500 prior to the market open on Monday, December 21, 2020. This article discusses the S&P 500's methodology, the significance of Tesla's inclusion, and its potential impact on the market, noting that Tesla's float market capitalization of USD 304 billion would make it the largest S&P 500 addition ever. The addition is expected to increase the weight of the Consumer Discretionary sector in the index and potentially reduce the sector's sensitivity to Amazon.

Title: U.S. upgrades safety probe into nearly 159,000 Tesla vehicles
Summary: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has expanded its safety probe into approximately 159,000 Tesla Model S and Model X vehicles, upgrading it to an engineering analysis. This investigation concerns touchscreen failures that can lead to loss of rear-camera display, impact defogging, and affect driver assistance system chimes. NHTSA reported that failure rates exceeded 30% in some vehicles, prompting Tesla to issue over-the-air updates to mitigate the issues.

Title: GM went public 10 years ago, and it’s been a mediocre investment — here’s how it can improve for the next 10
Summary: General Motors' stock performance over the past decade has been "mediocre" with a 5.2% annualized total return, significantly underperforming the S&P 500. Despite a sound balance sheet and consistently beating earnings expectations, GM's market value trails competitors like Tesla due to investor perception. The company is now hoping investments in electric vehicles (EVs) and autonomous technology will re-rate its stock and lead to stronger performance in the next 10 years.

Title: What’s the Most Reliable New-Car Brand for 2020?
Summary: Consumer Reports released its 2020 Auto Reliability Survey, naming Mazda as the most reliable new-car brand for the first time, surpassing perennial leaders Toyota and Lexus. Lincoln ranked last, primarily due to issues with its new Aviator and Corsair SUVs. Tesla also performed poorly, ranking second from the bottom due to quality issues with its Model Y.

Title: Why climate change is getting the attention of world's wealthy investors
Summary: Wealthy investors are increasingly focusing on climate change as a fundamental investment theme, driven by significant economic opportunities rather than political beliefs. Billionaires like Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk are leading the way, but this trend is also widespread among ultra-wealthy investors who see renewables becoming cheaper and creating vast capital investment opportunities. Despite concerns about short-term political uncertainties or the intermittency of renewable energy, experts believe the investment case for green technologies and addressing climate risk in portfolios remains strong, with potential for comparable performance to traditional investments.

Title: GM is increasing spending to $27 billion to make 40% of its cars electric by 2025
Summary: General Motors announced a significant increase in its electric vehicle (EV) spending to $27 billion through 2025, aiming to have 40% of its US models be electric by that year. The company is accelerating development and production of EVs, including the Cadillac Lyriq, and expects second-generation Ultium batteries to be cheaper and more efficient. This push is driven by regulatory pressure, competition from EV startups like Tesla, Lucid, and Fisker, and internal engineering progress.

Title: General Motors launches into auto insurance
Summary: General Motors (GM) has launched its own insurance unit, OnStar Insurance, which uses telematics data from OnStar-equipped vehicles to offer personalized premiums based on driving habits. The new service, along with OnStar Insurance Services, aims to provide comprehensive automobile security and will initially pilot in Arizona with GM employees before expanding to the public in early 2021. This move positions GM as a disruptor in the auto insurance industry, similar to Tesla.

Title: G.M. Accelerates Its Ambitions for Electric Vehicles (Published 2020)
Summary: General Motors announced an accelerated push into electric vehicles, significantly increasing its investment to $27 billion by 2025 and planning to introduce 30 electric models globally by that year. This strategic shift aims to challenge Tesla's dominance in the EV market and attract investors. Mary T. Barra, G.M.'s chief executive, emphasized that EVs are central to the company's growth and shareholder value.

Title: These 11 EV Startups Are Chasing Tesla. They Can’t All Win.
Summary: A field of electric-vehicle (EV) startups are attempting to emulate Tesla's success, fueled by significant Wall Street funding. However, the path ahead is fraught with challenges, as most haven't yet successfully built or sold cars profitably, face accusations of fraud, or are still building their workforce. Their ultimate success depends on consumer acceptance, strategic market focus, and the ability to compete with established automotive giants like General Motors.

Title: LG Chem beats CATL, Panasonic to supply batteries for Tesla’s Model Y SUV
Summary: LG Chem will supply batteries for Tesla's Model Y SUV to be manufactured in China, beating competitors CATL and Panasonic. This marks LG Chem's second contract with Tesla and reinforces its technological edge in high-end NCM batteries. The deal is expected to significantly boost LG Chem's market presence in China.

Title: Chinese EV rivals line up to challenge Tesla on their home turf
Summary: Chinese electric vehicle (EV) companies Nio and Xpeng have reported strong earnings, challenging Tesla in the world's largest EV market. While some analysts question their high valuations compared to Tesla, the immense growth potential in China suggests enough market share for multiple players. GM is also significantly increasing its investment in EVs, signaling a competitive future in the global electric vehicle industry.

Title: Tesla’s Mission: Accelerating World’s Transition to Sustainable Energy
Summary: This article delves into Tesla's mission of accelerating the world's transition to sustainable energy, examining Elon Musk's vision and the company's disruptive impact across various sectors. It analyzes Tesla's strategy, including its focus on R&D for EVs, energy, batteries, AI, and software, highlighting how these elements create a competitive ecosystem. The piece also discusses Musk's controversial public persona and its role in Tesla's marketing and stock market performance.

Title: Tesla market value crosses $500 billion in meteoric rally
Summary: Tesla Inc. has surpassed a market value of $500 billion, driven by investor enthusiasm ahead of its S&P 500 debut and a more than 500% surge this year. The electric carmaker's stock rose nearly 5%, making it Wall Street's seventh most valuable company, with index funds and actively managed funds expected to buy billions more in shares. This rally highlights the growing investor confidence in EV manufacturers, also boosted by President-elect Joe Biden's focus on clean energy.

Title: Tesla's upcoming S&P 500 debut fuels 'crazy' trading volume
Summary: Tesla's upcoming inclusion in the S&P 500 in December has led to a significant surge in its stock price and "crazy" trading volume. Investors, including institutional managers and retail traders, are buying shares ahead of index funds that will be forced to acquire over $50 billion worth of Tesla stock. This has made Tesla one of the most heavily traded companies on U.S. exchanges, surpassing Amazon and Apple combined in recent sessions.

Title: Tesla issues two recalls covering 9,500 U.S. vehicles - NHTSA
Summary: Tesla Inc. is issuing two recalls affecting approximately 9,500 vehicles. One recall concerns 9,136 Model X cars from 2016 for roof trim that may separate, while the other involves 401 2020 Model Y vehicles due to improperly tightened bolts connecting the front upper control arm. The company states it is unaware of any accidents or injuries related to these issues.

Title: Tesla zooms past Buffett's Berkshire to become 6th-largest US company
Summary: Tesla's market capitalization surged to $555.24 billion, surpassing Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway to become the sixth-largest U.S. company. This rapid increase was driven by news of its inclusion in the S&P 500 and a 600% gain in share price this year. Analysts have raised price targets for Tesla, citing strong demand and the potential for increased vehicle deliveries.

Title: Tesla isn't dominating the electric bike market, but here are the players that might
Summary: While Tesla dominates the electric vehicle market, Elon Musk has not pursued electric motorcycles and scooters. However, traditional motorcycle manufacturers like Harley-Davidson, Honda, and startups like Zero Motorcycles and NIU Technologies are making significant strides in the growing electric two-wheeler market, which is projected to reach $40 billion by 2026. The article highlights key players, market trends, and challenges in this evolving segment, including Harley's push into electric bicycles and NIU's success in smart scooters.

Title: Nikola Badger EV Truck Dead as Company Scales down GM Plans
Summary: Nikola's electric pickup, the Badger, has been canceled after General Motors withdrew its equity stake and development plans for the truck. Nikola will refund all deposits for the Badger and will now primarily focus on developing its electric and hydrogen fuel-cell semi-trucks, collaborating with GM on its Hydrotec fuel-cell and Ultium drivetrain technologies for these models. The company's stock experienced a significant drop following the announcement.

Title: Companies that support LGBTQ-inclusive policies outperform: Credit Suisse
Summary: A Credit Suisse analysis highlights that companies supporting LGBTQ-inclusive policies have historically outperformed the broader market. These firms, including Apple and Tesla, attract and retain talent more easily, and show stronger revenue growth and cash flow. While not proving causation, the report indicates a strong correlation between LGBTQ inclusivity and better financial performance.

Title: Mississippi Power plans ‘smart neighborhood’ with Tesla Solar Roofs
Summary: Mississippi Power, an affiliate of Southern Company, is partnering with Tesla to build the world's first smart neighborhood featuring Tesla Solar Roofs. The initial phase in Lauderdale County will include about 45 homes, expanding to 150, which will also incorporate Tesla Powerwall batteries and other smart home technologies. This project will serve as a research and development pilot to study the performance of solar roofs and their impact on the grid and energy consumption in southern Mississippi.

Title: Portland and Daimler team up for 5MW electric semi public charging ‘Island’
Summary: Portland General Electric (PGE) and Daimler Trucks North America (DTNA) are co-developing "Electric Island," a large public charging site for medium- and heavy-duty electric trucks near DTNA's headquarters in Portland, Oregon. This 5MW charging island, expected to be the first of its kind in the US, will initially feature nine charging stations with up to 1MW charging levels by spring 2021. The initiative aims to accelerate the development and deployment of electric commercial vehicles, amid increasing activity in the electric truck sector from companies like Tesla and Kenworth.

Title: Ex-Tesla employee agrees to pay $400K over claims he stole trade secrets
Summary: A former Tesla Inc. employee, Martin Tripp, has agreed to pay Tesla $400,000 to settle a lawsuit claiming he stole trade secrets. Tripp also acknowledged that his counterclaims against Tesla were funded by short seller Cable Car Capital LLC. The settlement includes an additional $25,000 payment for violating a protective order and an agreement to destroy all acquired documents.

Title: LG Chem to double China battery capacity to meet Tesla demand: Reuters, citing sources
Summary: South Korea's LG Chem plans to more than double its battery cell production capacity in China to supply Tesla's growing demand for electric vehicles. This expansion will support Tesla's Shanghai-built Model 3 and future Model Y vehicles, with increased output also shipping to Tesla factories in Germany and the United States. The move comes as Tesla aggressively expands global production and seeks to secure sufficient battery cell supplies from its key partners like LG Chem, Panasonic, and CATL.

Title: Exclusive: LG Chem to double China battery capacity to meet Tesla demand -sources
Summary: South Korea's LG Chem plans to more than double the production capacity of battery cells at its China plant, primarily to meet the growing demand from Tesla Inc. This expansion signifies LG Chem's increased role in Tesla's global supply chain, with cells from China and Korea also destined for Tesla factories in Germany and the United States. The move comes as Tesla aggressively expands production and seeks to secure sufficient battery supplies from its partners.

Title: Former Tesla employee to pay $400,000 to end lawsuit over tips to reporters
Summary: A former Tesla employee, Martin Tripp, has agreed to pay Tesla Inc. $400,000 to settle a lawsuit in which the company accused him of leaking trade secrets and making false claims to reporters. Tripp had previously characterized himself as a whistleblower exposing production inefficiencies, but the settlement states he did not contest Tesla's claims of trade secret theft. His counterclaims against Tesla were reportedly funded by a short seller of Tesla stock.

Title: Elon Musk says Tesla would consider merger with rival automaker
Summary: Elon Musk stated that Tesla would consider a merger with a rival automaker, but he would not initiate a hostile takeover. Despite Tesla's high market capitalization, Musk emphasized that any such relationship would need to be mutually acceptable. He noted that other companies, like Daimler and Toyota, had previously held stakes in Tesla.

Title: “Stocks only go up, $TSLA to the moon” — Elon Musk (probably)
Summary: This article discusses the psychological biases that influence stock trading, using Tesla ($TSLA) as an example. It highlights how cognitive pitfalls like hindsight bias and self-attribution bias lead even professional traders to make irrational decisions and overestimate their abilities. The author questions the implications of easy access to financial markets for the general public, given these inherent human biases.

Title: Is Elon Musk moving to Texas? A new rumor says so.
Summary: A rumor circulating on Friday, December 4, 2020, suggested that Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and founder of SpaceX, might be moving to Texas. While not confirmed by Musk himself, the report cited close friends and associates. Musk's companies, SpaceX and Tesla, have a significant and growing presence in Texas, with SpaceX operating a test site in McGregor and a launch facility in Boca Chica, and Tesla building a Gigafactory near Austin.

Title: Tesla publishes its first-ever diversity report revealing leadership is 83% male and 59% White
Summary: Tesla released its first diversity report showing that its U.S. workforce is a "majority minority," but leadership roles (director level and higher) are 83% male and 59% White. The report outlines demographic breakdowns for various groups in the workforce, leadership, new hires, and promotions. Tesla plans to recruit from historically Black colleges and universities and implement unconscious bias training for managers and recruiters to improve diversity.

Title: Tesla says Black people hold just 4% of its U.S. leadership roles
Summary: Tesla's first U.S. diversity report reveals that Black employees constitute only 4% of its American leadership roles and 10% of its total U.S. workforce. Women hold 17% of leadership roles and 21% of the overall workforce. The company acknowledged the lack of representation and committed to increasing diversity, including recruiting at Historically Black Colleges and Universities.

Title: Tesla announces second $5bn share sale in three months
Summary: Tesla announced its second $5 billion capital raise in three months, capitalizing on a significant rally in its shares this year, which pushed its market value above $600 billion. The move comes as demand for Tesla shares is fueled by its upcoming inclusion in the S&P 500 index, despite some analysts warning about a potential stock bubble. This capital raise aims to support the company's expansion plans, including new factories and vehicle lines.

Title: Apple, TSMC rumored to be working on chips for a Tesla-like 'Apple Car'
Summary: Apple is reportedly collaborating with TSMC to develop chips for its rumored "Apple Car," which is said to be similar to a Tesla. The companies are purportedly planning a U.S. factory for these chips, though DigiTimes, the source of this information, has a mixed track record. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo previously forecast an "Apple Car" debut between 2023 and 2025, possibly sourcing chips from TSMC.

Title: Ford Explores Making Its Own Electric Vehicle Battery Cells
Summary: Ford Motor Co. is evaluating whether to begin manufacturing its own electric vehicle battery cells, a significant shift from its current strategy of purchasing them from suppliers. While the company has historically relied on external suppliers for flexibility, CEO Jim Farley suggests that internal production could address capacity limitations and provide control over the supply chain. This potential move aligns Ford with rivals like GM and Tesla, who have invested in battery cell production, and reflects the growing commitment to EV investments and the anticipated surge in EV adoption.

Title: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: Tesla, Nio, Airbnb, Disney & more
Summary: This article details the midday stock movements of several notable companies on December 11, 2020. Key movements include Snowflake and Nio sliding after downgrades and a new share offering, respectively, while Disney soared due to projections for its streaming service. Other companies like Airbnb, Tesla, Qualcomm, UPS, Vail Resorts, Lululemon, and American Airlines also experienced significant shifts, driven by analyst ratings, earnings reports, or industry news.

Title: Oracle is the latest Silicon Valley company to head for the hills — of Austin
Summary: Oracle Corp. announced its decision to move its corporate headquarters from Redwood City, California, to Austin, Texas, following a trend of companies and executives relocating from Silicon Valley. This move aligns with a new flexible employee work location policy and positions Oracle for growth in a business-friendly state. Governor Greg Abbott lauded the relocation, emphasizing Texas's appeal for business, jobs, and opportunity, with other tech giants like Tesla and HP Enterprise also making similar moves or expanding in the state.

Title: Oracle is moving its headquarters from Silicon Valley to Austin, Texas
Summary: Oracle announced it is moving its headquarters from Redwood City, California, to Austin, Texas, becoming the latest tech company to relocate out of Silicon Valley. This move is part of a new flexible employee work location policy, allowing personnel more flexibility in where and how they work. Other tech companies like Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Palantir Technologies, as well as Elon Musk, have also moved or announced moves out of California.

Title: Oracle moving from California to Texas, joins Tesla, Hewlett Packard
Summary: Oracle has announced it is moving its corporate headquarters from California to Austin, Texas, following similar moves by Tesla and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. The company cited a new flexible employee work location policy and the belief that the move best positions Oracle for growth and offers more flexibility for its personnel. This trend suggests a growing disillusionment among corporations with California's business environment.

Title: Which 2021 Vehicles Have the Best Warranty Coverage?
Summary: This article analyzes and compares the new-car warranty coverage for 2021 model year vehicles across various brands, categorizing them into "Best Policies," "Very Good," "Better Than Average," and "The Rest." It details the bumper-to-bumper, powertrain, and roadside assistance coverage, including special provisions for hybrid and electric vehicles, and offers critical notes for potential buyers regarding transferability and other exclusions.

Title: Oracle joins Tesla founder Elon Musk and Hewlett Packard in relocating to Texas
Summary: Tech giant Oracle announced its headquarters are moving from Silicon Valley to Austin, Texas, following similar moves by Tesla's Elon Musk and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. This relocation is part of a growing exodus of companies from high-cost California to Texas, driven by factors like lower cost of living, no state income tax, and clashes with California officials over COVID-19 restrictions. Texas Governor Greg Abbott welcomed the announcement, highlighting the state's attractiveness for business and opportunity.

Title: Even More Tech Firms Are Leaving Silicon Valley for Texas
Summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is relocating its headquarters from Silicon Valley to Houston, Texas, following a trend of tech firms moving to states with more favorable business climates and lower costs. The article highlights that Texas offers significant financial advantages, such as no state income tax, lower housing costs, and a better business tax climate compared to California, attracting both companies and individuals like Elon Musk. This shift is prompting speculation that other major tech companies, such as Tesla, might follow suit, further solidifying Texas as an emerging tech hub.

Title: Oracle moving its HQ from California to Texas, like HP Enterprise, Tesla CEO
Summary: Oracle Corp. is moving its headquarters from Redwood City, California, to Austin, Texas, becoming the latest tech giant to leave Silicon Valley. The company cited a more flexible employee work location policy and positioning for growth as reasons for the move. This follows similar relocations by HP Enterprise and Tesla CEO Elon Musk to Texas, and Palantir Technologies to Denver, highlighting a trend of companies exiting California.

Title: Oracle to move HQ from Silicon Valley to Texas, but Ellison says aloha
Summary: Oracle Corporation is relocating its corporate headquarters from Silicon Valley to Austin, Texas, to offer employees more flexibility regarding their work location and arrangements. Despite this move, founder Larry Ellison has personally moved to Hawaii and will work remotely from there. This decision aligns with a broader trend of tech companies rethinking traditional office setups and relocating operations, with other prominent figures like Elon Musk also moving to Texas.

Title: How the ARKQ ETF Is All In for the 4th Industrial Revolution
Summary: The ARKQ ETF is positioned to capitalize on the fourth industrial revolution, driven by advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics. This actively managed fund invests in companies involved in autonomous vehicles, 3D printing, energy storage, and robotics. ARKQ's focus on these durable and early-stage disruptive technologies, including exposure to companies like Tesla, makes it a key investment vehicle for investors seeking to participate in AI-driven growth.

Title: Who is Li Xiang, the billionaire behind China’s Tesla rival Li Auto?
Summary: Li Xiang, the founder and CEO of Li Auto, has become a billionaire through his electric vehicle company, which is seen as a rival to Tesla in China. Xiang started his entrepreneurial journey at 18 with PCPop.com, then founded Autohome, a successful online car platform, before establishing Li Auto with a vision for exceptional electric vehicles. His third venture, Li Auto, recently listed on Nasdaq, raising significant capital.

Title: Rivian R1T is on its way to take on Tesla Cybertruck and Hummer EV
Summary: The article discusses the anticipated launch of the Rivian R1T electric pickup truck, highlighting its potential to beat competitors like the Tesla Cybertruck and Hummer EV to market. It details the R1T's specifications, Rivian's significant investments and future ambitions, and the growing market for electric trucks in the U.S.

Title: Bill Ford: ‘Our Family Name Is on the Line Every Day’ (Published 2020)
Summary: Bill Ford, chairman of Ford Motor Company and great-grandson of Henry Ford, discusses the challenges facing the auto industry, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the rise of electric vehicles. He highlights Ford's response to these issues, such as temporarily halting production and developing electric models. Despite intense competition, particularly from Tesla, Ford expresses optimism about the future, emphasizing new electric vehicle introductions and a partnership with Volkswagen for self-driving cars.

Title: Tesla shares jump to record high ahead of S&P 500 debut
Summary: Shares of Tesla Inc. surged to a record high on Friday, driven by anticipation of its inclusion in the S&P 500 index. The electric carmaker, led by Elon Musk, will become the most valuable company ever admitted to the benchmark, accounting for over 1% of its value. This event prompted index-tracking funds to buy an estimated $85 billion worth of Tesla shares, influencing significant trading volume and price movements.

Title: Tesla's Elon Musk asks about converting "large transactions" to bitcoin
Summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla, inquired on Twitter about the feasibility of converting significant portions of Tesla's balance sheet into Bitcoin. This query came in response to MicroStrategy CEO Michael Saylor's suggestion that such a move could greatly benefit Tesla shareholders, leading to an exchange where Saylor offered to share his experience with large Bitcoin purchases. The discussion coincided with Bitcoin's recent surge past $20,000 and Tesla's upcoming entry into the S&P 500 index.

Title: The secret Tesla reveals about index investing
Summary: Tesla's delayed inclusion in the S&P 500 Index, despite its early market capitalization, highlights a critical difference in index construction: objective, market-cap based selection versus subjective, committee-driven choices. Founder Chuck Schwab argues for transparent, rules-based indexes like the Schwab 1000 Index that prioritize market wisdom to better capture fast-growing companies earlier. The article emphasizes that how one chooses to "buy the market" via an index significantly impacts investment outcomes.

Title: Tesla stock slides on first day in S&P 500
Summary: Tesla's shares fell over 6% on its first day in the S&P 500, influenced by concerns about a new Covid-19 variant, disappointment over a stimulus deal, and news of Apple's self-driving car plans. The drop followed a significant pre-inclusion surge, with analysts noting similar post-inclusion declines for other high-profile S&P 500 additions. Analysts also voiced concerns about the stock's valuation and increasing competition in the EV market.

Title: A Backdoor Electric Vehicle Play with Tesla Entering the S&P 500
Summary: This article highlights the ALPS Disruptive Technologies ETF (DTEC) as a "backdoor" investment opportunity in the electric vehicle (EV) space, particularly with Tesla joining the S&P 500. DTEC provides exposure to energy storage and smart grid technologies, which are crucial for the burgeoning EV landscape. The ETF offers leverage to the EV theme through its clean energy and smart grid components, presenting a long-term growth opportunity as these technologies are increasingly integrated.

Title: Honda recalls over 700,000 vehicles because of possible BCM Software Malfunction
Summary: Honda is recalling over 700,000 Accord, Accord Hybrid, and Insight vehicles from model years 2018-2020 due to a software error in the Body Control Module (BCM). This malfunction can cause disruptions in essential systems like windshield wipers, defrosters, rearview cameras, and exterior lights, increasing the risk of a crash. Honda will update the BCM software free of charge, with the recall expected to begin in January 2021.

Title: Tesla Is Worth More Than All Big Car Companies in the World Combined
Summary: Tesla's market capitalization has surged to $615 billion, exceeding the combined value of the world's seven largest automakers, despite having significantly lower revenue. This valuation disconnect is attributed to some investors viewing Tesla as a technology company rather than just an automaker, envisioning an Apple-like ecosystem for its products. The company is expected to "grow into" its valuation not by volume but by enhancing the customer experience.

Title: Apple en route to face-off with Tesla
Summary: Apple is reportedly accelerating its plans for an Apple-branded electric vehicle, potentially launching as early as next September or with a 2024 timeframe. This move positions Apple to directly challenge Tesla, leveraging its expertise in supply chain management and manufacturing. The article suggests that while Tesla excels in design, Apple's strength lies in consistent product delivery and manufacturing, indicating that the competition will ultimately be decided on the factory floor.

Title: The Soaring Stock Index You’ve Never Heard Of - WSJ
Summary: The article discusses the S&P Completion Index, a lesser-known stock index that significantly outperformed the S&P 500 largely due to Tesla's presence. Tesla, which was the biggest stock in the Completion Index, has now moved to the S&P 500, impacting the performance of both indices and related ETFs. This shift has already led to a decline in Tesla's stock and changes in the performance of funds tracking these indices.

Title: Elon Musk says had once reached out to Apple for acquiring Tesla
Summary: Elon Musk revealed he tried to discuss a potential acquisition of Tesla by Apple during Tesla's "darkest days of the Model 3 program," but Apple CEO Tim Cook refused the meeting. This happened as Apple is reportedly looking to produce a passenger vehicle by 2024 with new battery technology, which Musk commented on. Tesla has since overcome its production issues and recently joined the S&P 500.

Title: Future Vehicles - Ouster Tests Latest High-Tech LiDAR On New Subaru Outback
Summary: Ouster Inc., a U.S. startup specializing in LiDAR sensors for self-driving cars, is testing its latest high-tech LiDAR on a 2021 Subaru Outback. This technology, which uses laser light to create precise images of the surroundings, is seen as crucial for enabling higher levels of driver assistance and eventually full self-driving capabilities. Subaru aims for zero fatal accidents in its cars by 2030 and plans to integrate advanced driver-assist systems like its new EyeSight X, using a combination of cameras and radar, with LiDAR potentially playing a future role.

Title: Like Elon Musk, the BOSS ETF Knows Best
Summary: The Global X Founder-Run Companies ETF (BOSS) has achieved over 50% year-to-date gains, outperforming many investments, much like Elon Musk's companies. The ETF invests in U.S. companies led by their founders or co-founders, including Tesla among its top holdings, highlighting the success potential of founder-led businesses. This approach aims to capitalize on founders' long-term value creation and entrepreneurial drive for alpha potential.

Title: Like Tesla's Elon Musk, the BOSS ETF Knows Best
Summary: The article highlights the Global X Founder-Run Companies ETF (BOSS) and its strong performance, generating over 50% year-to-date gains. It explains that BOSS invests in companies where the founder or co-founder serves as CEO, citing Tesla as one of its top holdings. The ETF aims to provide exposure to U.S. mid- and large-cap companies led by their founders, offering potential alpha through long-term value creation and entrepreneurialism, while providing ETF efficiency.

Title: China's Yahua agrees five-year deal to supply lithium to Tesla
Summary: China's Sichuan Yahua Industrial Group Co Ltd has signed a five-year deal to supply battery-grade lithium hydroxide to Tesla, valuing the contract at $630-$880 million from 2021-2025. This agreement highlights Tesla's significant demand for lithium hydroxide, particularly with the ramp-up of Model Y production in Shanghai, and comes as Yahua had recently more than doubled its lithium hydroxide production capacity.

Title: Li Auto Crushes Delivery Guidance. The Chinese EV Sector Remains Hot.
Summary: Li Auto (LI) crushed its delivery guidance for 2020, delivering 14,464 vehicles in the fourth quarter and 32,624 for the full year. This strong performance, along with that of peers like Nio and Tesla, indicates that the Chinese electric vehicle sector remains robust entering 2021.

Title: Nio (NIO) ends 2020 on a high note with triple-digit growth in deliveries
Summary: Nio Inc. (NIO) reported strong triple-digit growth in vehicle deliveries for December, Q4, and the full year of 2020, exceeding its guidance and marking a robust end to the year. The company delivered 7,007 vehicles in December, 17,353 in Q4, and 43,728 for the full year, all showing significant year-over-year increases. Nio's shares rose 6% on Monday, having surged over 1,200% in the past year, as it continues to compete with Tesla.

Title: Chinese electric car company Nio doubles deliveries in 2020 as local competition ramps up for Tesla
Summary: Chinese electric vehicle startups Nio, Li Auto, and Xpeng significantly increased their deliveries in 2020, with Nio doubling its deliveries to 43,728 vehicles. Despite this growth, their combined sales are still a fraction of Tesla's global deliveries, which neared 500,000 in 2020. The Chinese government's support, including subsidies and infrastructure development, has fueled the surge in EV demand in the country, intensifying competition for Tesla in the world's largest auto market.

Title: Up 120% in 2020, Can the LIT Lithium ETF Hold Its Charge in 2021?
Summary: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) surged over 120% in 2020, driven by the growth in electric vehicle demand. With Tesla as a top holding and its supplier CATL expanding production, the article explores whether LIT can maintain its momentum in 2021. Technical indicators show the fund is overbought, but a MACD filter suggests a potential buying opportunity.

Title: Up 120% in 2020, Can the LIT Lithium ETF Hold Its Charge in 2021?
Summary: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) soared over 120% in 2020, driven by the booming electric vehicle market and the expansion plans of Tesla supplier Contemporary Amperex Technology Co Ltd (CATL). As demand for green energy vehicles increases, the article questions if LIT can maintain its strong performance in 2021, noting some technical indicators like RSI are in overbought territory while MACD suggests a buying opportunity.

Title: Rock star chip designer Jim Keller joins Tenstorrent
Summary: Legendary computer chip designer Jim Keller has joined Toronto startup Tenstorrent Inc. as its new president and chief technology officer. Keller, known for his work at AMD, Apple, and Tesla, will guide Tenstorrent in its mission to create a machine learning training chip that utilizes software to optimize computing power and increase efficiency, challenging established players like Intel, AMD, and Nvidia.

Title: Elon Musk overtakes Bezos to become world’s richest person
Summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, has surpassed Amazon's Jeff Bezos to become the world's richest person. His net worth reached $188.5 billion after a 4.8% rally in Tesla's shares on Thursday, just over $1.5 billion more than Bezos. This milestone caps a remarkable year for Musk, whose net worth soared by over $150 billion, largely due to Tesla's impressive 743% stock surge in the past year.

Title: Stock Option Volume ‘Exploded’ in 2020. What Comes Next.
Summary: In 2020, stock option volume saw a significant surge, largely driven by individual investors entering the market. These investors showed a strong preference for popular stocks such as Apple, Tesla, and NIO, a Chinese electric vehicle company. The article discusses this explosive growth in option trading and anticipates future trends.

Title: Tesla market value crosses $800 billion for the first time
Summary: Tesla's market capitalization surpassed $800 billion for the first time, driven by a 5.6% jump in its shares. This surge also propelled CEO Elon Musk past Jeff Bezos to become the world's wealthiest individual. The electric automaker's valuation now dwarfs the combined market caps of traditional Detroit automakers, despite its production being a fraction of larger rivals.

Title: Tesla market value crosses $800 billion for the first time
Summary: Tesla Inc.'s market capitalization surpassed $800 billion for the first time, driven by a significant jump in its stock price on Friday. This surge has also propelled CEO Elon Musk to become the world's richest man, surpassing Amazon's Jeff Bezos. The company's valuation now places it among Wall Street's most valuable firms, despite its production volume being a fraction of larger automotive rivals.

Title: These Hot Stocks Made This American Century's Best 2020 U.S. Diversified Stock Fund
Summary: The American Century Focused Dynamic Growth Fund (ACFSX) was the top-performing U.S. diversified stock fund in 2020, up 73.63% compared to the S&P 500's 18.40%. The fund achieved this success by investing in high-growth companies like Amazon, Facebook, Alphabet, Tesla, Square, DocuSign, Nike, Chipotle Mexican Grill, and Chegg, focusing on those with high sustainable growth rates and strong fundamentals, consistent with CAN SLIM principles. Its strong performance has earned it repeated IBD Best Mutual Funds Awards.

Title: Which Automaker Has the Best MPG Cars?
Summary: The EPA's annual Automotive Trends Report for 2020 analyzed which manufacturers produce the most fuel-efficient vehicles based on fleetwide fuel economy ratings for the 2019 model year and projections for 2020. Tesla significantly leads both years due to its all-electric lineup, while traditional automakers with truck and SUV-heavy lineups, such as the Detroit Three, rank at the bottom. The report highlights trends in fuel economy and how vehicle electrification is expected to increase these figures in the future.

Title: Carmaker Nio is 'well positioned' to capture a lot of China's electric vehicle market, analyst says
Summary: An analyst believes that Chinese carmaker Nio is well-positioned to secure a significant share of China's electric vehicle market, despite competition from Tesla. Nio recently unveiled its first sedan, the et7, featuring self-driving technology it claims surpasses Tesla's, and is establishing itself as a premium EV brand. While homegrown EV makers saw delivery surges, their numbers still trail Tesla's, the current market leader.

Title: World’s top maker of tiny motors has sights on Tesla as EVs gather pace
Summary: Nidec Corp., the leading supplier of motors globally, is aiming to become a key component provider for Tesla's electric vehicles. Nidec's president, Jun Seki, expressed a strong desire to collaborate with Elon Musk, stating that Tesla would not meet its 2030 production goals without external partnerships. This move highlights Nidec's confidence in its ability to produce EV components more cheaply and effectively than competitors.

Title: U.S. vehicle safety agency asks Tesla to recall 158,716 older vehicles over touchscreen glitches
Summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has requested Tesla recall 158,716 Model S and Model X vehicles produced before 2019 due to touchscreen failures. This issue, stemming from a memory device with a limited "write cycle" in the media control unit, can lead to the loss of safety-related features like rearview cameras and defrost systems. Failure rates are projected to increase with vehicle age, with all 2018 models expected to fail within 10 years.

Title: NHTSA urging Tesla to recall 158,000 cars for touchscreen safety defect
Summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is pressuring Tesla to recall 158,000 vehicles over concerns about faulty touchscreen displays in certain Model S and Model X cars. These failures can disable crucial safety features like backup cameras and defroster controls. NHTSA has given Tesla until January 27 to respond, threatening a public hearing if the automaker doesn't address the issue.

Title: Tesla (TSLA) launches its own solar power inverter
Summary: Tesla (TSLA) has launched its own solar power inverter, completing its home solar offering alongside the Powerwall and solar roof tiles. This move leverages Tesla's power electronics expertise to integrate its solar ecosystem further, offering models with 3.8 kW and 7.6 kW power outputs and 97.5% efficiency. The new inverter features Wi-Fi, Ethernet, cellular connectivity with over-the-air updates, and is designed to integrate with the Tesla Powerwall and app.

Title: Monterey Bay power plant now a record-breaking battery project to ward off blackouts
Summary: The former fossil fuel-burning power plant in Moss Landing, Monterey County, is being converted into a massive battery storage facility by Vistra Corp. This new project, expected to become the world's largest at 300 megawatts, will help California's energy grid by storing excess solar power and releasing it during peak demand, thereby mitigating the risk of blackouts. Alongside Vistra's project, PG&E and Tesla are also developing a substantial battery system at an adjacent substation, further contributing to grid reliability and the state's transition to cleaner energy.

Title: New Year, Same Story: Tesla and ARKK Still on Fire
Summary: The ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) continues its strong performance from the previous year, significantly driven by its substantial investment in Tesla (TSLA). Analyst Dan Ives recently increased his target price for Tesla, citing the company's continuous advancements in electric vehicle technology and its dominant position in the EV market. ARKK, now the largest actively managed ETF by assets, has already seen a nearly 14% gain early in 2021.

Title: Tesla launches a standalone solar inverter, challenging Enphase and SolarEdge for market share
Summary: Tesla has introduced its first standalone solar inverter, available in 3.8kW and 7.8kW capacities, featuring multiple maximum power point trackers. This move positions Tesla as a direct competitor to Enphase and SolarEdge in the inverter market, allowing the company more control over the cost of its solar systems and offering complete product verticality for solar installations.

Title: Tesla’s Advanced Battery Research group gets new leadership, Jeff Dahn to become advisor for Novonix
Summary: Professor Jeff Dahn, a renowned battery researcher who has had an exclusive partnership with Tesla since 2016 through Dalhousie University, is stepping down from his leadership role at Tesla’s Advanced Battery Research group. He will now serve as Chief Scientific Advisor at Novonix Battery Technology Solutions, a company spun out from his research group. Dahn and his team will continue working with Tesla, which has extended its contract with the Dalhousie University group until 2026, welcoming two new chairs to lead research into advanced Li-ion battery materials and performance.

Title: Tesla’s Autopilot Won’t Achieve Full Autonomy, Waymo CEO Says
Summary: The CEO of Waymo, John Krafcik, stated in an interview that Tesla's Autopilot will not achieve full autonomy, calling its development approach "misguided." He criticized the idea that a driver assistance system can magically evolve into a fully autonomous one and emphasized that Waymo does not consider Tesla a competitor in the driverless vehicle space, instead viewing their system as a "really good driver assistance system." This comes despite Tesla CEO Elon Musk's past claims about achieving full autonomy.

Title: Up 140%, the 'SMOG' ETF Is Literally Cleaning House
Summary: The VanEck Vectors Low Carbon Energy ETF (SMOG) has seen significant gains, up 140% in the last 12 months, driven largely by its holdings in electric car companies like Tesla and Nio. The fund invests in companies focused on alternative energy and related enabling technologies. The broader clean energy sector continues to surge, further supported by policy changes under the new Biden administration, which has rejoined the Paris Climate Agreement and pledged investments in renewable energy.

Title: Tesla's report could trigger $7 billion payout to Musk
Summary: Tesla's upcoming quarterly report could lead to a $7 billion options payout for CEO Elon Musk if the company's adjusted EBITDA reaches $2.3 billion, triggering the vesting of a fifth tranche from his 2018 pay package. Investors are also keenly awaiting Tesla's 2021 delivery target after the company's stock soared nearly 700% in the past year, making it the fifth-most-valuable publicly traded U.S. company. The company's market capitalization now stands at $843 billion, despite producing a fraction of the vehicles compared to traditional automakers.

Title: Baron Partners' Huge Tesla Stake Leads to Downgrade
Summary: Baron Partners fund has been downgraded to a Morningstar Analyst Rating of Neutral from Bronze due to its highly concentrated stake in Tesla, which grew to 47% of net assets. Despite lead manager Ron Baron selling some shares and reducing overall fund leverage, the stock's meteoric rise disproportionately influenced the fund's risk profile, highlighting lax risk controls. This concentration, while leading to significant returns in 2020, introduces substantial volatility and risk.

Title: Fort Lauderdale Tunnel Could Be ‘Game Changer' for Traffic Issues: Mayor
Summary: Fort Lauderdale Mayor Dean Trantalis believes a proposed three-mile tunnel under the New River, built by Elon Musk's The Boring Company, could be a "game changer" for the city's traffic issues and help establish South Florida as a tech hub. The project, estimated at a minimum of $10 million per mile, could also extend commuter lines to suburbs and beaches. The idea gained national attention after discussions between Musk and Miami Mayor Francis Suarez, with Trantalis planning further talks with Boring Company representatives to assess ground topography.

Title: AI fund that's beating S&P 500 has shifted into tech stocks
Summary: A machine-guided fund, the AI Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ), has significantly shifted its holdings into technology stocks, now comprising over 37% of its portfolio. This move comes as the fund continues to outperform the S&P 500 Index, having risen 12% this year compared to the S&P 500's nearly 3% gain. The fund has also halved its industrial exposure and doubled its position in Tesla Inc., while significantly reducing its Apple Inc. holdings.

Title: STMicroelectronics, Tesla and Apple: what happens when eMobility & 5G collide
Summary: This article examines how STMicroelectronics' Q4 2020 results were bolstered by its key relationships with Tesla in e-mobility and Apple in 5G mobile and consumer markets. It highlights STMicroelectronics' dominance in Silicon Carbide (SiC) for electric vehicles, largely driven by Tesla's adoption, and its significant role in CMOS image sensors for Apple's 3D imaging and sensing applications. The article also discusses the company's strategies to address capacity constraints and maintain its market position against competitors.

Title: GameStop stock market surge captures attention, enriches Michigan billionaire Donald Foss
Summary: The article details the significant surge in GameStop's stock price, highlighting how it substantially increased the wealth of Michigan billionaire Donald Foss, who held a 5.3% stake. It describes the phenomenon as a battle between day traders and Wall Street short sellers, driven by activity on Reddit, and notes the skepticism of financial analysts regarding the company's underlying fundamentals. The piece also mentions the broader market impact, the involvement of figures like Elon Musk, and warnings about the irrationality of the market.

Title: GM to only sell zero-emissions models by 2035
Summary: General Motors announced a bold pledge to make all its global operations and vehicles carbon neutral by 2040, including selling only zero-emission models by 2035. This move aligns with California's emission-reduction goals and places GM ahead of rivals like Ford in its carbon neutrality target. CEO Mary Barra's strategy aims to challenge Tesla's electric vehicle dominance and reshape GM's image, investing $27 billion into 30 electric vehicles by 2025.

Title: How Tesla made it to the top
Summary: Tesla, co-founded by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning, was initially conceived to build high-performance electric sports cars using lithium-ion batteries. Despite facing near-bankruptcy and production challenges, Elon Musk took over as CEO in 2008 and spearheaded its growth. The company differentiated itself by integrating its entire supply chain, avoiding traditional advertising, and aiming for a global transition to clean energy, ultimately becoming the world's most valuable car company, though it now faces increasing competition from other major automakers entering the EV market.

Title: GM’s all-EV plan could shake the energy industry
Summary: General Motors announced its plan to stop making gas-powered cars by 2035 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2040, a move expected to transform the electric vehicle market and energy industry. This significant commitment will necessitate dramatic changes to the electric grid and put GM in direct competition with Tesla. The shift also marks a major policy turnaround for GM, which previously sided with the Trump administration against stricter emissions standards.

Title: Chip shortage hits General Motors production
Summary: General Motors announced it will cut production at three North American factories and half capacity at one in South Korea due to a global semiconductor chip shortage. This comes as chipmaker Qualcomm also reported that supply constraints are hampering its sales growth. The shortage is impacting several other automakers, and projections suggest the issue could last into the third quarter of the year.

Title: Elon Musk admits Tesla has quality problems
Summary: Elon Musk has acknowledged Tesla's quality issues, particularly during new model production ramp-ups, confirming criticisms from engineering consultant Sandy Munro. Munro, who initially criticized the Model 3's quality in 2018, noted significant improvements in later production runs. Musk advised customers to either buy a Tesla at the very beginning of a model's run or once production has stabilized to avoid early quality challenges.

Title: Tesla to recall 36,126 Model S and X vehicles in China over touch-screen failures
Summary: Tesla is recalling 36,126 Model S and Model X vehicles in China due to touch-screen failures, stemming from limited "write cycle" memory devices. This follows a similar recall in the U.S. and an investigation in Germany for the same issue, as Tesla agreed to replace the affected memory devices with a 64 GB version. China is a significant market for Tesla, where it held a 12% share of the "new energy vehicle" category in 2020.

Title: Tesla founders Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning talk about the early days and bringing on Elon Musk
Summary: Tesla founders Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning recount the early days of Tesla, challenging the popular belief that Elon Musk started the company. They discuss building and delivering the first Tesla Roadster, convincing the market about electric cars, and how Elon Musk became involved. Despite later contention with Musk, Eberhard and Tarpenning remain supportive of Tesla's mission and reflect positively on their contributions.

Title: Tesla Bets on Bitcoin in Blue-Chip Boost to Cryptocurrency
Summary: Tesla Inc. announced a $1.5 billion investment in Bitcoin and stated its intention to accept the cryptocurrency as a form of payment. This move by the electric-car maker caused Bitcoin prices to surge to a record high. The investment signals a significant endorsement of cryptocurrency from a major blue-chip company.

Title: Tesla (TSLA) Discloses $1.5B Investment in Bitcoin
Summary: Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) announced a $1.5 billion investment in Bitcoin and plans to accept Bitcoin payments for its cars, making it the first S&P 500 company to invest in the cryptocurrency. This move follows a change in its investment policy to diversify and maximize returns on cash. The announcement propelled Bitcoin's price to new record highs, reflecting CEO Elon Musk's bullish stance and broader corporate and retail interest in the asset.

Title: Tesla skips 401(k) match for third straight year
Summary: Tesla has reportedly skipped its 401(k) match for the third consecutive year. This information was reported in an article by Rob Kozlowski on February 8, 2021, at 3:43 PM EST. The move impacts employees who rely on employer contributions to their retirement savings plans.

Title: Tesla existed before Elon Musk: Founders on how they pitched the idea
Summary: This article details how Tesla was founded by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning in 2003, before Elon Musk's involvement. It covers their initial concept for the Tesla Roadster, their pitch to Lotus, and how they secured Musk's investment. The piece also touches on the co-founders' eventual departure from the company and their subsequent careers.

Title: Tesla Bets Big on Bitcoin, Starves its 401(k) Plan
Summary: Tesla announced a $1.5 billion investment in Bitcoin and plans to accept the cryptocurrency as payment, pushing Bitcoin to record highs. Despite this progressive financial move and significant stock growth, Tesla's 401(k) plan has received no company contributions for several years, offering a "pedestrian" plan to its employees. However, the company provides stock options to all employees, which have led to substantial gains for many, potentially offsetting the lack of traditional 401(k) matching.

Title: Why did Tesla buy bitcoin?
Summary: The article discusses Tesla Inc.'s recent investment in bitcoin, highlighting it as a significant move that underscores the increasing acceptance of the digital asset. It raises the central question observers are asking: why did Elon Musk's company make this investment?

Title: General Motors made $6.4 billion in 2020, despite COVID-19
Summary: General Motors reported a profit of $6.43 billion in 2020, despite a 4.5% fall from the previous year, driven by strong demand for trucks and SUVs in the latter half of the year. The company is facing new challenges, including an estimated $1.5 billion to $2 billion loss due to a global semiconductor chip shortage in 2021, but anticipates pretax income of $10 billion to $11 billion for the year. GM also unveiled plans to invest over $7 billion in electric and self-driving vehicles in 2021 as part of its broader push into EVs.

Title: Bitcoin hits record highs as more companies embrace crypto boom
Summary: Bitcoin reached new record highs following announcements from Mastercard Inc. and Bank of New York Mellon Corp. about their increased embrace of cryptocurrencies. This surge is further fueled by Tesla CEO Elon Musk's significant investment in Bitcoin and his public support for cryptocurrencies, attracting more traditional financial institutions to the digital asset class. Despite the growing adoption, critics continue to warn of speculative bubbles and potential misuse.

Title: Biden SEC Nominee Gary Gensler Worth as Much as $119 Million
Summary: Gary Gensler, President Joe Biden’s nominee for SEC chairman, has disclosed a net worth between $41 million and $119 million. This information came from a government ethics form filed as part of his confirmation process. Gensler's past holdings included Tesla and a pension payout from Goldman Sachs.

Title: Tesla to set up electric car manufacturing unit in southern India
Summary: Tesla Inc. plans to establish an electric car manufacturing unit in Karnataka, a southern Indian state, according to a government document. This move follows the incorporation of Tesla Motors India and Energy Private Limited in Bengaluru last month. The company's CEO, Elon Musk, has previously indicated Tesla's entry into India in 2021 as the country seeks to electrify its transport sector.

Title: South Florida Mayors to Visit Vegas, LA Test Tunnel for Local Commuter Rail
Summary: Mayors from Miami and Fort Lauderdale are traveling to the West Coast to examine Elon Musk's Boring Company tunnel technology in Las Vegas and California. Their goal is to assess whether this low-cost tunneling approach could be a viable solution for building underground commuter rail in South Florida, addressing traffic congestion and infrastructure challenges like the New River issue. The Boring Company has already expressed interest in collaborating with Fort Lauderdale officials on potential applications.

Title: Elon Musk may be betting on Bitcoin—but here’s what 50 other CFOs really think about it
Summary: A survey by Gartner Finance revealed that 95% of CFOs have no plans to purchase Bitcoin in the current year, despite Elon Musk's investment. While corporate America's curiosity about Bitcoin is growing, its volatility and cash management problems deter most finance leaders, who prioritize financial stability. However, 5% of companies plan to buy Bitcoin this year, and a larger percentage anticipate doing so in the future, with board risk aversion being less of a concern than expected.

Title: How ST is driving Tesla and Apple e-mobility and 5G ambitions
Summary: STMicroelectronics' success is heavily reliant on its key customers, Tesla and Apple. For Tesla, STMicroelectronics is a leading supplier of Silicon Carbide (SiC) power devices for e-mobility, particularly traction inverters, despite capacity constraints which ST is addressing through acquisitions and R&D. For Apple, STMicroelectronics makes significant contributions to 3D imaging and sensing, including NIR image sensors and Time of Flight detectors for iPhones, though Sony's increasing presence in Apple devices poses a potential challenge for STMicroelectronics' future in the CMOS image sensor market.

Title: Tesla sticker shock: Automaker slashes prices for two models
Summary: Tesla has reduced prices for its Model 3 Standard Range Plus and Model Y Standard Range by 2.6% and 4.8% respectively, while increasing prices for the Performance variants of both models. CEO Elon Musk has previously stated that Tesla's cars are too expensive, and the company frequently uses price adjustments to boost deliveries. This strategy, supported by cost cuts, aims to increase volume, according to analysts.

Title: Tesla cuts Model 3 prices in Japan by as much as 24%
Summary: Tesla has significantly reduced the prices of its Model 3 vehicles in Japan, with cuts reaching as high as 24%. This move comes as the company attempts to boost sales in the Japanese market. The price adjustments affect various configurations of the Model 3 lineup.

Title: Elon Musk explains Tesla's $1.5B bitcoin buy
Summary: Elon Musk explained that Tesla's decision to buy $1.5 billion of Bitcoin was motivated by the inability to get a return on the company's cash when fiat currency yields negative real interest. He also noted that "Bitcoin is almost as bs as fiat money," agreeing with MicroStrategy CEO Michael Saylor. Tesla plans to accept Bitcoin for car payments and may invest further in digital assets.

Title: The man charged with keeping SolarEdge’s current flowing
Summary: SolarEdge CEO Zvi Lando discusses the company's valuation spike to $18 billion, its expansion into new renewable energy sectors, and the challenge of stepping into the role previously held by the late founder Guy Sella. He also addresses issues like the impact of Elon Musk's Tesla announcement on SolarEdge's stock and the company's commitment to remaining Israeli despite global operations.

Title: Tesla Stock Wipes Out Gains for the Year
Summary: Tesla Inc. shares erased all their year-to-date gains and briefly traded below their S&P 500 entry level, experiencing a significant intraday decline. This drop was influenced by CEO Elon Musk's comments on cryptocurrency valuations and Tesla's decision to halt orders for its lowest-priced Model Y, amid increasing competition from traditional automakers in the EV market.

Title: Lucid Motors 'humbly' embarks on the difficult task of mass producing its electric cars, CEO says
Summary: Lucid Motors CEO Peter Rawlinson emphasized the company's commitment to "humbly and diligently execute" the mass production of its electric vehicles following a SPAC deal that valued the company at over $50 billion. Rawlinson, a former Tesla executive, highlighted Lucid's world-class technology and the challenge of scaling automobile production. The luxury Air sedan deliveries are set for the second half of 2021, with plans for an SUV in 2023 and more affordable models later, projecting significant EBITDA and vehicle deliveries by 2026.

Title: Nothing Lucid About a $57 Billion Valuation for an Electric-Vehicle Startup
Summary: Lucid Motors, an electric-vehicle startup, announced a merger with SPAC Churchill Capital IV, leading to an implied market valuation of roughly $57 billion. While Lucid is seen as a strong contender to follow Tesla's success, investors are questioning the inflated valuation. The article highlights the significant increase in Churchill Capital IV's market value following reports of the merger talks.

Title: Tesla's Elon Musk says U.S. factory closed for two days due to parts shortages
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that the company's Fremont, California plant was shut down for two days this week due to "parts shortages" but had since reopened. This closure comes as several major automakers are experiencing chip shortages, forcing them to reduce production. Musk also noted that the company was using the downtime for equipment upgrades and maintenance, and that production of the Model S and Model X lines would soon return to two shifts.

Title: Powerful House Dem bought cannabis stocks after pushing decriminalization
Summary: Rep. John Yarmuth, chairman of the House Budget Committee, purchased up to $60,000 worth of stock in cannabis companies shortly after pushing for the decriminalization of marijuana. While such stock purchases by members of Congress are legal under the STOCK Act if not based on non-public information, Yarmuth's investment coincided with a House bill he co-sponsored to decriminalize cannabis. This event follows other instances of Congressional members or their spouses facing scrutiny for timely investment decisions, including Paul Pelosi's Tesla options and Senators' stock sales prior to the COVID-19 market crash.

Title: EXCLUSIVE Goldman Sachs restarts cryptocurrency desk amid bitcoin boom
Summary: Goldman Sachs has reactivated its cryptocurrency trading desk to deal in bitcoin futures and non-deliverable forwards, driven by increasing institutional interest in digital assets. This move positions the bank within the rapidly expanding digital assets sector, which also involves exploring blockchain technology, central bank digital currencies, and the potential for a bitcoin exchange-traded fund. The decision follows bitcoin's significant price surge and broader acceptance by major companies like Tesla and Bank of New York Mellon, despite its inherent volatility.

Title: Steer clear of Tesla, look at semiconductors, says American Century
Summary: American Century Investments advises investors to avoid Tesla (TSLA) due to its high valuation and instead consider component suppliers for electric and autonomous vehicles, such as Aptiv (APTV), NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), and Cree (CREE). Brent Puff, a senior portfolio manager at American Century, highlights the significant growth potential in electrification and autonomous driving, suggesting these lesser-known semiconductor companies offer a better risk-reward profile than Tesla. Morningstar analysts largely agree on Tesla's overvaluation and competitive challenges, while noting some of the recommended companies are either fairly valued or, in Aptiv's case, overvalued despite strong fundamentals.

Title: The Parent of All Parents: Here's What Berkshire Hathaway Actually Does
Summary: Berkshire Hathaway is a holding company led by Warren Buffett that owns about 70 private companies and minority stakes in 41 public stocks across various sectors. While it doesn't engage in manufacturing, it controls company shares and investment interests. Buffett is the top shareholder, and notable holdings include significant stakes in Apple and Coca-Cola, with a clear disinterest in investing in Tesla.

Title: Why Cathie Wood's once hot Ark Innovation ETF has lost all its 2021 gains
Summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK), which skyrocketed in 2020, has lost all its 2021 gains, declining 5.5% on Thursday and bringing its year-to-date decline to a similar amount. This pullback reflects a broader trend in tech stocks, driven by rising 10-year Treasury yields and fears of inflation leading to higher interest rates, which disproportionately affect growth stocks. The ETF's top holdings, including Tesla, Square, Roku, Teladoc, and Spotify, have seen significant declines.

Title: BUZZ, the ETF of Social-Media Darlings, Drops in Trading Debut
Summary: The VanEck Vectors Social Sentiment ETF (BUZZ) began trading, aiming to capitalize on the retail-investing trend and the influence of social media buzz on stock performance. This ETF includes stocks like Tesla and DraftKings, aiming to capture the "new era of investing" where information is sourced and shared online.

Title: Four Investments of Nancy Pelosi and Her Husband Reveal Much
Summary: The article discusses four significant investments made by House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and her husband, Paul Pelosi, on December 22. These investments include shares in AllianceBernstein (AB) and call options in Apple (AAPL), Tesla (TSLA), and Walt Disney Co (DIS), totaling between $1,751,003 and $3,500,000. Experts weigh in on the implications of these bullish trades, noting that while the Pelosis are wealthy, their investment choices align with market opportunities, although the full scope and reasoning behind the trades are not publicly known.

Title: Tech-heavy Nasdaq hits correction with 10.5% fall from peak
Summary: The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite has entered correction territory, falling 10.5% from its February peak, as technology shares experienced a significant sell-off. This downturn was driven by concerns over rising bond yields and inflation fears stemming from a new $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief bill. While financial, restaurant, and travel stocks rose on reopening hopes, they couldn't offset the weight of declining big tech shares like Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla.

Title: Tesla to boost Texas energy grid with secret mega-battery, report says
Summary: Tesla is reportedly building a 100-megawatt mega-battery in Angleton, Texas, through a subsidiary named Gambit Energy Storage LLC, to enter the state's power market. This project aims to support the Texas energy grid, which faced near-total collapse during recent winter storms. The battery's construction comes amid increased scrutiny of Texas's energy infrastructure and Tesla CEO Elon Musk's growing presence and investments in the state.

Title: Steel Dynamics Inc. ranks No. 1 in Fortune metal industry list
Summary: Steel Dynamics Inc. (SDI) was ranked No. 1 in the metals industry category on Fortune's World’s Most Admired Companies list. This recognition, based on a poll of corporate executives, directors, and analysts, highlights SDI's strong operational and financial performance, innovation, and leadership. The article also notes SDI's new plant in Sinton, Texas, is expected to be operational this year and may supply steel to Tesla's Gigafactory for the Cybertruck.

Title: Tesla loses a third of its value for the third time in a year
Summary: Tesla Inc.'s stock experienced its third significant drop in a year, losing a third of its value from its January record high, primarily due to investor concerns about rising interest rates affecting high-valuation stocks. The selloff wiped off nearly $300 billion from its market capitalization, moving it behind Facebook. This decline is more pronounced than other major tech companies, and its shares have steadily fallen since announcing a bitcoin purchase, even as bitcoin’s price climbed.

Title: Tesla shares bounce back following steep five-day decline
Summary: Tesla shares rebounded on Tuesday after experiencing a significant five-day decline, which erased about $149 billion from its valuation. The recovery was fueled by positive news, including an analyst upgrade from New Street Research, a rally in Bitcoin, and a general shift in sentiment towards high-multiple technology stocks. Analyst Pierre Ferragu upgraded Tesla to buy, citing strong earnings momentum and demand, suggesting the stock could trade at a high multiple similar to Amazon's historical performance.

Title: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF surges more than 10% for its best day ever
Summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK) surged over 10% for its best day ever, driven by a rebound in tech stocks like Tesla, Zoom Video, and Palantir. This rally helped recoup some recent sharp losses for the fund, which had been impacted by a market rotation out of high-growth tech into value stocks. Despite recent volatility, Wood remains confident in her disruptive strategy, viewing the sell-off as an opportunity to buy.

Title: Exclusive: LG hopes to make new battery cells for Tesla in 2023 in U.S. or Europe -sources
Summary: LG Energy Solution aims to produce advanced 4680 battery cells for Tesla's electric vehicles by 2023, considering manufacturing sites in the United States and Europe. While LG has made samples, it faces technological hurdles and has not yet secured orders from Tesla for these new cells, which Tesla is also developing in-house. LG currently supplies smaller cells to Tesla in China and is a major battery supplier for other automotive giants like General Motors.

Title: West Michigan gets first Tesla service center in Grand Rapids
Summary: Tesla is opening its first service center in West Michigan, located in Grand Rapids, following a settlement with the state that allows the company to sell and service its vehicles directly to customers. This new facility, which will also handle sales and delivery, is part of Tesla's expansion after previously being restricted from direct sales and service in Michigan. Michigan residents previously had to travel out-of-state for Tesla purchases and service.

Title: If You Invested $1,000 In Tesla 10 Years Ago, Here's How Much You'd Have Now
Summary: This article evaluates the return on a hypothetical $1,000 investment in Tesla Motors (NASDAQ: TSLA) made 10 years ago. It highlights Tesla's growth from its IPO to becoming a major electric vehicle manufacturer, detailing its stock performance, market capitalization milestones, and recent fluctuations. The article illustrates the substantial profit an early investor would have accrued despite the stock's volatility.

Title: Promotion? Musk is ‘Technoking of Tesla’, CFO is ‘Master of Coin’
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has adopted the new title "Technoking of Tesla," and CFO Zach Kirkhorn is now "Master of Coin," according to a regulatory filing, though both retain their original executive titles. Additionally, Jerome Guillen, previously president of automotive, has transitioned to lead Tesla's heavy trucking program, a move analysts view positively as the company prepares to enter the critical heavy-trucks market.

Title: Tesla Names Jerome Guillen President of Heavy Trucking
Summary: Tesla has appointed Jerome Guillen as president of its heavy trucking division, signaling a strategic focus on the electric Semi program. Guillen, formerly president of automotive, will now lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi, including charging and servicing networks, as the company plans to start deliveries by the end of 2021. This move has been viewed positively by investors, with analysts highlighting Tesla's commitment to its trucking vision.

Title: Volkswagen aims to knock Tesla out of top spot by 2025 in major EV push
Summary: Volkswagen plans to become the global electric vehicle market leader by 2025, surpassing Tesla, by increasing cost-saving efforts, standardizing technologies, and boosting EV sales to 1 million this year. The company will focus on a "platform" approach for economies of scale, expand its software division to compete with tech giants, and aims for an operating return on sales of 7% to 8% by 2025. This aggressive strategy includes significant investments in battery production and software development despite challenges posed by the pandemic and semiconductor shortages.

Title: Classic Range Rover Electromod Is Powered By A Tesla Drivetrain And Can Hit 60MPH In 5.2 Sec
Summary: E.C.D. Automotive Design has completed its first electric conversion, transforming a Classic Range Rover into an electromod powered by a Tesla drivetrain. This restomod can achieve 0-60 mph in 5.2 seconds and boasts a 220-mile range from its 100 kWh battery pack. The company plans to continue electrifying other Land Rovers following this successful project.

Title: Leverage Shares launches 25 single stock short and leveraged ETPs
Summary: Leverage Shares has introduced 25 new single-stock short and leveraged (S&L) Exchange-Traded Products (ETPs) on the London Stock Exchange, expanding its existing range. These ETPs track STOXX indices and include prominent names like Tesla and PayPal, as well as UK blue chips such as Barclays and BP. The products are physically backed and available in USD, GBP, and EUR, catering to investors looking to capitalize on market shifts and hedge exposures in volatile markets.

Title: EV Makers Fall on Lordstown SEC Review, Nikola Investor Sale
Summary: Electric-vehicle (EV) startups experienced a downturn due to issues at Lordstown Motors and Nikola, compounded by rising Treasury yields. Lordstown Motors (RIDE), Nikola Corp. (NKLA), Nio Inc. (NIO), Workhorse Group Inc. (WKHS), XPeng Inc. (XPEV), and Li Auto Inc. (LI) all saw declines. Tesla Inc. (TSLA) also fell after the UK reduced its purchasing bonus for EVs, disqualifying Tesla models from subsidies.

Title: What Happens When You Smash a Tesla Into a Vintage Range Rover?
Summary: E.C.D. Automotive Design, a restomodding company based in Florida, is building electric Range Rover Classics using Tesla drivetrains. These modified vehicles aim to resolve the notorious unreliability of vintage Land Rovers while offering a modern electric power source and extended range. The custom-built electric Range Rovers start at around $195,000, with higher-end builds approaching $300,000.

Title: New Meets Old in This Tesla-Powered Range Rover Classic
Summary: East Coast Defenders (E.C.D.) Automotive Design has introduced an electric conversion for Range Rover Classics, featuring a Tesla Direct Drive EV powertrain and 100-kWh battery pack. This allows the classic SUV to achieve 0-60 mph in 5.2 seconds and offers a 220-mile range. The vehicle retains its vintage exterior while boasting a luxurious, modern interior, highlighting a growing trend of electrifying classic cars.
