Title: 2 Long-Term EV Plays Trading Under $20
Summary: The article highlights two long-term electric vehicle (EV) investment opportunities trading under $20: Ford Motor Company (NYSE: F) and ChargePoint Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: CHPT). Ford is praised for its aggressive push into EV production and carbon neutrality, with strong growth potential and a low P/E ratio compared to Tesla. ChargePoint is presented as a leading EV charging network operator, poised for growth through its expanding network and subscription-based model, despite not yet being profitable.

Title: Tesla denies that legal chief who conducted internal probe has left
Summary: Tesla has denied reports that its legal chief, who was involved in an internal probe, has left the company. The article briefly mentions this denial.

Title: Tesla Supercharger network ranks highest in customer satisfaction, finds J.D. Power
Summary: A J.D. Power study found that the Tesla Supercharger network leads in customer satisfaction for DC fast-charging with a score of 739, significantly above the industry average. While most EV owners are satisfied with the ease of public charging, reliability remains a major concern, with 20% of respondents unable to charge due to malfunctioning equipment. Tesla plans to triple the size of its Supercharger network and may open it to other EV brands, potentially using federal funding.

Title: Ford is laying off about 3,000 workers
Summary: Ford Motor Co. is laying off approximately 3,000 white-collar and contract workers in the U.S. and Canada as part of a restructuring effort to lower costs and accelerate its transition to electric vehicles. The cuts, which represent about 6% of its salaried workforce in the region, come after the company's executive chairman and CEO emphasized the need to reshape operations and improve competitiveness against rivals like General Motors, Stellantis, and Tesla. Ford aims to streamline its business by eliminating redundant work and reorganizing functions across its various units.

Title: Musk seeks documents from Jack Dorsey in fight over Twitter deal
Summary: Elon Musk is seeking documents from Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey as part of his legal battle to terminate the $44 billion acquisition deal. Musk's subpoena requests communications and documents regarding his April agreement to buy Twitter and information about spam accounts, a key issue in his claim that Twitter violated the contract. Dorsey, who supported Musk's offer and shares views on Twitter's algorithm and subscription model, leads Block Inc.

Title: These Wide-Moat Stocks Are Gaining Ground
Summary: Quality stocks with wide economic moats, including Microsoft and Amazon, have outperformed since the bear market low in June, despite still being undervalued. While narrow-moat stocks have seen stronger recent gains due to market-cap weighting of companies like Apple and Tesla, wide-moat companies are better positioned to handle inflation due to their pricing power. Overall, Morningstar analysts consider wide-moat stocks to be deeply undervalued compared to overpriced narrow-moat stocks.

Title: PG&E, Tesla virtual power plant delivers 16.5 MW to California grid amid calls for energy conservation
Summary: Nearly 2,500 PG&E customers with Tesla battery systems contributed up to 16.5 MW of solar power to California's grid, marking the first activation of the virtual power plant. This initiative comes as California faces high temperatures and calls for energy conservation, with participating customers receiving $2/kWh for exported electricity. The program aims to bolster grid reliability during peak demand and emergencies.

Title: Tesla's former energy head launches startup to compete against Powerwall with key partners
Summary: Kunal Girotra, formerly Tesla's head of energy products, has launched a new startup called Lunar Energy to compete with Tesla's Powerwall. Lunar Energy secured $300 million in funding from Sunrun and SK Group and plans to introduce a home battery system and home electrification products. The company also acquired Moixa, a software company specializing in distributed energy resources management, to integrate intelligent software with its hardware offerings.

Title: Tesla shares close lower after 3-1 stock split
Summary: Tesla's shares closed 2% lower after its three-for-one stock split took effect, aimed at attracting retail investors. The stock opened at $302 and closed at $296.07 after previously closing at $891.29 before the split. This marks Tesla's second stock split in two years, a strategy adopted by high-growth companies to make shares more affordable for individual investors.

Title: Tesla announces 3-for-1 stock split
Summary: Tesla Inc. announced a three-for-one stock split, aimed at diversifying its investor base and making shares more accessible to individual investors. This is Tesla's second stock split, following a five-for-one split in August 2020. The move is seen as an acknowledgment of the importance of retail investors, despite the availability of fractional shares through many brokerages.

Title: Elon Musk Says Nuclear Plants Must Remain Open. Uranium Stocks Are Surging.
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has publicly stated his support for keeping nuclear power plants operational, leading to a surge in the stock prices of several uranium mining companies. Musk's comments underscore a growing debate about the role of nuclear energy in global power grids, particularly in the context of energy security and climate change.

Title: Uranium Stocks Soar As Elon Musk Applauds the Alternative Energy Source
Summary: Uranium stocks are rising amidst increasing global interest in nuclear power as an alternative energy source. This interest is driven by the ongoing global energy crisis and the war in Ukraine. Elon Musk has voiced his approval for the return to nuclear energy and highlighted the need for fossil fuels in the short term to maintain civilization.

Title: Hyundai narrows Level 3 self-driving tech gap with Tesla to one year
Summary: Hyundai Motor Co. has significantly narrowed its Level 3 self-driving technology gap with Tesla to just one year, with plans to launch Level 3 cars starting with the Genesis G90 later this year. The company aims to surpass Tesla in system computation speeds within a few years and intends to roll out fully autonomous vehicles by 2030. Hyundai also revealed it has cross-checked its technology by disassembling a Tesla Model 3 and plans to reduce integrated controllers in future IONIQ models for better efficiency.

Title: U.S. agency: 'unlawful' for Tesla to prevent employees from wearing union shirts
Summary: The National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) ruled that it was unlawful for Tesla Inc. to prohibit employees from wearing shirts with union insignia, reaffirming the right to display union clothing. This decision stems from a 2017 dispute with the United Automobile Workers (UAW) union and reverses a prior 2019 NLRB ruling involving Walmart Inc. The NLRB ordered Tesla to rescind its policy against union shirts, noting this is not the first clash between Tesla and the agency.

Title: Which Charging Networks Can your EV Access?
Summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to electric vehicle (EV) charging networks in the U.S., detailing which networks are compatible with various 2022 and 2023 EV models. It explains that most EVs use standard Level 2 and DC fast-charging connectors, with exceptions like Tesla's Supercharger and Rivian's Adventure Network. The article also lists incentives offered by automakers for specific charging networks.

Title: Cruise lines to begin using Elon Musk's Starlink Wi-Fi
Summary: Royal Caribbean Group, including brands Royal Caribbean, Celebrity Cruises, and Silversea Cruises, will implement Elon Musk's Starlink Wi-Fi across its fleet by the end of Q1 2023. This initiative aims to provide significantly faster and more reliable internet connectivity for both passengers and crew, addressing the long-standing issue of slow and expensive internet at sea. The cost structure for Starlink will vary by brand, with Silversea offering it free, Celebrity including basic Wi-Fi with premium upgrade options, and Royal Caribbean yet to announce its pricing model.

Title: With Tesla Decision, NLRB Rules Dress Codes Unlawful That Restrict Pro-Union Apparel
Summary: The NLRB has ruled in the Tesla Inc. case that workplace dress codes prohibiting pro-union apparel are presumptively unlawful, overturning a previous standard. Employers must now demonstrate "special circumstances" to justify such restrictions, with the NLRB rejecting Tesla's arguments regarding damage to vehicles. This decision signals a more pro-labor stance from the current NLRB and requires employers to review and potentially revise their dress code policies.

Title: Musk says SpaceX discussed iPhone satellite service with Apple
Summary: Elon Musk revealed that SpaceX has engaged in discussions with Apple Inc. regarding the integration of Starlink's satellite connectivity into iPhones. This announcement follows Apple's recent partnership with Globalstar Inc. for satellite services on its latest iPhone model, indicating a growing trend in offering satellite-based communication for smartphones. Musk emphasized that dedicated technology is crucial for optimal satellite-to-cell phone service.

Title: TESLA Inc. looking to bring lithium refinery to Coastal Bend
Summary: Tesla Inc. is considering building a "battery-grade lithium hydroxide refining facility" in the Coastal Bend area of Texas, near Robstown, or potentially in Louisiana. The company has applied for tax breaks from the state of Texas, which could lead to significant job creation and economic growth for the chosen location. However, the proposal faces concerns regarding water usage and environmental impact from some local residents.

Title: Under the Hood of RCD
Summary: The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF (RCD) saw significant inflows in August, making it the most popular Invesco equal-weight sector ETF for the month. RCD offers investors exposure to the consumer discretionary sector with an equal-weighted approach, diversifying away from large-cap bias and providing a tilt towards smaller, potentially undervalued companies. This strategy aims to reduce concentration risk by ensuring each of its 60 holdings, including companies like Etsy, Tesla, and Amazon, receives approximately equal allocation during quarterly rebalances.

Title: Tesla wants to mine Lithium in Nigeria: What are the hidden costs?
Summary: Nigeria rejected Tesla's request to mine lithium unless the company establishes a battery-making factory within the West African nation to add value to the mineral. The Nigerian minister of mines is seeking other lithium miners who align with the country's industrial policy. This decision aligns with Nigeria's goal of retaining value along the global processing chain of lithium, a mineral whose demand is projected to triple by 2040.

Title: Tesla struggles with Elon Musk’s strict return-to-office policy
Summary: Three months after Elon Musk's strict return-to-office mandate, Tesla faces challenges with insufficient office space and resources to accommodate all employees. The policy has led to a decline in morale, increased absenteeism tracking, and the dismissal of some remote workers who could not relocate, impacting the company's ability to retain talent.

Title: Tesla (TSLA) Keeps Duping Consumers About Self-Driving Cars, Suit Says
Summary: Tesla Inc. is facing a class-action lawsuit for allegedly misleading consumers about the capabilities of its self-driving cars. A California man claims the company deceptively marketed its driver-assistance systems, continuously promising advancements that have not materialized. This suit follows similar accusations from California's Department of Motor Vehicles regarding false advertising.

Title: Tesla is sued by drivers over alleged false Autopilot, Full Self-Driving claims
Summary: Tesla is facing a proposed class-action lawsuit from drivers who allege that the company and Elon Musk falsely advertised its Autopilot and Full Self-Driving features. The lawsuit claims Tesla misled the public into believing these technologies were fully functional or imminent since 2016, despite known deficiencies, to boost sales and stock price. This legal action follows similar complaints from California's Department of Motor Vehicles regarding the overstatement of Tesla's advanced driver assistance systems.

Title: GM to sell up to 175,000 electric vehicles to Hertz through 2027
Summary: General Motors has agreed to sell up to 175,000 electric vehicles to Hertz Global over the next five years, starting early next year with Chevy Bolt EV and EUV models. This deal is GM's largest vehicle sale agreement with Hertz, following similar agreements between Hertz and Tesla and Polestar, and aims to significantly increase EV adoption and Hertz's electric fleet. Despite a broader market decline, the companies decided not to release financial details of the deal, but GM plans to sell the EVs at "retail margin" rather than at discounted fleet sales.

Title: 7 Meme Stocks to Buy During a Stock Market Crash
Summary: This article identifies seven meme stocks that aggressive investors might consider buying during a stock market crash for long-term potential. Each stock is discussed with reasons for its meme stock appeal and potential for recovery despite current market downturns.

Title: Weekly Recalls: Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz (2), Nissan (2), Tesla
Summary: This article details the weekly vehicle recalls issued for Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz (two separate recalls), Nissan (two separate recalls), and Tesla. The recalls address issues ranging from fuel system defects and improperly tightened lug nuts to electrical system faults, detaching window trim, transmission park pawl problems, faulty seat belts, and malfunctioning automatic window reversal systems. Each recall specifies the affected models, potential number of units, the nature of the defect, the manufacturer's proposed remedy, and owner notification timelines.

Title: Tesla Recalls Almost 1.1 Million Vehicles Over Window Glitch
Summary: Tesla has recalled nearly 1.1 million vehicles across all four of its models due to a power window glitch where windows may close too quickly, posing a pinching risk to occupants. The electric car manufacturer plans to resolve this issue with an over-the-air software update, eliminating the need for vehicle owners to bring their cars in for service. The recall impacts Model S, X, 3, and Y vehicles manufactured between 2017 and 2022.

Title: Hertz is buying up to 175,000 electric vehicles from GM
Summary: Hertz has announced a major purchase of up to 175,000 electric vehicles from General Motors over the next five years, expanding its EV rental fleet. This follows earlier agreements with Tesla and Polestar. The acquisitions will include a variety of GM's North American passenger vehicle brands and types, with GM aiming to significantly ramp up EV production and Hertz targeting a quarter of its fleet to be electric by 2024.

Title: Tesla workers' lawsuit over layoffs likely belongs in arbitration, judge says
Summary: A U.S. magistrate judge has recommended that a proposed class-action lawsuit against Tesla Inc, concerning alleged failures to provide advance notice for layoffs, be moved to private arbitration. The judge stated that an arbitrator, not a court, should determine the validity of the arbitration agreements signed by Tesla workers. This decision means former employees will likely pursue their claims individually in arbitration rather than through a class action.

Title: Tesla names Airbnb co-founder to board
Summary: Tesla Inc. has appointed Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia to its board of directors, bringing the total number of directors back to eight. Gebbia steps into a role previously held by Larry Ellison and continues to serve on Airbnb's board. He had previously stepped back from a daily operational role at Airbnb, which he co-founded in 2007.

Title: Elon Musk seeks to end SEC 'muzzle' requiring pre-approval of tweets
Summary: Elon Musk's lawyers have petitioned a federal appeals court to dismantle a provision within his 2018 consent decree with the SEC, which necessitates a Tesla lawyer's pre-approval for some of his tweets. They argue this requirement acts as a "government-imposed muzzle" violating free speech principles. The SEC has not yet commented but is expected to file its own brief in response.

Title: Tesla adds billionaire Airbnb co-founder Gebbia to board
Summary: Tesla Inc. has appointed Airbnb co-founder Joseph Gebbia to its board, reversing an earlier plan to reduce the number of directors. This move follows criticism from a shareholder group regarding the lack of independent board members and the need to comply with a 2018 SEC consent decree. Gebbia will waive cash and stock compensation for a period, though some experts question whether his appointment truly adds diversity to the board.

Title: CATL – The Battery Giant Leading Innovation In China A-Shares
Summary: Contemporary Amperax Technology Co., Limited (CATL) is a leading innovator and one of the largest EV battery suppliers globally, providing batteries for major companies like Tesla, Ford, and NIO. Due to its listing on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, CATL is often inaccessible to international investors through standard brokerage accounts and ETFs, making the KraneShares Bosera MSCI China A-Share ETF (KBA) a key avenue for investment access. The article highlights CATL's significant role in the EV market and its founder's origin story.

Title: Here are the people who texted Elon Musk to offer advice or money for the Twitter deal
Summary: This article details text messages between Elon Musk and various tech and media luminaries concerning his bid to buy Twitter. The exchanges reveal advice, investment offers, and discussions about the platform's future, as shared in court documents related to Musk's attempt to back out of the $44 billion acquisition. Notable texters include Jack Dorsey, Larry Ellison, Joe Lonsdale, and Sam Bankman-Fried.

Title: Tesla Gets a Warning From NIO, Li, XPeng Deliveries
Summary: Deliveries from Chinese electric vehicle makers NIO, XPeng, and Li indicate a warning for Tesla as their growth lags behind the overall industry. The article suggests that car buyers are drawn to new models, potentially impacting Tesla's market share. This trend highlights the importance of innovation and new product offerings in the EV market.

Title: Tesla's a 'key stock in everyone’s ESG portfolio.' So why is that so controversial?
Summary: This article examines the controversy surrounding Tesla's inclusion in ESG portfolios despite its environmental contributions. While Tesla is a leader in EV technology and carbon emission reduction, concerns about its corporate governance, transparency on emissions, and controversies like racial discrimination and Autopilot safety issues have led to scrutiny and even removal from certain ESG indices. This highlights a fundamental debate within the ESG investing world regarding what constitutes true social responsibility and impact.

Title: Tesla slides on widening delivery and production gap, demand worries
Summary: Tesla Inc. shares dropped 8.6% due to lower-than-expected third-quarter deliveries, attributed to logistical challenges and growing concerns about demand amidst rising prices and economic slowdown. Despite record deliveries, the significant gap between production and deliveries highlighted transport issues, impacting Tesla's market value and raising questions about future sales. Analysts, however, anticipate robust manufacturing margins for Tesla, while rival Rivian reported increased production.

Title: Can Vietnam’s VinFast be the Real Contender to Tesla’s EV Throne?
Summary: VinFast, a Vietnamese automotive company, is emerging as a potential contender in the electric vehicle (EV) market against established players like Tesla. Despite being a relatively new entrant, VinFast has ambitious goals for production and profitability, offering lower-cost, tech-heavy EVs with comparable ranges to Tesla models. The company is actively expanding its manufacturing capabilities and supply chain, including battery production and semiconductor partnerships, with a focus on penetrating high-wealth Western markets.

Title: Cathie Wood bought up Tesla shares after a Monday stock plunge. They quickly rebounded.
Summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Investment Management LLC purchased 132,213 shares of Tesla on Monday, marking her firm's first buy since mid-June after a significant stock decline. This dip-buying activity led to a quick rebound in Tesla's shares by as much as 4% on Tuesday, contributing to S&P 500 gains. The purchase indicates a renewed strategy of buying the dip after a year of selling down her stake in the EV manufacturer, whose shares had previously lost their "crown jewel" status in her main fund.

Title: Micron chooses New York for $100B factory instead of Central Texas
Summary: Micron Technology announced its decision to build a new $100 billion semiconductor factory in Central New York, opting against Lockhart, Texas, which had been a finalist for the facility. The move comes with the aid of $5.5 billion in incentives from New York. This investment is part of Micron's larger plan to invest $40 billion in the U.S.

Title: Is Tesla seeing a slowdown in demand?
Summary: Early signs suggest a potential slowdown in demand for Tesla vehicles, indicated by falling waiting times for deliveries in the US and China and the company building more EVs than it delivered in Q3 2022. Analysts note increasing premium pricing and exposure to a decelerating global economy as key factors, while Tesla maintains it still has more demand than supply. The issue of demand and supply balance will be crucial for investors when the company reports quarterly results on October 19.

Title: Icahn had Twitter stake worth over $500 mln before Musk's about-face - WSJ
Summary: Activist investor Carl Icahn amassed a Twitter stake worth over $500 million in the months leading up to Elon Musk's decision to proceed with the takeover. Icahn, who paid around the mid-$30s per share, made an estimated profit exceeding $250 million after Twitter shares jumped over 22% following Musk's announcement. Other investors like D.E. Shaw Group and Daniel Loeb's Third Point LLC are also expected to see significant gains from their recent bets on Twitter shares.

Title: Exclusive: Apollo, Sixth Street no longer in talks to finance Twitter deal
Summary: Apollo Global Management and Sixth Street Partners are no longer discussing providing financing for Elon Musk's proposed $44 billion acquisition of Twitter. These talks reportedly ceased months ago when Musk first began to express doubts about the deal. Musk later confirmed that neither entity was part of the announced third-party equity or debt financing.

Title: Tesla Stock Gets a Little Good News: S&P Upgrades Tesla Bonds
Summary: S&P Global has upgraded the bonds of electric-vehicle maker Tesla, removing their junk status. This development is a piece of good news for Tesla stock investors. The upgrade signifies improved financial health and creditworthiness for the company.

Title: Musk says Pepsi to receive Tesla's first Semi trucks in December
Summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla is starting production of its Semi electric trucks and PepsiCo Inc will receive the first deliveries on December 1st. The truck, which has a 500-mile range and is expected to cost $180,000, has seen its production timeline pushed back multiple times since its 2017 unveiling. PepsiCo had reserved 100 of these trucks to reduce fuel costs and fleet emissions.

Title: Tesla Aims to Deliver First Semitrailer Trucks in December to PepsiCo
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced plans to deliver the first all-electric semitrailer truck to PepsiCo in December, five years after its initial reveal. The truck is expected to have a 500-mile range on a single charge. This delivery marks a significant step for Tesla's long-delayed Semi project.

Title: PepsiCo confirms Tesla Semi truck deliveries to start in December
Summary: PepsiCo has confirmed it will be the first company to receive Tesla Semi truck deliveries, starting December 1st. The electric trucks will be deployed at PepsiCo's Frito-Lay plant in Modesto, California, and its PepsiCo beverages factory in Sacramento, as part of the company's efforts to reduce fuel costs and emissions. Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced production of the Semi truck, which boasts a 500-mile range, after years of delays.

Title: Tesla's China-made sales hit record following Shanghai factory upgrade
Summary: Tesla Inc. delivered a record 83,135 China-made electric vehicles in September, following an upgrade to its Shanghai factory. This increase comes despite a challenging economic environment and growing competition from domestic EV makers in China. Globally, Tesla's third-quarter deliveries fell short of analyst expectations, yet still marked a record for the company.

Title: PayPal says policy to fine customers for 'misinformation' was an 'error'
Summary: PayPal clarified that a recent policy update suggesting fines for misinformation was an error and never intended to be implemented. The company faced significant backlash on social media, leading its shares to drop, and prominent figures like former president David Marcus and co-founder Elon Musk criticized the policy. PayPal apologized for the confusion caused by the incorrect information.

Title: Pepsi first in line for Tesla semi truck deliveries starting in December
Summary: Five years after its unveiling, the Tesla semi truck is finally set for delivery, with Pepsico Inc. being the first recipient in December. Pepsico has reserved 100 semi trucks and plans to have 15 on the road by year-end. This development follows Tesla's prioritization of other models due to supply shortages and is boosted by the Inflation Reduction Act's tax incentives for heavy-duty electric trucks.

Title: General Motors launches electric grid division
Summary: General Motors has launched a new division called GM Energy, signaling the auto industry's strategic goal of fusing electric cars with the electric grid. This new unit will offer a comprehensive suite of energy services, including bi-directional charging, vehicle-to-home capabilities, stationary storage, and microgrid solutions, positioning GM to compete with companies like Tesla in the broader battery and energy market. The initiative aims to address challenges with grid infrastructure, energy storage, and management, with plans for dealerships to promote these new energy products and vehicles to serve as aggregated resources for utilities.

Title: Tesla Plans to Deliver Semis to Pepsi Years After Unveiling
Summary: Tesla is set to deliver its first Semi trucks to PepsiCo Inc. on December 1, five years after the electric big rigs were initially unveiled by Elon Musk. PepsiCo confirmed it will take delivery of 15 of the 100 reserved trucks by year-end, which will be deployed at its Frito-Lay and beverage plants in California. The delivery follows production delays due to prioritizing other Tesla models and supply chain issues, with renewed urgency fueled by new federal tax credits for heavy-duty electric trucks.

Title: GM takes on Tesla in home and commercial energy storage, management
Summary: General Motors is launching a new unit, GM Energy, to compete with Tesla in the home and commercial energy storage and management market. GM Energy will offer stationary storage batteries, solar panels, and hydrogen fuel cells, bundling existing public charging services with new residential and commercial offerings. This expansion leverages GM's expertise in batteries, manufacturing, and connectivity, aiming for a significant share in the estimated $120-$150 billion energy management market.

Title: General Motors takes on Tesla with new energy division
Summary: General Motors is launching a new unit called GM Energy to offer energy storage and management services to residential and commercial customers, directly competing with Tesla's established energy business. GM Energy will provide EV chargers, stationary batteries, solar panels, and hydrogen fuel cells, with Ultium Home services starting in late 2023. The company aims to leverage its core competencies in vehicles and batteries to tap into a multi-billion dollar energy management market.

Title: General Motors is launching its own energy storage service, GM Energy
Summary: General Motors (GM) is launching a new energy storage service called GM Energy, which will offer residential and commercial customers services like stationary storage batteries, solar panels, and hydrogen fuel cells, similar to Tesla's offerings. The service will bundle public charging with "Ultium Home" and "Ultium Commercial" units, and GM expects to begin sales of Ultium Home boxes in late 2023. GM also plans to team up with SunPower Corp for solar panels and allow businesses to sell energy back to utilities during peak consumption.

Title: Why CATL Is the Global EV Battery Leader and How to Gain Exposure
Summary: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Ltd (CATL) is the global leader in electric vehicle batteries, supplying major brands like Tesla, NIO, and Ford. The Chinese company, founded by Yuqun Zeng, has leveraged innovation and China's dominance in battery-grade metal refining to become a powerhouse in the rapidly growing EV market.
