Title: Valkyrie to Liquidate Bitcoin Balance Sheet ETF After Limited Uptake
Summary: Valkyrie Funds announced the liquidation of its Bitcoin Balance Sheet Opportunities ETF (VBB) due to limited investor uptake. The fund, which included companies like Tesla and MicroStrategy, will be liquidated by the end of October and delisted from Nasdaq, with investors receiving cash redemption. VBB had only about $570,000 in net assets under management and underperformed the S&P 500 significantly.

Title: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy gets a surprise endorsement from Twitter's soon-to-be owner Elon Musk
Summary: Elon Musk revealed on Twitter that his recent weight loss was partly due to using Novo Nordisk's Wegovy, an injectable GLP-1 drug for chronic weight management. This unexpected endorsement provides free advertising for Novo Nordisk, although it raises questions about the drug's appropriate usage. Wegovy is poised to become a blockbuster obesity drug despite potential competition from Eli Lilly's tirzepatide.

Title: 7 Things to Know About the God Bless America (YALL) ETF
Summary: The God Bless America ETF (YALL) is a new exchange-traded fund designed to invest in "anti-woke" companies that avoid "left-leaning statements" unrelated to their businesses. The ETF prioritizes valuation metrics like P/E ratios and job growth, with Tesla (TSLA) and Nvidia (NVDA) as its top holdings. It will have an expense ratio of 0.65% and hold 30-40 U.S.-listed companies with market capitalizations over $1 billion.

Title: Why Tech Won’t Give Up on Silicon Valley, Despite Rising Regulation
Summary: Despite a trend of major tech companies relocating out of California in 2020-2021 due to rising regulation, entrepreneurship in Silicon Valley continues to thrive. Companies like Palantir, Oracle, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, and Tesla moved their headquarters, sparking concerns about the region's long-standing dominance. However, the article suggests that Silicon Valley remains a vibrant hub for technological innovation.

Title: New Sony-Honda Venture to Compete in Premium EVs with Software Prowess
Summary: Sony Honda Mobility, a new venture between Sony and Honda, announced plans to deliver high-end electric vehicles (EVs) by 2026. The company aims to differentiate itself in the competitive luxury EV market by focusing on software, offering advanced features like automation, personalization, and metaverse connectivity. Despite being a latecomer, Sony Honda Mobility seeks to challenge established players like Tesla and European automakers by leveraging Sony's sensor technology and collaborative partnerships.

Title: Tesla Sales Rise, but Revenue Still Lower Than Expected
Summary: Tesla Inc. reported third-quarter revenue of $21.5 billion, falling short of analysts' estimates despite a 56% rise in sales. The company's shares declined as CEO Elon Musk acknowledged economic headwinds impacting demand and delivery challenges, though he remained confident about Q4 performance and future growth targets. Tesla is also pursuing a share buyback and building a lithium refinery to secure its supply chain.

Title: Tesla stock down on growth worries
Summary: Shares of Tesla Inc sank after Wall Street analysts expressed concerns that the electric carmaker's growth momentum may be hindered by rapid inflation and logistical challenges, causing several brokerages to cut price targets. Investors are also watching for signs of cooling consumer demand in the face of surging inflation and rising interest rates, which could impact Tesla's delivery growth targets. Despite these concerns, some analysts remain optimistic about Tesla's long-term prospects due to the global shift towards electric vehicles.

Title: Tesla cars will not be approved as fully self driving this year, Musk says
Summary: Elon Musk has stated that Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) software will not receive regulatory approval in 2022, indicating that the company cannot yet guarantee its cars can operate without human oversight. Despite plans to release an upgraded FSD software by year-end that allows for largely autonomous drives, regulatory approval is still a hurdle. Analysts suggest that the primary issues are both regulatory scrutiny from bodies like NHTSA and the inherent complexity of the autonomous driving technology itself.

Title: Industronics’ Executive Director Datuk Chu acquires around 10% of HK-based renowned stocking firm
Summary: Industronics Berhad's Executive Director, Datuk Chu Boon Tiong, has personally acquired a 10% stake in Hong Kong-based Bluemount Financial Group Limited, coinciding with Industronics' own postponed acquisition interest in the firm. Another company, Tesla Technology Holdings Limited, also acquired a 26.08% stake in Bluemount, with the condition that Bluemount apply for listing on the London Stock Exchange's Main Market by the end of the year. Datuk Chu will join Bluemount's Board of Directors to lead its expansion in Southeast Asia, focusing on asset management, fund management, and IPO services.

Title: ARK Buys the Dip in Tesla, Shows Strength in Active Management
Summary: ARK Invest's Cathie Wood increased the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK)'s position in Tesla (TSLA) by buying the dip after the stock declined to a 52-week low. This move demonstrates the advantage of active management. ARKK is an actively managed ETF that invests in companies relevant to disruptive innovation, including those in DNA technologies, automation, AI, and fintech.

Title: United Airlines, Netflix, Tesla: Stocks That Defined the Week
Summary: This article highlights seven major companies whose stocks experienced significant movement based on recent news. It specifically mentions United Airlines, Netflix, and Tesla as key players, with United Airlines showing a 2.71% increase. The piece suggests that resilient demand is expected to drive profits for companies like American Airlines through year-end, despite economic concerns.

Title: Lucid Motors opens factory in Saudi Arabia, tightening energy ties with China
Summary: Lucid Motors has opened a factory in Saudi Arabia, with the Saudi Public Investment Fund owning a majority stake. This move is part of Saudi Arabia's National Industry Strategy to diversify its economy away from oil by manufacturing 150,000 EVs by 2026. The article highlights that while Lucid may appear American, it has significant Chinese investment and aims to compete with Tesla in the Chinese market. It also touches on concerns regarding the treatment of migrant workers in Saudi Arabia's labor force.

Title: Tesla Cuts China Prices, Partly Reversing Previous Increases
Summary: Tesla has reduced prices for its electric vehicles in China, with cuts ranging from approximately 5% to 9% on its locally built Model 3 and Model Y. This move comes as competitive and economic pressures are intensifying in the Chinese market, leading to a drop in Tesla's shares to their lowest point since June of the previous year. The company's management also anticipates falling short of its growth targets for the current year.

Title: Lawsuit alleges Tesla HR, managers ignored ‘obscene and misogynistic’ music at work
Summary: A former Tesla employee has filed a lawsuit alleging that the company's HR department and managers ignored "obscene and misogynistic" music at a Nevada worksite, leading to a sexually hostile work environment. The plaintiff claims Tesla violated Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 by failing to address her repeated complaints about the music, sexual remarks, stalking, and unwanted touching, ultimately forcing her to resign. The case highlights crucial requirements for HR professionals to address harassment promptly and appropriately to avoid employer liability.

Title: Tesla Is No Longer Alone in the Electric Vehicle Race
Summary: Tesla, once the sole leader in the electric vehicle (EV) market, now faces significant competition from well-established automakers like General Motors, Ford, and Mercedes-Benz. As more than a dozen new EVs are set to launch, analysts predict Tesla's market share will decline considerably by 2025. Despite CEO Elon Musk's optimism, concerns about demand, driven by economic downturns and increased interest rates, have led to price cuts in China and left analysts uneasy about Tesla's near-term outlook.

Title: Toyota Motor unveils bZ3 all-electric sedan for Chinese market
Summary: Toyota Motor has unveiled the bZ3, its second all-electric model, developed specifically for the Chinese market in collaboration with BYD and FAW Toyota. This medium-sized sedan, featuring BYD's LFP battery and Toyota's electrification technologies, boasts a CLTC-rated range of over 600km and will compete with models like the Tesla Model 3. Its design emphasizes family comfort and aerodynamic efficiency.

Title: Creepy deepfake of Elon Musk tied up and held hostage goes viral
Summary: A deepfake video of Elon Musk tied up and held hostage, created by reAlpha Tech Corp as an advertisement, has gone viral. The real-estate startup aims to get Musk's attention to join their board, highlighting the growing concern over convincing deepfakes and their ethical implications, further underscored by Scarlett Johansson's past experiences. The video also features a photoshopped Jeff Bezos.

Title: Tesla faces U.S. criminal probe around self-driving claims
Summary: U.S. prosecutors are investigating if Tesla misled the public about its Autopilot driver assistance system's capabilities, according to Reuters reports. This criminal probe from the Justice Department's Washington and San Francisco offices began last year and is ongoing. The Autopilot feature is crucial to Tesla's marketing and customer attraction efforts, with CEO Elon Musk stating that solving full self-driving technology is critical to Tesla's valuation.

Title: Tesla faces U.S. criminal probe over self-driving car claims, sources say
Summary: Tesla is under a previously undisclosed U.S. criminal investigation regarding claims that its electric vehicles can drive themselves. The probe by the U.S. Department of Justice began last year following over a dozen crashes, some fatal, involving Tesla's Autopilot driver assistance system. Prosecutors are examining whether Tesla misled consumers, investors, and regulators about the capabilities of its technology.

Title: GM temporarily suspends advertising on Twitter following Elon Musk takeover
Summary: General Motors announced a temporary suspension of its advertising on Twitter following Elon Musk's acquisition of the social media platform. The automaker stated it is evaluating Twitter's new direction under Musk's ownership and will continue to use the platform for customer interactions but not paid advertising. Other auto companies, including Ford, Stellantis, and Rivian, are also assessing their ad strategies or have commented on their plans regarding the platform.

Title: GM pauses advertising on Twitter after Elon Musk takeover
Summary: General Motors announced it is temporarily pausing its advertising on Twitter following Elon Musk's takeover of the social media platform. The automaker stated it is evaluating Twitter's "new direction" under its new ownership but will continue to use the platform for customer interactions. This decision raises concerns among analysts about a potential wave of advertisers pulling out, which could be disastrous given advertising accounts for 92% of Twitter's revenue.

Title: Report: Tesla Cybertruck production won’t ramp up until late 2023
Summary: A new report suggests that Tesla Cybertruck production might not ramp up until late 2023, meaning mass deliveries would not begin until 2024. This follows Elon Musk's previous announcement of "early production" by mid-2023. The article details the Cybertruck's long development timeline, initial specifications and pricing, and subsequent delays.

Title: Casey’s alternative fuel choices expand; new EV charging stations
Summary: Casey’s General Stores is expanding its alternative fuel options by adding new electric vehicle charging stations and promoting biofuels. The retailer now has 134 EV chargers at 28 locations, including 11 Tesla Superchargers. This initiative is part of Casey's environmental stewardship efforts, aiming to provide more lower-carbon fuel options to its customers.

Title: Solid-state Hesai FT120 LiDAR covers blind spots on self-driving vehicles as Tesla keeps shunning radars
Summary: Hesai has launched the FT120, a solid-state LiDAR designed to cover blind spots on self-driving vehicles, contrasting with Tesla's camera-only Vision system. While Tesla believes in its camera-based approach, other EV manufacturers and experts emphasize the need for LiDAR and radars for higher levels of autonomous driving, especially in adverse weather or as a redundancy. Hesai's FT120 has already secured orders for about one million units and is slated for delivery to autonomous vehicle makers in 2023.

Title: 7 Electric Vehicle Stocks That Will Make You a Millionaire by 2030
Summary: The electric vehicle market is booming, with sales accelerating globally. This article highlights seven EV-related stocks—Tesla, Lion Electric, Albemarle, Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF, iShares Self-Driving EV and Tech ETF, Nio Inc., and General Motors—that are positioned to capitalize on this growth and potentially make investors millionaires by 2030. The author details the unique opportunities and recent performance of each stock, emphasizing their potential for significant returns.

Title: New Twitter owner Elon Musk sells almost $4 billion in Tesla stock
Summary: Elon Musk, the new owner of Twitter, sold nearly $4 billion worth of Tesla shares between November 4 and November 8, according to regulatory filings. This latest sale brings his total Tesla stock sales since April to over $19 billion, largely to finance his acquisition of Twitter. The continuous sales have drawn criticism from industry analysts, especially since Musk had previously indicated he was done selling Tesla stock.

Title: A Tailgate with Tesla comes to campus | College of Engineering and Applied Sciences
Summary: Recruiters from Tesla Inc. will host "A Tailgate with Tesla" event at Western Michigan University's College of Engineering and Applied Sciences on November 16, 2022, to connect with students for co-op, internship, and entry-level positions. Kyle Liechty, a WMU alumnus and talent partner at Tesla, emphasizes the importance of genuine self-expression and technical alignment for prospective candidates. The event aims to recruit students from various engineering disciplines to help accelerate the world's transition to sustainable energy.

Title: Tesla stock hits two-year low after boss Musk sells more shares
Summary: Tesla Inc shares have dropped to a two-year low after CEO Elon Musk sold $3.95 billion worth of shares. This sale, coupled with concerns about Musk's distraction due to his Twitter acquisition, has intensified investor jitters. Analysts are questioning Musk's credibility and urging him to refocus on Tesla amid increasing competition and production issues.

Title: Tesla stock hits 2-year low after Musk sells $4 bln worth of shares
Summary: Tesla Inc. shares dropped to a two-year low after CEO Elon Musk disclosed he sold an additional $3.95 billion worth of shares. This sale, bringing his total sales since last November to about $36 billion, intensified investor concerns about the impact of his Twitter acquisition on Tesla and his potential distraction from the automaker's operations. Analysts suggest the sales may not be over, adding to credibility issues for Musk among investors, who are already worried about a potential recession affecting Tesla's demand.

Title: Cathie Wood's ARK Innovation ETF surges 14% for its best day ever
Summary: Cathie Wood's flagship ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) experienced its best day ever, surging over 14% on Thursday following an easing inflation reading. Major holdings like Zoom Video, Tesla, Roku, and Teladoc saw significant jumps. This rally indicates a potential rebound for growth stocks if reduced price pressures lead the Federal Reserve to scale back its aggressive tightening.

Title: 3 Stocks That May Be Kicked Out of the Dow Jones Industrial Average (and the 3 Stocks That Could Replace Them)
Summary: This article discusses three companies, Walgreens Boots Alliance, Dow Inc., and Verizon Communications, that are at risk of being removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average due to their declining influence or market cap. It also proposes potential replacements: CVS Health for Walgreens, Tesla for Dow Inc., and Alphabet for Verizon, highlighting how these changes could update the index to better reflect the current economic landscape. The Dow's share price-weighted methodology means that lower-priced stocks have less influence, making these companies vulnerable.

Title: Fake account posing as pharmaceutical giant says 'insulin is free', causes stocks to plummet
Summary: Pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly & Co apologized after a fake "verified" Twitter account announced that insulin was free, causing the company's stock to drop. This incident highlights issues with Twitter's new verification policy under Elon Musk, which has led to a wave of impersonations of major brands and significant reputational risk for advertisers. The controversy led Twitter to temporarily roll back its premium service and revive "official" labels for some accounts.

Title: Truck stops will soon need the same amount of power as a small town if electrified rigs continue, study shows
Summary: A new study by National Grid Plc. indicates that the widespread adoption of electric semi-trucks will dramatically increase power demands at truck stops, requiring as much electricity as a small town by 2035. The main challenge isn't the total electricity supply, but rather the infrastructure needed to deliver high-speed charging quickly and efficiently, a process that currently takes years to build out. This infrastructure gap is a significant concern for fleets considering electrification, potentially hindering the transition to electric trucks without proactive investment and policy changes.

Title: Can GM electric vehicles turn a profit by 2025? Mary Barra is betting on it [Update]
Summary: General Motors (GM) CEO Mary Barra is confident the company's electric vehicle (EV) segment will become profitable by 2025, a goal she highlighted during an investor update. This forecast comes as GM scales its EV production and invests heavily in battery technology and manufacturing, aiming to mirror the profitability seen in pure EV companies like Tesla. The company's strategy includes launching new EV models, building battery plants, and improving margins through initiatives like a new digital platform for dealers.

Title: Trial over Tesla boss Musk’s $56bn pay package starts
Summary: A trial has begun over allegations that Elon Musk's $56bn pay package from Tesla was based on easily achievable performance targets and that investors were misled into approving it. A shareholder is attempting to prove that Musk used his influence over Tesla’s board to dictate the terms of the 2018 package, which did not require him to work full-time at the company. Musk and Tesla's directors deny the allegations, arguing that the pay package incentivized him to guide Tesla through a critical growth period.

Title: Court told Musk's $56 billion pay wasn't for punching a clock
Summary: A Delaware court heard arguments regarding Elon Musk's $56 billion Tesla pay package, with a director and former executive defending it against a shareholder's claim that Musk dictated terms. The shareholder alleges Musk used his dominance to craft the 2018 package and duped investors, while defendants argue the package incentivized Musk during a critical growth period for Tesla. The trial examines the board's latitude in setting executive compensation, especially for a controlling shareholder, and will impact the future of Musk's compensation from Tesla.

Title: Ford must bring more work in-house to preserve jobs - CEO
Summary: Ford CEO Jim Farley stated that the company needs to bring more electric vehicle component manufacturing in-house to preserve jobs, as EV production requires 40% less labor than combustion vehicles. This strategy aims to ensure "everyone has a role" in the future and improve competitiveness, similar to Tesla's integrated production approach. Farley also noted that upcoming contract talks with the United Auto Workers will focus heavily on the shift to electrification.

Title: Musk's all-nighters at Twitter raise concern for Tesla investors
Summary: Elon Musk's intense focus on Twitter, including working all-nighters at its San Francisco headquarters, is causing concern among Tesla investors about his capacity to lead the electric carmaker. Tesla's stock has dropped 50% since Musk disclosed his stake in Twitter in April, and his recent tweets have shown a significant shift in attention towards Twitter. While some supporters remain confident, others in the financial community fear Twitter has become a major distraction for Musk, negatively impacting Tesla's brand and stock performance.

Title: Tim Draper turns attention from China to Taiwan
Summary: US venture capitalist Tim Draper, an early investor in Tesla and SpaceX, has shifted his investment focus from China to Taiwan. He stated that he stopped investing in China due to early signs that it was moving away from a free market under President Xi Jinping, and he now sees Taiwan as a natural place for investment, particularly in its booming tech and semiconductor sector. Draper also expressed concerns about a potential Chinese attack on Taiwan and praised Elon Musk's ability to get things done.

Title: Elon Musk says in court that he doesn't want to be CEO of any company and tries to walk back SEC insults
Summary: In a Delaware court testimony regarding a lawsuit over his 2018 Tesla compensation, Elon Musk stated he does not want to be CEO of any company, including Tesla, and confirmed his role at Twitter is temporary. He also attempted to clarify past insults directed at the SEC, suggesting his notorious "SEC, three letter acronym, middle word is Elon's" tweet was misunderstood and meant "Save Elon's Company." Musk also defended using Tesla employees for Twitter work as voluntary, after-hours assistance.

Title: Ford fighting electric vehicle bottlenecks with industrial automation giant
Summary: Ford has partnered with industrial automation giant Rockwell to address electric vehicle (EV) manufacturing bottlenecks and accelerate its EV rollout to meet overwhelming demand. This collaboration aims to enhance Ford's production capabilities and supply chain efficiency for its next three EV assembly lines, including the Blue Oval City campus. Ford wants to become the number one EV brand, trailing only Tesla in US sales, and believes this partnership will help strengthen its manufacturing prowess.

Title: Tesla board member says Elon Musk identified potential successor as CEO
Summary: A Tesla director, James Murdoch, testified that Elon Musk has identified a potential successor as CEO in recent months, though the individual was not named. This revelation comes amid investor concerns about Musk's divided attention following his acquisition of Twitter. Previous discussions within the board also explored finding an "administrative CEO" to allow Musk to focus on product development.

Title: Musk says he made some Tesla decisions without board nod, defends $56 bln pay
Summary: Elon Musk testified in court, defending his $56 billion Tesla pay package against claims he dictated terms to the board. He acknowledged making some decisions without board approval, including ending Bitcoin acceptance and discussing stock buybacks, but denied that his pay package goals were easy to achieve. The trial centers on whether Musk exerted undue influence to secure his compensation.

Title: Musk's pay trial asks if Tesla's growth justifies $56 bln compensation
Summary: A Delaware judge is set to rule on whether Elon Musk's $56 billion pay package from Tesla was justified by the company's significant growth or if the process was flawed. The trial heard testimony from Musk and Tesla directors, who argued the package incentivized extraordinary growth and enriched shareholders. Shareholders challenging the package claim it was dictated by Musk to subservient directors and approved based on misleading information.

Title: Tesla recalls 321,000 U.S. vehicles over rear light issue
Summary: Tesla has issued a recall for over 321,000 vehicles in the U.S. due to an issue where tail lights may intermittently fail to illuminate. The recall affects certain 2023 Model 3 and 2020-2023 Model Y vehicles, and Tesla plans to address the problem with an over-the-air software update. The company has reported no crashes or injuries related to this defect.

Title: Weekly Recalls: Ford, Kia, Tesla (2)
Summary: This article details recent recalls announced by Kia, Ford, and Tesla. Kia is recalling certain 2017-2018 Niro hybrid electric vehicles due to a potential issue with the Power Relay Assembly overheating rear seats. Ford is recalling 2021-2022 F-150 vehicles for a front windshield wiper motor failure. Tesla has two recalls: one for 2021-2023 Model X vehicles due to an incorrect front passenger airbag deployment calibration and another for 2023 Model 3 and 2020-2023 Model Y vehicles concerning intermittent taillight illumination.

Title: Former Twitter Employees Sue Company Alleging WARN Act Violations
Summary: Former Twitter employees have filed a lawsuit against the company, alleging violations of both California's and the federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Acts. The lawsuit claims that Twitter failed to provide the legally required 60 days' notice before mass layoffs, impacting approximately 3,700 employees. This action seeks to prevent further unlawful layoffs and secure back pay and benefits for affected workers, though potential arbitration clauses similar to those in a Tesla case could complicate the class action.

Title: Tesla Confirmed the Cybertruck Is Made of Starship Material Supplied by Steel Dynamics
Summary: Tesla has officially confirmed that its Cybertruck is made of steel supplied by Steel Dynamics Inc. (SDI), the same company that provides material for SpaceX's Starship. This information was revealed during the "Inside Tesla: Supercharging the Electric Revolution" exhibition at the Petersen Automotive Museum, corroborating long-standing rumors. Franz von Holzhausen, Senior Design Executive at Tesla, also confirmed the accuracy of the information presented at the exhibit.

Title: YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY) Price, Holdings, & News
Summary: This article provides detailed information about the YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY), an exchange-traded fund launched in October 2022 that uses a synthetic covered call strategy on Tesla stock to generate income. It includes current pricing, key statistics such as dividend yield and expense ratio, and a list of recent news headlines regarding its weekly distributions. The article also offers insights into its holdings, major shareholders, and FAQs about its performance and how to purchase shares.

Title: TSLY Stock Fund Price and Chart — AMEX:TSLY
Summary: The YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY) aims to generate monthly income and provide exposure to Tesla (TSLA) stock price returns, subject to a cap on potential gains. Launched on November 22, 2022, TSLY uses a synthetic covered call strategy involving options and US Treasuries for collateral, but does not directly invest in TSLA stocks. The fund currently has $966.97 million in assets under management and an indicated dividend yield of 97.69%.

Title: YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF Trade Ideas — AMEX:TSLY
Summary: This article provides trade ideas and an in-depth analysis of the YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY). It details how TSLY generates income by selling TSLA options for premium, aiming for high dividend yields, and explains the mechanics of synthetic stock leverage. The article also outlines the risks and advantages of investing in TSLY, including its high yield, capital gain limitations, and sensitivity to TSLA's performance and volatility.

Title: Technical Analysis of YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (AMEX:TSLY)
Summary: This article provides a technical analysis of the YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY) based on various indicators. It details the summary of oscillators, moving averages, and pivots, categorizing them into buy, sell, or neutral signals. The overall technical rating for TSLY is currently a strong sell, emphasizing that this information is not investment advice and market conditions can change.

Title: Tesla's Full Self-Driving Beta now available to all in N. America, Musk says
Summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla's Full Self-Driving Beta software is now available to all North American customers who have purchased the option. This release comes as the automaker seeks regulatory approval for vehicles to operate without human oversight, with Musk hoping an FSD update in 2023 will demonstrate its safety advantage over human drivers. The $15,000 FSD add-on allows autonomous lane changes and parking, supplementing the standard Autopilot feature, while the company faces a U.S. Department of Justice investigation regarding claims its EVs can drive themselves.

Title: Tesla owners are keeping GM service techs busy
Summary: Tesla owners are reportedly bringing their vehicles to General Motors service centers for maintenance and repairs, keeping GM technicians busy. This article, published by Automotive News, highlights a surprising trend in the auto service industry.

Title: Tesla is still dominant, but its U.S. market share is eroding as cheaper EVs arrive
Summary: Tesla remains the top-selling electric vehicle brand in the U.S., but its market share is declining as more affordable EV models from competitors enter the market. S&P Global Mobility reports Tesla's U.S. market share of new registered EVs was 65% through Q3, down from 71% last year, and forecasts it will drop to under 20% by 2025. This shift is attributed to the proliferation of cheaper alternatives with comparable technology.

Title: No, you can’t buy a self-driving car yet, but a lot of people seem to think you can
Summary: Despite widespread misconceptions, fully self-driving cars (Level 3-5 autonomy) are not yet available for purchase in Canada or the U.S. Many consumers mistakenly believe that current driver-assist technologies, like Tesla's Autopilot or GM's Super Cruise (which are Level 2), provide full self-driving capabilities, leading to dangerous misuse. Experts emphasize that drivers must remain attentive as these systems are only aids and not replacements for human operators, and more advanced systems are still in limited testing or decades away.

Title: Tesla EV battery packs repurposed into energy storage systems in Finland and California
Summary: Two companies, Smartville Inc. in California and Cactos in Finland, are repurposing Tesla EV battery packs into energy storage systems. Smartville received a US$6 million grant to commercialize its systems, while Cactos raised €2.5 million to expand production of its behind-the-meter ESS product. Both companies are scaling their operations to meet the growing demand for energy storage, with Smartville focusing on entire battery packs and Cactos using both second-life and new batteries to manage supply and demand.

Title: Spotify, Epic Games get ally in Musk in fight against Apple fees
Summary: Elon Musk has joined Spotify and Epic Games in criticizing Apple's 30% App Store fees, even suggesting Apple threatened to remove Twitter from its store. This stance strengthens the position of companies previously involved in antitrust complaints and lawsuits against Apple over its in-app purchase policies. Analysts are concerned that Musk's battle with Apple could deter Twitter users, as people are unlikely to abandon their iPhones.

Title: Tesla Delivers Semi Trucks to PepsiCo, Expanding Beyond Passenger Vehicles
Summary: Tesla Inc. delivered its first all-electric semitrailer trucks to PepsiCo Inc. on Thursday, marking a significant expansion beyond its traditional passenger vehicle market. This delivery comes five years after Elon Musk initially revealed the Semi model, which was originally due out in 2019. The Semi represents the first new model Tesla has put into customer hands since early 2020.

Title: Tesla to issue software updates for 435,000 cars in China over marker light issue
Summary: Tesla will issue software updates for over 435,000 vehicles in China to fix an issue with side marker lights that could potentially lead to collisions. This fix is considered a recall and will be implemented via an over-the-air update, affecting Model 3 and Model Y cars. This follows a previous recall for over 80,000 vehicles in China for other software and seat belt issues.

Title: Ford claims No. 2 spot in EVs behind Tesla – but gap remains wide
Summary: Ford has claimed the No. 2 spot in U.S. electric vehicle sales, surpassing Hyundai/Kia, though it remains a distant second to market leader Tesla. Despite this achievement, the gap with Tesla is significant, and Ford's overall November sales were down. Tesla's market share in EVs is decreasing as more competitors enter the market, with General Motors also aiming to overtake Tesla in EV sales by mid-decade.

Title: Workhorse Group Inc. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
Summary: Workhorse Group Inc. (WKHS) stock increased by 4.31% on Friday, closing at $2.42, outperforming both the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the NASDAQ Composite Index. This marked the third consecutive day of gains for the company's stock, though it remained $3.17 below its 52-week high. The stock also outperformed competitors like Tesla Inc. while General Motors Co. declined.

Title: Tesla expands with the first electric Semi-truck to PepsiCo
Summary: Five years after its prototype reveal, Tesla delivered its first electric Semi-truck to PepsiCo\'s Frito-Lay in Modesto, California. PepsiCo has reserved 100 trucks and plans to deploy 15 by year-end, aiming to reduce fuel costs and emissions. Tesla CEO Elon Musk projects significant cargo transportation cost decreases and safety boosts, with a tentative plan to produce 50,000 Semis for North America in 2024.

Title: Janitors set up picket line after being fired by Twitter in latest attack by billionaire owner Musk
Summary: Janitors at Twitter's San Francisco headquarters began picketing after being fired without notice due to a terminated contract with their building maintenance contractor, FlagShip. The 48 affected janitorial workers, members of SEIU Local 87, are demanding rehire and compensation, highlighting that San Francisco law often requires existing workers to be hired for 90 days after a contractor switch. This incident is the latest in a series of workforce reductions and changes at Twitter following Elon Musk's acquisition, which has included significant layoffs and a demand for an "extremely hardcore" work environment.

Title: Tesla launches EVs in Thailand amid competition from cheaper brands
Summary: Tesla Inc. has launched two electric vehicle models in Thailand, marking its first entry into the market previously dominated by Japanese automakers. The move comes as Thailand promotes EV adoption through tax cuts and subsidies, but Tesla faces strong competition from Chinese brands offering more affordable options. Tesla did not disclose sales targets, as Thailand aims for 30% of its vehicle production to be electric by 2030.

Title: Tesla to suspend Model Y output in Shanghai in last week of Dec-memo
Summary: Tesla plans to suspend Model Y production at its Shanghai plant between December 25 and January 1, reducing output by about 30% for the month. This planned suspension is unusual for the factory, which usually operates normally at year-end, and follows earlier reports of production cuts due to elevated inventory levels. Despite record sales in November and recent price cuts, weakening demand and increased inventory in China appear to be factors for the adjustment.

Title: Exclusive: Toyota to outline 3-year EV plan changes to suppliers
Summary: Toyota Motor Corp is set to announce adjustments to its electric vehicle strategy to major suppliers early next year, aiming to compete more effectively with industry leaders like Tesla and BYD on price and performance. The changes, which cover the period until early 2026, include accelerating the adoption of performance-enhancing technologies for EVs and potentially delaying some original development programs. Toyota is also reviewing its e-TNGA platform, considering a dedicated EV platform instead, to improve cost performance and technology in the rapidly expanding EV market.

Title: GM, Stellantis rank as worst automakers for fuel efficiency, even amid EV push, EPA says
Summary: General Motors and Stellantis were identified by the EPA as having the worst average estimated real-world fuel economy and highest carbon emissions among major automakers for the 2021 model year. Both companies saw a decline in fuel efficiency and an increase in CO2 emissions since 2016. This report comes as the Biden administration pushes for a transition to electric vehicles, with GM aiming for an all-electric consumer fleet by 2035, despite their current fleet's poor efficiency.

Title: Tesla Investors Voice Concern Over Elon Musk’s Focus on Twitter
Summary: Tesla investors are increasingly concerned that Elon Musk's focus on Twitter is negatively impacting the electric-vehicle maker. The company's stock is headed for its worst full-year performance amidst Musk's controversial takeover of Twitter. A major investor even tweeted that "There is no TSLA CEO today," reflecting the growing anxieties.

Title: GraniteShares goes live with three leveraged single stock ETFs on NASDAQ
Summary: GraniteShares has launched three new leveraged single-stock ETFs on the NASDAQ Stock Exchange, offering sophisticated investors 1.5x to 1.75x long exposure to Meta, Alibaba, and Nvidia. This expansion builds on GraniteShares' existing leveraged ETF offerings for Tesla, Coinbase, and Apple and aims to make leveraged single-company exposure, previously confined to specialists, accessible to a broader range of investors. Having pioneered the single-stock ETF market in Europe, GraniteShares is now bringing its expertise and popular product range to the U.S. market.

Title: Elon Musk sold $3.6 billion more in Tesla stock, stoking fear that the carmaker is his ‘ATM’
Summary: Elon Musk has sold an additional $3.6 billion in Tesla stock, raising fears among investors that he is using the carmaker as a personal "ATM" to fund his other ventures, particularly Twitter. This latest sale of nearly 22 million shares occurred between December 12 and December 14, causing Tesla shares to drop by 12.4% over three trading sessions. The ongoing stock sales and Musk's involvement with Twitter continue to be concerns for Tesla investors regarding operational and financial distractions.

Title: What is Tesla?
Summary: This article provides an overview of Tesla, detailing its history, product lines, and key figures. It covers the company's founding, its role as a pioneer in electric vehicles and energy storage, and the current ownership structure with Elon Musk as the largest shareholder. The article also addresses reasons for the recent decline in TSLA stock price, attributing it to investor concerns about Elon Musk's involvement with Twitter and his sale of Tesla shares.

Title: 2023 Kia EV6 GT Review: Affordable All-Electric Performance
Summary: The 2023 Kia EV6 GT is reviewed as an affordable, high-performance all-electric SUV that excels in power, handling, and fun. It outperforms competitors like the Ford Mustang Mach-E GT Performance Edition and Tesla Model Y Long Range in acceleration and driving engagement, while also being significantly less expensive. Despite some comfort compromises in the cabin, the EV6 GT offers substantial performance thrills both on the street and track.

Title: PepsiCo to roll out 100 Tesla Semis in 2023 for deliveries
Summary: PepsiCo plans to deploy 100 heavy-duty Tesla Semis in 2023 for deliveries to major customers like Walmart and Kroger. The company is investing significantly in infrastructure, including charging stalls, supported by state grants and federal subsidies. Initially, the trucks will haul lightweight Frito-Lay products for longer distances and sodas for shorter routes, with plans to expand beverage delivery ranges as well.

Title: Elon Musk’s troubling week pushes Tesla investors closer to the edge
Summary: Elon Musk's controversial actions and management of Twitter have led to a significant 16 percent drop in Tesla's stock price over the last five sessions, marking its worst week since March 2020. Prominent Wall Street analysts have reduced their expectations for Tesla, and concerns about the economy and potential recession are expected to further impact demand for electric vehicles. This decline has pushed Tesla's market value below $500 billion, and analysts warn of further risks due to valuation and Musk's preoccupation with Twitter.

Title: Ford Motor has once again raised prices for the third time this year
Summary: Ford Motor Company has increased the price of its F-150 Lightning Pro for the third time this year, raising the base model's MSRP by $16,000 to $55,974. The company attributes these price hikes to rising material costs, similar to other EV manufacturers like Tesla, Lucid, and Rivian. Despite the increases, Ford plans to expand production and anticipates increased demand due to the Inflation Reduction Act's tax benefits for electric commercial vehicles.

Title: Tech short-sellers make $12bn betting against Tesla in 2022
Summary: In 2022, short-sellers profited nearly $50 billion from betting against tech stocks, with Tesla being the most profitable target at $11.7 billion. This trend reflects a market shift from bullish to bearish, driven by high inflation and rising interest rates, leading to significant stock price declines for major tech companies like Amazon, Meta, and Apple. Despite the substantial sell-off, some analysts predict continued opportunities for short-sellers as tech valuations remain relatively high compared to historical averages.

Title: Tesla (TSLA) Illegally Fired Workers for Criticizing Elon Musk, Complaints Claim
Summary: Tesla is accused of illegally firing two California employees for criticizing CEO Elon Musk, according to complaints filed with the National Labor Relations Board. The employees were involved in drafting letters that objected to Musk's return-to-office policy and his tweets, which they claimed violated company policy. The filings suggest that these terminations were in violation of labor laws protecting employees' right to engage in such discussions.

Title: Tesla fired workers for criticizing Musk, company policies, say new complaints
Summary: Tesla is facing new complaints alleging the company illegally fired two employees for their involvement in drafting letters critical of the company and CEO Elon Musk. The workers claim their firings were intended to discourage other employees from speaking up about working conditions and company policies. Similar claims have been filed against SpaceX, another company owned by Musk.

Title: New YieldMax ETFs Seek Covered Call Strategies on Tesla and ARKK
Summary: Tidal Financial Group has launched two new actively managed ETFs, YieldMax TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (TSLY) and YieldMax Innovation Option Income Strategy ETF (OARK), which employ a synthetic covered call strategy on Tesla (TSLA) and the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), respectively. These ETFs aim to generate monthly income for investors by capitalizing on the volatility of the underlying assets. This launch marks the first in a series of yield-producing ETFs under the YieldMax brand.

Title: Tesla falls on growing angst over Musk's focus on Twitter
Summary: Tesla shares fell nearly 6% after several brokerages cut price targets due to concerns over Elon Musk's focus on Twitter. Analysts fear Musk may need to sell more Tesla shares to fund Twitter, and the social media acquisition could harm Tesla's brand. This comes amid weakening demand in China and ahead of Tesla's quarterly deliveries report.

Title: Purpose pushes through with yield-focused single-stock ETFs
Summary: Purpose Investments has launched its initial suite of Yield Shares ETFs, which are single-stock, yield-focused ETFs. These world-first ETFs allow Canadian investors to gain exposure to individual stocks like Tesla and Apple while receiving enhanced monthly distributions through a covered-call options strategy and moderate leverage. The ETFs also address an advisor pain point by simplifying the process of generating augmented income from individual stocks and offer Canadian dollar-denominated exposure to U.S. stocks with currency hedging.

Title: S&P Global Mobility Makes 2023 Light Vehicle Sales Forecast
Summary: S&P Global Mobility forecasts global new light vehicle sales to reach nearly 83.6 million units in 2023, a 5.6% increase year-over-year, despite ongoing supply chain challenges, economic deterioration, and fading pent-up demand. The forecast remains cautious due to factors like semiconductor disruption, the Russia-Ukraine war, and an intensifying affordability squeeze. Electrification is expected to grow significantly, with battery electric vehicles projected to hit almost 10 million units in 2023.

Title: I drove hundreds of miles 'hands-free' in GM, Ford and Tesla cars – here's how it went
Summary: This article details a CNBC reporter's experiences test-driving the "hands-free" advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) from Tesla, General Motors, and Ford. While none of the systems are fully autonomous, the author found GM's Super Cruise to be the most consistent and best-performing on highways, followed by Ford's BlueCruise which still has areas for improvement, especially with curves and construction. Tesla's FSD Beta is noted as the most ambitious but also the most "nerve-wracking" on city streets, with communication issues and challenges in complex driving scenarios.

Title: Tesla owners didn’t buy a car: We bought a set of beliefs Elon is trashing
Summary: The author, a Tesla owner, argues that buying a Tesla was an investment in a set of beliefs and a brand dedicated to doing good in the world, not just a car. However, Elon Musk's recent behavior, particularly since his acquisition of Twitter, has undermined these beliefs, causing disillusionment and embarrassment among many loyal customers and investors. The article details how Musk's erratic actions and political pandering are jeopardizing the strong brand loyalty Tesla had cultivated and leading to financial and emotional divestment from the company and its mission.

Title: Micron To Reduce Workforce By Almost 5,000 Due to Plunging Demand
Summary: Micron Technology Inc. announced it will cut 10% of its workforce, impacting nearly 4,800 positions, and suspend 2023 bonuses due to a significant downturn in demand for semiconductors and soaring inventories. The company reported a $195 million net loss in the first quarter of its 2023 fiscal year and expects rebalancing of customer inventory levels by mid-2023. This move follows similar workforce reductions by other tech giants like Meta and Snap amid a slowing global economy and inflation-related concerns.

Title: Tesla Dangles $7,500 Discount in Rare Move to Boost Deliveries
Summary: Tesla is offering a rare $7,500 discount on its Model 3 and Model Y vehicles for deliveries taken before year-end, signaling potential struggles with demand. This discount is double what was offered earlier in the month and aligns with anticipated changes in US tax credit eligibility for consumers. The move represents a departure from Elon Musk's previous stance against discounts and advertising.

Title: The Tesla struggle is so real that the company is offering a $7,500 discount on cars—with one big catch
Summary: Tesla is offering a rare $7,500 discount on its Model 3 and Model Y vehicles for customers taking delivery before the end of the year. This unusual move, departing from Elon Musk's long-standing no-discounts policy, suggests the automaker is facing demand challenges. The discount coincides with new federal EV tax credit guidance, which is expected to make many EVs eligible for the full $7,500 credit in early 2023, effectively accelerating a tax credit that buyers would likely receive next year.

Title: Will XPeng's $140,000 Electric Flying Car Become the 'Tesla of the Flying Vehicle Industry'?
Summary: XPeng's urban air mobility (UAM) business, AeroHT, demonstrated its gull-winged electric flying car, which could enter commercial production by 2025 with an estimated cost of $140,000. Unlike many eVTOLs, AeroHT's sixth-generation model is also a drivable car intended for road use over 90% of the time, flying only when necessary. The company aims to overcome regulatory hurdles and capture a share of the trillion-dollar urban air mobility market, with investors hoping it becomes the "Tesla of the flying car industry."

Title: Elon Musk says he will not sell more Tesla stock for about two years
Summary: Elon Musk has stated he will not sell any more Tesla (TSLA.O) stock for approximately two years, anticipating a "serious recession" in 2023. This announcement comes amid a significant sell-off of Tesla shares due to concerns about softening demand and Musk's focus on Twitter. Tesla shares rose in after-hours trading following his comments despite previous instances where Musk sold stock after similar pledges.

Title: Tesla ups its discount on Model 3 and Model Y to $7,500
Summary: Tesla has increased its discount on the Model 3 and Model Y to $7,500, following an earlier $3,750 discount, and is also offering 10,000 miles of free Supercharging. This move comes after significant price hikes earlier in the year and may be influenced by lagging demand and high inventory despite record vehicle deliveries. The $7,500 figure is notably the potential maximum federal EV tax credit amount for next year, though its applicability to Tesla vehicles after January is uncertain as new guidelines are expected.

Title: Elon Musk's vow to not sell more Tesla stock fails to calm investors
Summary: Elon Musk's pledge not to sell more Tesla stock for two years failed to reassure investors, as shares hit a new two-year low. This comes after Musk previously sold $40 billion worth of shares, partly to fund his acquisition of Twitter, despite similar past pledges. Investors are concerned about Musk's focus on Twitter and his history of issues with the SEC.

Title: Tesla stopped reporting its Autopilot safety numbers online. Why?
Summary: Tesla ceased reporting its Autopilot safety statistics online in 2021, around the same time the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) began collecting and releasing its own data. Critics suggest Tesla stopped reporting because its safety record, based on NHTSA numbers, appears to have worsened significantly compared to its sales growth and rivals like Ford and GM. The article also highlights the controversial nature of Tesla's past safety reports and the distinction between Autopilot and the more advanced, aspirational Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature, emphasizing that even FSD requires full human attention.

Title: Cox Automotive Forecast: U.S. Auto Sales Expected to Finish 2022 Down 8% Year Over Year, as General Motors Reclaims Top Spot, Honda and Nissan Fall Significantly
Summary: Cox Automotive forecasts that U.S. new-vehicle sales for 2022 will end at 13.9 million units, an 8% decrease from 2021, marking the lowest sales volume in a decade. While December sales saw a slight increase due to improved inventory, the full-year decline reflects challenges in both supply and, increasingly, demand, particularly exacerbated by rising interest rates and affordability concerns. General Motors is expected to reclaim the top sales spot from Toyota, while Honda and Nissan experienced significant declines, and Hyundai, Kia, and Tesla gained market share.

Title: Tesla shares extend losses on demand worries in China
Summary: Tesla shares fell sharply after a Reuters report indicated the company plans a reduced production schedule in January at its Shanghai plant due to demand concerns in China. Investors are also worried about CEO Elon Musk's time commitment to Twitter and his recent share sales, contributing to the stock's significant decline.

Title: ERTH: Holding Up Well Despite Tesla Tanking (NYSEARCA:ERTH)
Summary: The Invesco MSCI Sustainable Future ETF (ERTH) is a sustainability-focused fund with global holdings, which has demonstrated resilience despite a high concentration in electric vehicle stocks like Tesla. The article suggests that the ETF's diversification strategy has been effective in mitigating downside risks for investors interested in higher-risk asset classes. The author highlights the fund's broad range of holdings focused on sustainable operations and technologies, including unexpected top-10 holdings in net-zero focused data centers.

Title: Musk tells Tesla workers not to be 'bothered by stock market craziness'
Summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla Inc., urged employees not to be concerned by the company's significant stock decline, which saw shares fall nearly 70% this year amidst demand jitters and his involvement with Twitter. In an email, Musk expressed his belief that Tesla will ultimately be the most valuable company globally and pushed staff to prioritize deliveries to close out the quarter. This appeal came as analysts cut price targets for Tesla, forecasting a shift from supply exceeding demand to demand exceeding supply in 2023.

Title: Occidental and Enphase Were Top Performing Stocks in 2022. Tesla Wasn't Last.
Summary: The article identifies Occidental Petroleum as the top-performing stock in the S&P 500 for 2022, marking the end of a volatile year for the stock market. It suggests that while the year was challenging, there were still companies that saw significant gains, with Occidental leading the pack. This highlights the divergent performances within the market despite overall volatility.

Title: Tesla Poised for Delivery Record Despite Demand Concerns
Summary: Tesla is expected to announce record quarterly deliveries despite investor concerns over inflation, rising interest rates, and softening demand. The company offered a $7,500 discount and free Supercharging to U.S. customers at year-end, coinciding with the upcoming restoration of federal tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act. Analysts estimate fourth-quarter deliveries to be around 421,000 units.

Title: Warren Buffett Surpassed Jeff Bezos in Wealth, May Overtake Bill Gates
Summary: Warren Buffett has surpassed Jeff Bezos in wealth this year and is nearing Bill Gates' net worth, potentially making him the second-richest American after Elon Musk. This shift is attributed to the strong performance of Berkshire Hathaway stock compared to the declines seen in tech giants like Amazon, Microsoft, and Tesla. Despite significant charitable donations, Buffett's conservative investment strategy has proven resilient in the current economic climate, attracting investors away from growth stocks.

Title: GM opens EV fulfillment centers. Here's how they affect dealers, buyers
Summary: General Motors has launched EV fulfillment centers to streamline the delivery of electric vehicles, beginning with Chevrolet Bolts, aiming to get products to customers faster and save costs for both GM and dealerships. While some dealers initially feared this move might mimic Tesla's direct sales model, top dealers and experts see it as a strategic partnership to enhance the customer experience, reduce overhead for retailers, and improve market competitiveness. These centers promise faster order fulfillment, with GM President Mark Reuss stating deliveries can be made in as little as four days, and are expected to save the company $2,000 per unit, leveraging cloud data and machine learning for optimal inventory management.

Title: GM's Barra goes quiet on Twitter following rival Musk's takeover
Summary: General Motors and its CEO, Mary Barra, significantly reduced their Twitter activity, including halting advertising, after Elon Musk completed his acquisition of the platform. This move is attributed to concerns over data management and advertising strategies, particularly since Musk also owns rival electric vehicle maker Tesla. While GM's main brands and Barra have gone quiet, some parts of GM, such as the BrightDrop electric van business and Cruise, and other automakers like Ford, continue to use Twitter.

Title: What the Stock Split by Google’s Parent, Alphabet, Means - WSJ
Summary: Alphabet announced a 20-for-1 stock split, its first since 2014, making its shares more accessible to individual investors. This move follows similar actions taken by Apple and Tesla since the pandemic, signaling a renewed interest in stock splits among major tech companies. The split will apply to all three classes of Alphabet stock.

Title: The AP Interview: GM’s Barra talks electric vehicles, future
Summary: General Motors CEO Mary Barra is confident the company will surpass Tesla in U.S. electric vehicle sales by mid-decade, despite economic challenges like inflation, rising interest rates, and chip shortages. GM plans to introduce more affordable EVs, including a Chevrolet Equinox SUV for around $30,000, and aims to offer 30 battery-powered vehicles globally by 2025. Barra also discussed GM's strategy for battery cost reduction, expanding charging infrastructure, and navigating geopolitical challenges and social issues.

Title: GM tells remote workers to ‘pivot’ in return-to-office mandate
Summary: General Motors has mandated that its corporate employees return to the office three days a week, requiring remote workers to "pivot to a more regular in-person work cycle." This decision aligns GM with other major corporations like Apple and Peloton, which have also implemented return-to-office policies since Labor Day. The move contrasts with more flexible policies from companies such as Ford and Mitsubishi, as well as Tesla's CEO Elon Musk's strict in-office requirement.

Title: Tesla Says Company Sold a Record 1.3 Million Vehicles Last Year, Falls Short of 50% Growth Pledge
Summary: Tesla announced it sold a record 1.3 million vehicles in 2022, a 40% increase year-over-year, but this figure still fell short of CEO Elon Musk's ambitious 50% growth target for the company. The shortfall occurred despite significant year-end discounts and challenges like rising COVID-19 cases in China impacting production. The company also faces increasing competition and criticism regarding Musk's focus on Twitter, which contributed to a substantial decline in Tesla's stock value last year.

Title: Tesla stock suffers worst-ever year in 2022 despite deliveries hitting record high
Summary: Tesla's stock experienced its worst year in 2022, plummeting 65% despite recording an all-time high of 1.3 million vehicle deliveries. This decline was attributed to logistical challenges, fears of slowing demand, Elon Musk's stock offloading, and his acquisition of Twitter. Analysts project improved logistics and continued delivery growth in 2023, though concerns about demand amid economic slowdowns persist.

Title: Tuesday's ETF with Unusual Volume: IWL
Summary: The iShares Russell Top 200 ETF (IWL) experienced unusually high trading volume on Tuesday, with shares down about 0.8%. Tesla and Apple, major components of the ETF, saw significant trading volume and share price drops, while PayPal Holdings performed best, rising 4.3%.

Title: Report: South Korea fines Tesla $2.2M over cold-weather range
Summary: South Korea has fined Tesla 2.85 billion won ($2.2 million) for allegedly misleading consumers about the driving range of its electric vehicles, particularly concerning performance in cold weather. The Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) found that Tesla's website did not adequately disclose the significant range reduction—up to 50.5%—that its EVs experience in cold temperatures. This decision follows a 2021 finding by a consumer advocacy group highlighting similar issues with EV range in winter conditions in South Korea.

Title: The ARK Innovation ETF: Tesla Is Cathie Wood’s Latest Problem
Summary: The ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) is experiencing a difficult start to 2023, largely due to the continued selloff of Tesla Inc. (TSLA) stock, its most heavily weighted investment. Despite averaging down on Tesla, its weighting in ARKK has decreased to 6.6%, though overconcentration remains a concern for the fund.

Title: Tesla's stock lost over $700 billion in value. Elon Musk's Twitter deal didn't help
Summary: Tesla's stock plummeted by 65% in 2022, losing over $700 billion in value due to a tough year for the auto industry, increased competition in the EV market, and investor concerns over Elon Musk's distraction with his Twitter acquisition. Despite the significant stock drop, Tesla still leads the EV market and remains the world's most valuable automaker. The article highlights that while Tesla's sales volume will likely continue to grow, the stock market is re-evaluating its valuation from a tech company to an auto manufacturer.

Title: XPeng stock just misses a record selloff, snaps 5-day win streak
Summary: XPeng Inc. (XPEV) stock plunged nearly 15% to close at $10.11, narrowly missing its record one-day drop. This selloff broke a five-day win streak for the company's U.S.-listed shares. The decline was attributed to negative sentiment among China-based electric vehicle makers following Tesla Inc.'s price cuts in China.

Title: Pepsi turns on Tesla semis
Summary: PepsiCo plans to deploy 100 heavy-duty Tesla Semis in 2023 for deliveries to customers such as Walmart and Kroger, becoming the first company to extensively use these electric trucks. The company is purchasing the Semis outright and investing in charging infrastructure at its California plants, partially supported by state grants and federal subsidies. This move marks PepsiCo's commitment to reducing its environmental impact through early adoption of electric truck technology.

Title: Tesla: what 2023 holds for the electric vehicle company and why it might be time for Musk to go
Summary: Despite Tesla's strong financial performance and advanced technology, its market leadership is threatened by increasing competition and challenges like production delays and software recalls. The article suggests that CEO Elon Musk's divided attention between Tesla and Twitter, coupled with his controversial management style, could become a liability for Tesla, indicating a need for the company to mature beyond its "sales only" approach and possibly for a change in leadership.

Title: Disney asks employees to work from office four days a week - CNBC
Summary: Walt Disney Co.'s top boss, Bob Iger, has mandated that employees return to corporate offices four days a week starting March 1, as reported by CNBC. This move aligns Disney with other companies like Snap, Tesla, and Uber, which are also asking employees to return to the office after widespread remote work during the pandemic. The decision follows Iger's return as CEO and coincides with Disney's efforts to boost investor confidence and profitability in its streaming media unit.

Title: Tesla to spend $775 million expanding its Gigafactory Texas electric vehicle plant near Austin
Summary: Tesla plans to invest $775 million in expanding its Gigafactory Texas, located near Austin. The expansion will include new facilities like a cathode facility, cell test lab, die shop, drive unit, and an undisclosed 693,093-square-foot facility, with construction starting soon and continuing into early 2024. This growth initiative comes after a challenging year for Tesla's stock and ongoing production struggles at the factory, despite Elon Musk's efforts to build his Texas-based empire.

Title: Tesla slashes prices on new electric vehicle models in the U.S.
Summary: Tesla has significantly cut prices on its new electric vehicle models in the U.S., including the Model 3, Y, X, and S. These price reductions could enable some buyers to qualify for the $7,500 federal tax credit and come as the company faces declining market share and a "significant demand problem," with its stock dropping 65% in 2022. While some investors see the price cuts as a way to boost volume amidst growing competition, others worry about a potential pricing war and Musk's divided attention with Twitter.

Title: Tesla cuts prices across the board up to 20%
Summary: Tesla has announced significant price cuts across its entire model lineup, with some reductions as high as 20%. The Model Y received the largest cut, bringing its effective price for many U.S. buyers below $47,000 after tax credits, which could be a strategic move to qualify for new clean-vehicle tax credits. These price adjustments reverse years of increases and come amidst softening demand for used Teslas and increasing competition in the EV market, despite a record sales year for the brand in 2022.

Title: Ev Charging Stations Market to See Massive Growth by 2028 | Siemens, Tesla, Schneider Electric
Summary: A new research study by HTF MI evaluates the Worldwide EV Charging Stations Market, forecasting massive growth by 2028. The report provides an in-depth analysis of market trends, growth drivers, technologies, and investment structures, segmenting the market by residential and commercial applications, as well as AC and DC charging stations. Key players analyzed include ABB, Tesla, Schneider Electric, and Siemens, with a focus on market share, size, and future growth outlook across various global regions.

Title: Chinese EV maker Xpeng joins Tesla, Seres in price cuts
Summary: Chinese automaker Xpeng announced price cuts for several of its electric vehicle models, including its best-selling P7 sedan, P5 sedan, and G3i SUVs. This move follows similar price reductions by Tesla and Seres, intensifying competition and fueling expectations of a wider price war in China's EV market. Xpeng aims to make intelligent vehicles more accessible and will offer free extended maintenance services as compensation to existing car owners who purchased before the cuts.

Title: Xpeng Follows Tesla With Major Price Cuts on China Electric Cars
Summary: Xpeng Inc. has joined the electric vehicle price war in China by reducing the prices of its models by up to 12.5%. This move follows Tesla's earlier price cuts at the beginning of the year. The price of Xpeng's G3i SUV dropped significantly, while the P7 sedan also saw price reductions, though the G9 model remained unchanged.

Title: 2023 Tesla Model Y Review, Ratings, Specs, Prices, and Photos
Summary: The 2023 Tesla Model Y is an electric crossover SUV praised for its excellent range, performance, and spacious interior, but sometimes criticized for inconsistent build quality and styling. It offers Long Range and Performance versions with impressive acceleration and efficiency, high safety ratings, and a minimalist interior centered around a 15-inch touchscreen. While its "Full Self-Driving" mode is noted as a misnomer, the vehicle provides good value, especially in its Long Range variant, compared to other electric crossovers.

Title: Tesla video promoting self-driving was staged, engineer testifies
Summary: A senior Tesla engineer testified that a 2016 video promoting the company's self-driving technology was staged, showcasing features like stopping at red lights and accelerating at green lights that the system did not possess at the time. This testimony, given in a lawsuit concerning a fatal 2018 crash, confirmed that the video was produced at Elon Musk's request to demonstrate "what was possible to build into the system" rather than what was available to customers. Tesla is currently facing lawsuits and a criminal investigation over its driver assistance claims.

Title: Silicon Valley 2.0? 5 US cities that could be the new tech start-up central
Summary: Several southern US cities are emerging as new tech hubs, drawing companies like Tesla, Apple, Oracle, Microsoft, and Google away from California's Silicon Valley. High tax rates, labor costs, regulations, and a declining quality of life in Silicon Valley are pushing these companies to look for more affordable and business-friendly environments in states such as Texas, Arizona, Georgia, and Florida. These new tech centers offer incentives, lower costs of living, and new luxury residential developments to accommodate the influx of workers.

Title: Should You Invest in the iShares U.S. Consumer Discretionary ETF (IYC)?
Summary: This article evaluates the iShares U.S. Consumer Discretionary ETF (IYC) as an investment option. It details IYC's objective to track the consumer discretionary sector, its expense ratio, top holdings like Amazon, Home Depot, and Tesla, and its performance. The article also provides alternatives such as the Vanguard Consumer Discretionary ETF (VCR) and the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY).

Title: ‘The Nasdaq is our favorite short.’ This market strategist sees recession and a credit crunch slamming stocks in 2023.
Summary: Hedgeye CEO Keith McCullough predicts a U.S. corporate profit recession and credit crunch in 2023, causing a slide in the S&P 500, junk bonds, and previous market favorites like Tesla. McCullough, who has been critical of the Federal Reserve's handling of inflation and interest rates, recommends investors consider gold, silver, and defensive ETFs as a hedge. He views the Nasdaq as a prime short opportunity due to these anticipated market conditions.

Title: Bad Week of Earnings Pulls Q4 Growth Rate Lower
Summary: The S&P 500's blended EPS growth for Q4 decreased to -4.6% due to a week of mixed earnings reports from major financial institutions and other companies. This marks the lowest growth rate in over two years, driven by factors like increased loan loss provisions and consumer credit deterioration. Despite the decline, the earnings season is picking up, with key companies like Microsoft, Tesla, IBM, and Intel expected to report, and some companies like Danaher and Weyerhaeuser signaling positive results.

Title: Stocks Making the Biggest Moves After Hours: Tesla, Chevron, ServiceNow, Levi Strauss, IBM and More
Summary: This article details the after-hours stock movements of several major companies following their latest earnings reports. Tesla saw a slight rise despite volatile trading, while Chevron's shares advanced after announcing a large stock repurchasing program. ServiceNow tumbled, and IBM fell despite beating forecasts due to job cuts, while Levi Strauss and Las Vegas Sands both experienced gains.

Title: STMicroelectronics Tops Estimates. The Tesla Supplier’s Stock Is Rising.
Summary: STMicroelectronics, a European chip maker and Tesla supplier, saw its stock rise after reporting profit and revenue that exceeded analyst expectations. The company also announced plans to invest approximately $4 billion in capital spending to boost its manufacturing capacity this year.

Title: Used Tesla Prices Take a Dive; Should I Buy One?
Summary: Used Tesla prices have been declining significantly since their peak in July, a trend that accelerated recently and was likely influenced by Tesla's new-car price cuts. While new Teslas are also more affordable, the new federal EV tax credit rules complicate eligibility for both new and used EV purchases. Shoppers considering a used Tesla should weigh the decreasing prices against tax credit limitations, battery degradation, and fluctuating inventory levels.

Title: Ford slashes cost of EVs as it plans to boost production of Mustang Mach-E
Summary: Ford announced it is cutting the prices of its electric vehicles, including the Mustang Mach-E, to remain competitive in the market, following similar price reductions by Tesla. The automaker plans to increase production of the Mach-E to shorten customer wait times, attributing the cost reduction to streamlined supply chain dynamics. Ford emphasized its commitment to making EVs more accessible and boosting its market share.

Title: Ford to cut prices of Mustang Mach-E, following Tesla's lead
Summary: Ford Motor Co. has announced price reductions of up to $5,900 for its Mustang Mach-E electric SUV, following Tesla's recent global price cuts. This move aims to make some Mach-E models eligible again for the $7,500 federal tax credit and is part of Ford's strategy to increase production and share cost savings with customers. Analysts suggest this could signal the beginning of a price war in the EV market.

Title: Top Performing Leveraged/Inverse ETFs: 01/29/2023
Summary: This article highlights the top-performing leveraged and inverse ETFs for the week ending January 29, 2023. Key drivers for these strong performances include positive Tesla earnings, growth in electric and autonomous vehicles, and hopes for a slower pace of interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, boosting technology and consumer discretionary sectors. The list provides specific ETF tickers, their names, and weekly returns, along with brief explanations for their performance.

Title: Austin company lays off 250 janitorial, maintenance workers after Tesla cancels contract
Summary: A facilities services company, ABM Texas General Services, is laying off 255 janitorial and maintenance employees in Austin after their contract with Tesla was terminated. Tesla ended the contract on January 16, with a new vendor, SBM, set to take over services. The layoffs affect workers at Tesla's Austin property, including its corporate headquarters and manufacturing facility.

Title: CEO longevity pays off for JPMorgan Chase’s Jamie Dimon and other chiefs of World’s Most Admired Companies
Summary: This article highlights how CEO longevity, exemplified by Jamie Dimon of JPMorgan Chase, contributes to a company's success and reputation, as seen in Fortune's World's Most Admired Companies list. Long-tenured CEOs develop deep pattern recognition, build strong internal cultures, and foster innovation, leading to greater efficiency and financial performance. The article also touches on other long-serving CEOs like Warren Buffett and Jensen Huang, and notes Elon Musk's recent "most overrated CEO" distinction.

Title: Tesla Investors Lost $12 Billion After Musk Tweet, Experts Tell Jury
Summary: Tesla Inc. investors lost $12 billion after Elon Musk's 2018 tweet claiming he had "funding secured" to take the company private, expert witnesses testified in a trial. Lawyers for Musk contention that the initial part of the tweet was truthful was countered by testimony that emphasized the collective impact of the "interwoven bundle" of statements, the expert stressed the "funding secured" aspect was the new, impactful information. The case, now in its third week, delves into the impact of Musk's statements on Tesla's stock prices and potential damages to investors.

Title: Rivian to lay off 6% of its workforce as EV price war concerns grow
Summary: Rivian announced it will lay off 6% of its workforce to conserve cash amidst growing concerns of an EV price war, following price cuts by competitors like Tesla and Ford. CEO RJ Scaringe stated that these cuts would not affect manufacturing jobs at the company's Illinois factory. Despite a successful IPO, Rivian's shares have significantly dropped, prompting a focus on operational efficiency and profitability while ramping up production of its vehicles.

Title: A battle may be shaping up between the two richest men in the world over who controls the luxury electric car market
Summary: Bernard Arnault, the world's richest man, is backing a SPAC deal to take luxury carmaker Lotus Technology public, valuing it at $5.4 billion. This move positions Lotus, majority-owned by Geely Holding, to expand its electrified luxury vehicle offerings, potentially creating competition with Elon Musk's Tesla in the premium EV market although on a much smaller scale. Lotus boasts a rich European heritage and luxury cachet that appeals to Arnault, despite its relatively small production volume compared to Tesla.

Title: General Motors Files to Trademark ‘GM Financial Insurance Company’ Name
Summary: General Motors has filed to trademark "GM Financial Insurance Company," indicating a potential expansion into the insurance sector. This move follows GM's increasing involvement in usage-based insurance solutions, such as its OnStar Insurance launched in late 2020, which tailors rates based on individual driving behavior. While OnStar Insurance is underwritten by American Family Insurance subsidiaries and is distinct from the new trademark filing, it highlights GM's strategic interest in leveraging vehicle data for insurance purposes, similar to Tesla's insurance offerings.

Title: Tesla sales of China-made electric vehicles up 18% in January
Summary: Tesla sold 66,051 China-made electric vehicles in January, an 18% increase from December and 10% higher than January last year. This increase comes after intentional production cuts in December and an extended Lunar New Year holiday in January to manage inventory. Tesla plans to boost output at its Shanghai plant in the coming months following price cuts that spurred demand, making it the second-best selling EV maker in China last month behind BYD.

Title: State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
Summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY), including its stock price, key statistics, top holdings, and dividend information. It highlights XLY's portfolio value, turnover rate, and its largest positions in companies like Amazon, Tesla, and Home Depot, based on its latest N-PORT filing.
