Summary: The GraniteShares YieldBoost TSLA ETF (TSYY) generated a 7.9% total return with an annualized distribution of approximately 35% since its inception on December 17, 2024, despite Tesla (TSLA) stock being down 14.1% in the same period. The fund employs an innovative "YieldBOOST" strategy that sells "out of the money" options on leveraged ETFs to maximize income and preserve NAV, differentiating itself from traditional covered call strategies that often prioritize income over total return. TSYY is the first in a new lineup of YieldBOOST products from GraniteShares, aiming to provide high income potential coupled with exposure to underlying stock performance.

Title: Cathie Wood Sours on Tesla and Moderna, but Likes These Stocks Instead
Summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Investment Management made significant portfolio adjustments in Q4 2024, selling all Moderna shares and trimming its Tesla holdings. The firm instead focused on growing its positions in healthcare and genetic stocks, with Illumina being the largest new purchase and Natera a key addition. These moves come as the ARK Innovation ETF sees a strong start to 2025 despite past underperformance.

Title: You can't buy a Cybertruck in Wisconsin. Tesla appeals after state denies 4-dealership plan
Summary: Tesla is appealing Wisconsin's denial of its plan to open four direct-sales dealerships in the state, despite annually selling 3,000-4,000 vehicles to Wisconsin residents who must purchase them out of state. The state's "factory store" law prevents manufacturers from owning dealerships, and an administrative law judge upheld the denial, contending Tesla did not prove no independent dealer could meet its needs. Tesla argues an exemption should apply due to its unique direct-to-consumer model and claims the decision infringes on its economic liberty.

Title: Charles Schwab Asset Management Increases Stake in Tesla in Q4
Summary: Charles Schwab Asset Management increased its stake in Tesla during the fourth quarter of 2024, acquiring nearly 800,000 additional shares to hold over 17.32 million shares valued at almost $7 billion. This continued investment highlights institutional confidence in Tesla, despite a reported 23% drop in net income in 2024 and declining vehicle registrations in key markets like the U.S., Germany, France, the Netherlands, UK, and China. Tesla's shares have risen 92% over the last twelve months, trading at $360.50 at the time of writing.

Title: BYD puts driver-assistance features in most of its cars for free
Summary: BYD will make its advanced driver-assistance features standard in almost all future models at no extra cost, aiming to compete with Tesla and other rivals in China's EV market. The company's "God's Eye" system will be included in vehicles priced from 100,000 yuan and even several lower-cost models. BYD sees intelligent driving as a "must-have" feature in the coming years and plans to integrate software from DeepSeek.

Title: Largest AC Charging Networks in the US: February 2025
Summary: In January 2025, the number of public AC Level 2 charging ports in the US grew by over 3,100, reaching more than 158,000 total ports by February 1, 2025, according to AFDC data. ChargePoint continues to dominate the market, holding a 44.6% share with over 70,000 ports, followed by Blink, Tesla Destination, Shell Recharge, and EV Connect. These top five networks collectively account for 71.5% of all public AC Level 2 charging ports in the country.

Title: Elon Musk Questions Congress Members' Wealth: 'Where Did They Get All The Money?'
Summary: Elon Musk has publicly questioned the significant wealth accumulation of several prominent members of Congress, highlighting discrepancies between their salaries and net worths. This comes amid increased scrutiny from retail traders on politicians' stock and options trading activities, which have often been linked to potential conflicts of interest. The discussion also touches upon the better-than-market returns achieved by congressional traders and renewed calls for a ban on such trading by figures like Joe Biden and Representative Ro Khanna.

Title: │‘Armored Teslas’ Vanish From Government Procurement List
Summary: │The State Department removed "Armored Tesla" from its procurement forecast for a $400 million armored EV purchase after reports highlighted the company's mention. The document now generically lists "armored electric vehicles" without Tesla’s name, although similar plans for BMW X5 and X7 SUVs remain. The solicitation, initially from the Biden administration, has been put on hold, and Elon Musk stated he was "pretty sure" Tesla would not receive the contract, raising questions about potential conflicts of interest given Musk's role in government spending oversight.

Title: Trade Desk Stock, AppLovin, Intel, Tesla, Robinhood, Deere, MGM, and More Movers
Summary: Stocks, including Trade Desk, AppLovin, Intel, Tesla, Robinhood, Deere, and MGM, saw movement on Thursday. This occurred despite persistent wholesale inflation in January and President Donald Trump's directive to propose reciprocal tariffs.

Title: Invenergy completes 300-MW Texas solar array for two major automakers
Summary: Invenergy has announced that its 300-MW Delilah I Solar Energy Center in Texas has commenced commercial operations. This solar array will supply 200 MW to Honda Motor Co. and 100 MW to Tesla through virtual power purchase agreements. WEC Energy Group is the majority owner of the project, which aims to provide affordable, reliable, clean energy while generating economic impact for the local community.

Title: New Battleshares ETF Pits Tesla Against Ford
Summary: Defiance ETFs has launched the Battleshares TSLA vs. F ETF (ELON), the first in a new series of actively managed Battleshares ETFs designed to offer dynamic exposures to competitive companies. This fund specifically targets the rivalry between Tesla (TSLA) and Ford Motor Company (F), employing a leveraged long position on Tesla and a short position on Ford. ELON aims to provide capital appreciation by allowing investors to bet on innovative disruptive companies outperforming their legacy counterparts.

Title: Tesla takes Wisconsin to court over blocking it from opening dealerships in the state
Summary: Tesla is suing Wisconsin after the state denied its request to open dealerships, citing a law prohibiting manufacturers from owning dealerships. The company argues it should be exempt as a non-franchising manufacturer and believes sales would increase if it had direct sales locations in the state. This legal challenge follows Tesla's first annual sales drop in over a decade.

Title: Hertz Tumbles With Worse-Than-Expected Loss on EV Sale Plan
Summary: Hertz Global Holdings Inc. announced a significant loss of $2.9 billion in 2024, largely due to its strategy of investing heavily in electric vehicles. The company reported a worse-than-expected adjusted loss of $1.18 per share in the fourth quarter and has completed the sale of 30,000 EVs, many of them Teslas, as it pivots away from its previous EV bet. This move comes after customers showed little interest in the electric fleet and maintenance proved costly.

Title: Tesla uses Chinese courts to silence critics and make them pay
Summary: Tesla has adopted an aggressive legal strategy in China, suing customers and critics for defamation when they publicly complain about vehicle malfunctions or quality issues. The company has won nearly 90 percent of its cases, which critics argue is due to its strong ties with the Chinese Communist Party and special status granted by the government. This strategy allows Tesla to silence dissent and limit accountability, creating a chilling effect among consumers and media.

Title: Tesla loses battle to keep 4680 battery tech under wraps
Summary: A U.S. District Court Judge denied Tesla's request to block Matthews International Corporation from selling its dry battery electrode technology, which is fundamental to Tesla's 4680 cells. Tesla had sued Matthews, alleging theft of trade secrets and seeking over $1 billion in damages. However, the judge sided with Matthews, who claims its technology predates Tesla's existence.

Title: TSLW ETF Analysis: Dividends, Returns CBOE:TSLW
Summary: This article provides an analysis of the Roundhill TSLA WeeklyPay ETF (TSLW), detailing its investment strategy, which aims for weekly income and leveraged exposure to TSLA stock. It covers key statistics like Assets Under Management, dividend yield, expense ratio, and its holdings, primarily U.S. Treasury Bills and Tesla, Inc. The article also discusses the ETF's performance metrics and answers frequently asked questions about its dividends and structure.

Title: Tesla and Honda will buy power from this new 300 MW Texas solar farm
Summary: Tesla and Honda have committed to purchasing all the power from the new 300 MW Delilah I solar farm in Texas through virtual power purchase agreements. This project, developed by Invenergy and majority-owned by WEC Energy Group, is part of a larger solar portfolio and will help both companies, particularly Honda, reach their carbon-neutrality goals by integrating more clean energy into the grid. Delilah I is located near Dallas and will contribute significantly to US-made clean energy.

Summary: This article provides an overview of the YieldMax Short TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (CRSH), detailing its price, chart, key statistics, and investment strategy. CRSH aims for monthly income and inverse exposure to Tesla stock using a synthetic covered put strategy involving options, and holds short-term US Treasury securities as collateral. The fund is actively managed and does not directly invest in Tesla stocks, offering investors a unique way to gain exposure to TSLA's performance.

Title: Roundhill Launches 5 Leveraged Weekly Income ETFs
Summary: Roundhill Investments has launched five new WeeklyPay ETFs (NVW, TSW, AAPW, COIW, PLTW) on the Cboe Exchange, offering weekly distributions and leveraged exposure to specific single stocks like Nvidia, Tesla, and Apple. These actively managed funds aim to generate 1.2 times the weekly returns of their underlying companies, providing income-focused investors with amplified returns and potential tax advantages through return of capital distributions. This innovation expands Roundhill's portfolio of weekly income strategies, with plans for additional leveraged WeeklyPay ETFs covering other major companies.

Summary: The Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X Shares ETF (TSLL) is a leveraged ETF designed for active traders to amplify Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) trading performance by aiming for 2x TSLA's daily return. Despite the author's bullish outlook on TSLA due to its autonomous robotics and Robotaxi program, investors are cautioned about the risks associated with TSLL's daily reset, especially when holding shares beyond a single day. The article rates TSLL as a BUY for those understanding these leverage-related risks.

Title: Tesla's Cars Have the Worst Drivers in America, New Study Finds
Summary: A new study by LendingTree found that Tesla drivers have the highest rate of crashes, speeding citations, and DUIs for every 1000 drivers in America, making them the worst drivers. Ram and Subaru followed in second and third place, respectively. Conversely, older, discontinued brands like Mercury and Pontiac, along with Cadillac and Chrysler, were found to have the best drivers, suggesting an impact on insurance costs.

Title: Clean200 list shows sustainable companies on path to dominate global economy
Summary: The 2025 Clean200 list, compiled by As You Sow and Corporate Knights, highlights 200 publicly traded companies leading the sustainable clean energy economy. Despite political attacks, these companies, including Apple, Microsoft, and Tesla, generated $2.5 trillion in sustainable revenue and outperformed fossil fuel stocks and the global benchmark MSCI ACWI since 2016. The report emphasizes that the clean energy economy is demonstrating robust growth and is on track to dominate the global economy.

Title: Tesla's market cap sinks below $1 trillion as stock slumps more than 8%
Summary: Tesla's market capitalization has fallen below $1 trillion after its stock slumped over 8%, erasing most gains since President Donald Trump's election victory. The company's shares are down 25% this year, impacted by a disappointing upgrade to its partially automated driving system in China and concerns related to CEO Elon Musk's political involvement. Furthermore, Tesla reported missed earnings and sales estimates for the fourth quarter, with automotive revenue declining.

Title: GM, Tesla win S&P Global Mobility’s 2024 Automotive Loyalty Awards
Summary: General Motors and Tesla have been recognized with S&P Global Mobility’s 2024 Automotive Loyalty Awards. Tesla notably won for overall loyalty, ethnic market loyalty, and highest conquest percentage. The article mentions these awards in the context of broader automotive news.

Summary: Kim Bolton, President and Portfolio Manager of Black Swan Dexteritas, reviews his previous stock selections including ASML Holding NV, Canon, and Tesla. The article discusses how these past picks are currently performing in the market. It appears to be part of a recurring segment on BNN Bloomberg's "Market Call" program.

Title: Software Defined Vehicle (SDV) Market Research 2025 - Global Forecast to 2030 with Tesla, Li Auto, NIO, Rivian, XPENG, and ZEEKR Leading the $1.23 Trillion Industry
Summary: The Software Defined Vehicle (SDV) market is projected to grow significantly from USD 213.5 billion in 2024 to USD 1.23 trillion by 2030, driven by personalized driving experiences, new revenue streams for OEMs, and the rise of pay-per-use mobility. Key players include Tesla, Li Auto, NIO, Rivian, XPENG, and ZEEKR, with Europe showing strong growth potential due to stringent safety requirements and OEM transitions to SDVs. Zonal controller architecture is expected to lead during the forecast period due to its efficiency and ability to integrate advanced software features.

Title: Tesla Targets Waymo, Uber in California Ride-Hail Bid
Summary: Tesla is seeking approval to launch ride-hailing services in California, initially with human drivers, to compete with Waymo, Uber, and Lyft. This move comes as CEO Elon Musk pushes for autonomous driving while the company's traditional EV sales slow. Tesla's application with the California Public Utilities Commission suggests an imminent rollout of a new revenue stream.

Summary: This article identifies eight top ETFs that include Tesla stock, catering to various investor strategies from conservative S&P 500 tracking to aggressive, leveraged bets. Title: Backyard backup: Virtual power plants give homeowners — and grid — security
Summary: Virtual power plants, which are networks of residential power systems like solar panels and batteries, are emerging as a key solution to stabilize the Texas electrical grid amid increasing demand. While the technology holds great promise for providing backup power to homeowners and selling excess energy back to the grid, adoption has been slow due to policy hurdles. Companies like Bandera Electric Cooperative and Tesla are pioneering pilot programs, with regulators now taking steps to expand these initiatives.

Summary: Tesla's significant stock drop suggests caution and a potential future opportunity for the Nasdaq 100. Summary: Tuttle Capital Management is launching a new "Tuttle Capital UFO Disclosure AI Powered ETF" (UFOD) to capitalize on the growing interest in space and unidentified aerial phenomena, appealing to investors looking to align with the speculative and forward-thinking spirit often embodied by figures like Elon Musk. It joins a small but growing group of space-themed ETFs, highlighting a novel approach to thematic investing rooted in emerging technologies and public fascination.

Title: 2 ‘Strong Buy’ Stocks to Snap Up If You Want to Invest in Elon Musk’s DOGE
Summary: Elon Musk, in his role heading the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), is focused on cutting federal spending and expanding his economic influence through AI and other ventures. For investors looking to capitalize on this, Nvidia (NVDA) and Modine Manufacturing (MOD) are highlighted as "Strong Buy" stocks. Nvidia is crucial to Musk's AI efforts, powering xAI's supercomputers, while Modine, a longtime Tesla supplier, provides essential thermal management solutions for data centers and EVs, positioning both companies for significant growth.

Title: Tesla's China-made EV sales fall to lowest since August 2022
Summary: Tesla's China-made EV sales plunged 49.2% in February from a year earlier to 30,688 cars, marking the lowest sales since August 2022. This decline comes as the U.S. automaker faces intense competition and a relentless price war from Chinese rivals like BYD. Despite Tesla's efforts to update its autopilot software and launch refreshed models, the market remains challenging with strong contenders like Xiaomi and Nio's Onvo L60.

Title: Feds fine Tesla $49,650 for August worker death at Austin factory
Summary: Federal regulators have fined Tesla Inc. $49,650 for "serious" safety violations linked to the August electrocution death of worker Victor J. Gomez at its Austin factory. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) issued three citations for issues including lack of protective equipment and inadequate safeguards. This incident is one of several safety concerns raised against Tesla, which has faced previous fines and lawsuits regarding workplace safety.

Title: UK Court of Appeal denies Tesla a pool licence
Summary: The UK Court of Appeal has upheld a lower court's decision denying Tesla a 5G pool licence, rejecting the car manufacturer's attempt to have UK courts set a global FRAND rate for Avanci's patent pool. While one judge believed the UK court had the authority to rule on a global FRAND rate, the majority dismissed Tesla's appeal entirely. Tesla had challenged Avanci's flat rate of $32 per vehicle, arguing it far exceeded a FRAND rate, but Avanci and InterDigital successfully disputed the UK courts' jurisdiction in this matter.

Title: Why Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (CRDO) Went Down on Wednesday
Summary: Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (CRDO) stock fell by 13.97 percent on Wednesday despite reporting impressive third-quarter fiscal year 2025 earnings. The decline is attributed to investors having already factored in higher income due to the company's growth in AI infrastructure and strong customer base, including Amazon, Tesla, and Microsoft. While CRDO posted significant increases in net income and revenues, it was among the worst performers for the day, suggesting that some AI stocks may offer more promising returns.

Title: Tesla, Inc. (TSLA): Among The Stocks With At Least $20 Million In Insider Sales Recently
Summary: This article examines Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) in the context of recent insider sales exceeding $20 million, noting that director Kimbal Musk sold over $27 million worth of shares. It discusses market fluctuations, the impact of tariffs, and analyst ratings for TSLA, while also highlighting the importance of thorough research in investment decisions. Despite Tesla's potential, the article suggests that AI stocks might offer greater returns in a shorter timeframe.

Title: US OPEN: Selloff on Monday as Uncertainty Continues
Summary: US markets experienced a selloff on Monday, with major indices showing negative performance and the VIX fear gauge climbing, indicating rising market anxiety. European markets also saw significant declines, while specific company news included Google Chrome divestiture pressures, plummeting Tesla China sales, Rocket Companies acquiring Redfin, and Robinhood settling with FINRA for $30 million.

Title: NY State Senators Urge Comptroller DiNapoli to Begin Pension Fund Divestment in Tesla, Inc.
Summary: New York State Senators are urging Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli to begin divesting the state's pension fund from Tesla, Inc. Citing Tesla's recent stock volatility and significant profit decline, the senators believe that divestment is a prudent step to protect the long-term stability of the pension fund, which serves over one million members. The letter highlights a 28% plunge in Tesla shares in February and a 71% drop in Q4 2024 profits compared to the previous year.

Title: Is It Time to Buy the Magnificent Seven?
Summary: After a recent selloff in the US stock market, the valuations of the "Magnificent Seven" mega-cap tech stocks have decreased. Morningstar analysts now consider Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet to be undervalued, while Nvidia and Tesla are fairly valued, and Apple remains overvalued. Despite these changes, Morningstar strategists continue to recommend underweighting growth stocks, favoring a rotation into value stocks.

Title: China's Xpeng may invest up to $13.8 billion in humanoid robots, state media reports
Summary: Chinese EV maker Xpeng is considering a long-term investment of up to 100 billion yuan ($13.80 billion) in humanoid robots, as stated by its CEO He Xiaopeng. The company entered the sector in 2020 and unveiled its humanoid Iron to compete with Tesla Bot. Other automakers like Stellantis-backed Leapmotor are also exploring humanoid robot development for industrial applications.

Title: Tesla, Netflix among market cap stock movers on Wednesday
Summary: This article details market cap stock movers on a Wednesday, highlighting rallies in Tesla and Microchip Technology, alongside declines in Pure Storage and Netflix. It categorizes stock movements by mega-cap, large-cap, mid-cap, and small-cap companies, providing specific percentage changes and brief news catalysts for some of the featured stocks.

Title: US Leveraged ETFs Keep Luring Korean Buyers as Tech Stocks Slump
Summary: South Korean investors have significantly increased their investment in US leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and Tesla stock this week, despite a market correction. They injected a net $519 million into three US leveraged ETFs and an additional $371 million directly into Tesla shares between March 10 and 13. This continued influx of capital highlights a persistent trend among Korean retail investors to engage in riskier, but potentially high-reward, financial products even amidst market downturns.

Title: Tesla Stock Is Reaching a Breaking Point, Analyst Says. Plus, Vertical Aerospace, OPKO Health, and More.
Summary: This article from Barron's reports on an analyst's view that Tesla stock is reaching a breaking point. It also mentions insights on Vertical Aerospace and OPKO Health, among other companies, based on recent reports from investment and research firms. The content emphasizes that these reports are a sampling of analyst thinking and not recommendations from Barron's.

Title: Tesla, led by Elon Musk, warns of export retaliation due to new Trump tariffs
Summary: Tesla has expressed concerns that new tariff policies implemented by the Trump administration could lead to retaliatory actions by other countries, negatively impacting its global sales and exports. The company stated that U.S. exporters are disproportionately affected by such trade actions, which have historically resulted in increased tariffs on goods like electric vehicles. This warning comes as Tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, has formed a close alliance with President Trump, despite previous political differences.

Title: ETF Spotlight: XLY Plunges With Consumer Sentiment
Summary: The Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY) has been a poor performer in 2025 due to declining consumer sentiment, triggered by economic uncertainty, inflation fears, and a trade war. Despite short-term struggles, the article suggests this downturn could be a buying opportunity for long-term investors, as consumer spending tends to rebound. XLY, heavily weighted with Amazon and Tesla, offers exposure to leading consumer brands but carries risks like cyclicality and concentration.

Title: Tesla v Interdigital: Tesla hits a speed bump as Court of Appeal dismisses its claim for a FRAND ‘pool’ licence
Summary: The UK Court of Appeal dismissed Tesla's claim for the UK court to set the FRAND rate for a licence to the Avanci 5G patent pool. The majority judgment found no contractual obligation for a FRAND pool licence, noting that ETSI undertakings provide for bilateral FRAND licences, not pool licences. This decision further clarifies the limitations on implementers seeking court-determined FRAND rates for patent pools in the absence of a direct contractual right.

Title: The Compound and Friends: Big Market Delusion
Summary: This article announces a new episode of "The Compound and Friends" podcast, titled "Big Market Delusion." The episode, sponsored by VanEck, discusses topics including TSLA performance, U.S. equity valuations, the S&P 500 selloff, bullish European stocks, and making a case for small caps. The article also promotes the Morningstar Investment Conference.

Title: Tesla launches free trial of assisted driving service in China
Summary: Tesla is offering a free trial of its Full Self-Driving (FSD) service in China from March 17 to April 16. This initiative aims to expand FSD's reach in the country, with Tesla collaborating with Baidu to enhance the system's performance. Unlike in the U.S., Tesla faces data localization challenges in China which limit its ability to train the FSD system using local EV data.

Title: America's Best And Worst EV Charging Networks: These Fail Half The Time
Summary: A Consumer Reports study revealed significant reliability issues with various EV charging networks in the U.S., with Shell Recharge and EVgo failing nearly half the time. Tesla Superchargers and the Rivian Adventure Network demonstrated the highest reliability. Problems often stemmed from glitchy payment systems, broken hardware, and slow charging speeds, highlighting the need for better integration and accountability among charging providers.

Title: Tesla gets permit to ferry passengers in California, a stepping stone toward autonomous taxis
Summary: Tesla Inc. has received a permit from California regulators to start a charter service using company-employed drivers to transport its employees. This step is seen as groundwork for its future plans for driverless Tesla taxis, although the permit does not currently allow for public rideshare or driverless operations. The company plans to launch driverless vehicles in Austin, Texas, in June, while full public deployment in California would require further regulatory approvals.

Title: Tesla Cybertruck recalled eighth time, exterior body panels can fall off
Summary: The Tesla Cybertruck has been recalled for the eighth time due to issues with its stainless steel exterior. Specifically, the cant rail trim pieces can detach, posing a hazard to other road users, a problem Tesla plans to fix using a different structural adhesive and a stud-welded reinforcement. Despite multiple recalls for various issues including accelerator pedals and inverter faults, Tesla reports no collisions or injuries related to this particular defect.

Title: Was Tesla key to ESG outperformance last year?
Summary: In 2020, sustainable US stock funds significantly outperformed the broader market, largely due to their focus on high-performing technology stocks like Tesla and Nvidia, and their avoidance of energy companies. This article examines the drivers behind the top-performing diversified US sustainable funds, highlighting how holdings in companies such as Tesla, Moderna, and various solar energy firms contributed to exceptional returns, with many funds achieving over 35% growth. Both active and index-based ESG funds benefited from overweighting tech and renewable energy sectors.

Title: Xcel Energy to Deploy Advanced Virtual Power Plant in Colorado with Itron and Tesla
Summary: Xcel Energy is partnering with Itron and Tesla to deploy an advanced virtual power plant (VPP) in Colorado. This initiative integrates Itron's IntelliFLEX Aggregator DERMS solution with Tesla Home Batteries to enhance grid flexibility, visibility, and control. The collaboration aims to expand Xcel Energy’s Renewable Battery Connect program, leveraging residential batteries to stabilize the electric grid during peak energy demand and advance electrification goals.

Title: Betting Against Tesla and Elon Musk Is Easy With These ETFs. The Risks Outweigh the Rewards. -- Barrons.com
Summary: This article discusses the ease of betting against Tesla and Elon Musk using ETFs, specifically highlighting the TSLQ and SARK funds. Title: Amazon, Tesla and 18 other US companies that bagged maximum H-1B visas in 2024
Summary: Amazon and Tesla, along with numerous other US companies, were among the top recipients of H-1B visa approvals in 2025, according to USCIS data. Amazon led with 9,265 approvals, followed by Cognizant and Google, while Indian IT giants like Infosys and TCS also secured a significant number of visas. These companies rely heavily on skilled foreign workers for specialized roles in technology, engineering, research, and development.

Title: Stock market today: Nasdaq, S&P 500 dive, snap 3-day win streak as Trump preps auto tariffs
Summary: US stocks closed lower on Wednesday, snapping a three-day win streak, as President Trump prepared to announce new tariffs on auto imports. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite led the losses, falling over 2%, with Nvidia and Tesla shares down more than 5%. The looming tariffs also fueled a surge in copper prices amidst reports of accelerated plans for copper levies.

Title: Is Cathy Wood’s ARKK ETF a Safe Investment?
Summary: This article analyzes the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) managed by Cathy Wood, focusing on its safety as an investment. It highlights ARKK's high volatility, significant concentration in tech stocks and a few specific holdings like Tesla, and a relatively high expense ratio with no dividends. The author suggests that despite the potential for disruptive innovation, ARKK's lack of diversification and past performance indicate it may not be a safe choice for risk-averse investors.

Title: GM shares tank as U.S. auto industry digests new Trump tariffs
Summary: General Motors (GM) shares fell significantly after President Trump announced new tariffs on imported vehicles and auto parts, impacting the U.S. auto industry. GM is particularly vulnerable due to its extensive operations in Mexico and Canada, unlike Tesla and Ford which appear more shielded. Experts and industry leaders anticipate major repercussions, including increased vehicle prices, though the UAW has expressed support for the tariffs.

Title: Electric Semi Trucks: 7 Promising Insights in Freight Evolution
Summary: Electric semi-trucks are transitioning from pilot programs to mainstream logistics, with companies like Saia testing Tesla Semis and reporting benefits like smoother acceleration and reduced operating costs. While challenges such as charging infrastructure and battery fire risks exist, incentives and regulatory mandates are accelerating EV adoption. The article details operational efficiencies, cost comparisons with diesel trucks, and regional variations in adoption, highlighting the potential for electric semis to become standard in freight operations.

Title: The anti-Trump movement has found its target: Elon Musk’s Tesla
Summary: The anti-Trump movement has shifted its focus to Elon Musk and his company, Tesla. This decline comes as the company prepares for the delivery of the new Model Y in June, which is expected to boost sales and address an aging model lineup. The sales drop contrasts with overall EV market growth in these regions, with competitors like BYD gaining significant market share.

Title: The Dan Ives Wedbush AI Revolution ETF Starts Trading Today. Should You Buy the IVES ETF Now?
Summary: Wedbush senior analyst Dan Ives has launched the "Dan Ives Wedbush AI Revolution ETF" (ticker: IVES) to offer investors targeted exposure to his top 30 AI stock picks, including Nvidia and Tesla. Ives describes the ETF as a "living organism" that will be reconfigured quarterly to adapt to the evolving AI landscape. The fund aims to capitalize on the ongoing AI revolution, which Ives believes is still in its early stages and expanding beyond chips into software and consumer applications.

Title: REX Financial Expands Growth & Income ETF Suite with New Single-Stock Covered Call Strategies on MSTR, COIN, and TSLA
Summary: REX Financial has expanded its Growth & Income Covered Call ETF suite by introducing three new funds: REX COIN Growth & Income ETF (COII), REX MSTR Growth & Income ETF (MSII), and REX TSLA Growth & Income ETF (TSII). These new ETFs aim to provide investors with weekly income generation and targeted exposure to Coinbase, Strategy (MicroStrategy), and Tesla, building on the recent launch of the REX NVDA Growth & Income ETF (NVII). The funds target daily exposure of 1.25x to their underlying stock while generating income through the strategic sale of call options, offering both uncapped upside potential and volatility monetization.

Title: REX Launches 3 New Growth & Income Covered Call ETFs
Summary: REX Financial has introduced three new "Growth & Income Covered Call ETFs" (COII, MSII, TSII) targeting Coinbase, MicroStrategy, and Tesla, respectively. These ETFs aim to provide growth potential and weekly income through a dual portfolio strategy, writing call options on approximately half of the portfolio while maintaining uncapped upside potential on the remainder. Title: Trump, Musk public feud escalates; Nasdaq falls; Tesla, DJT tumble
Summary: A public feud between President Donald Trump and billionaire Elon Musk erupted, leading to significant drops in the stock values of Tesla (TSLA.O) and Trump Media & Technology Group Corp (DJT.O). Trump threatened to cancel government contracts with Musk's companies, causing Tesla's stock to fall 14.3% and losing $150 billion in market value, while DJT was down 8.04%. Analysts suggest the dispute, seen as a "jaw-dropping" reversal of their previous alliance, could impact Tesla's regulatory environment and the broader market.

Title: Shift4 appoints new CEO
Summary: Shift4 has appointed Taylor Lauber as its new CEO, following founder Jared Isaacman's return to an executive chairman role. This change occurred after President Trump withdrew Isaacman's nomination to run NASA, reportedly due to past political contributions and ties to Elon Musk. Isaacman will retain his super voting shares in the company.

Title: FTXR: Tesla Now A Fixture For This Factor-Based Transportation ETF (NASDAQ:FTXR)
Summary: The First Trust Nasdaq Transportation ETF (FTXR) tracks a transportation-themed index with a significant allocation to auto stocks, including notable holdings like Tesla, Ford, and General Motors. Despite a history of underperformance compared to competitor ETFs, the fund underwent a strategy adjustment in March 2023. The author has assigned FTXR a "hold" rating, citing concerns about potential high volatility and low growth, despite an attractive forward P/E.

Title: President Trump Could Sell His Barely Used Tesla Model S Amid Feud with Elon Musk
Summary: President Trump is reportedly considering selling his red Tesla Model S due to an escalating public feud with Elon Musk. This symbolic act comes after the car's purchase in March was celebrated, highlighting the deterioration of their relationship. The disagreement, sparked by Musk's comments on a public spending bill, has already negatively impacted Tesla's stock price and could threaten SpaceX's government contracts.

Title: Tesla seeks to block city of Austin from releasing records on robotaxi trial
Summary: Tesla is attempting to prevent the city of Austin, Texas, from releasing public records to Reuters concerning the electric vehicle maker's upcoming self-driving robotaxi launch. The company argues that releasing these documents would expose "confidential, proprietary, competitively sensitive commercial, and/or trade secret information" and "irreparably harm Tesla" by revealing its deployment strategy. This comes after Reuters requested communications between Tesla and Austin officials following Elon Musk's announcement of a robotaxi launch in Austin.

Title: The EV Startup That Wanted to Beat Tesla Suddenly Shutters Half its Stores
Summary: VinFast, the Vietnamese EV startup that aimed to compete with Tesla, is closing half of its retail locations in Canada just two and a half years after entering the market. This move reflects a broader strategy to refocus resources as the EV market cools and rising interest rates put pressure on new players. The company will maintain five showrooms and is considering franchise dealer partnerships, a departure from its original direct-sales model.

Title: Top 3 FOMO Stocks for 2025 With More Room to Run
Summary: This article discusses three "FOMO" (Fear Of Missing Out) stocks—CoreWeave (CRWV), Palantir (PLTR), and Tesla (TSLA)—that are identified as having momentum and potential for further gains in 2025, despite some having high valuations. CoreWeave is highlighted due to its NVIDIA backing and revenue growth, Palantir for its government contracts and strong momentum, and Tesla for potential short-term catalysts despite recent market drops and a feud involving Elon Musk. The author advises careful charting and identification of entry/exit points for these momentum-driven stocks.

Title: Tesla’s retail army defies Musk-Trump spat to place record ETF bet
Summary: Despite a significant drop in Elon Musk's fortune and Tesla's stock price, retail investors poured a record $651 million into the Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X Shares ETF (TSLL), a leveraged fund designed to double Tesla's daily return. This massive inflow occurred even amid a public spat between Musk and Donald Trump, increased competition for Tesla, and concerns over the company's valuation. The move reflects a continued faith among retail traders in betting on Musk's comebacks during sell-offs, a strategy that has historically yielded substantial returns.

Title: Uber will bring robotaxis to London in 2026
Summary: Uber is set to launch its first robotaxi pilot scheme in London in early 2026, partnering with British AI firm Wayve Technologies Ltd. This initiative aims to catch up with competitors like Waymo and Tesla in the autonomous vehicle market. While the UK government has introduced legislation to support self-driving services, London taxi drivers remain skeptical about their feasibility on the city's complex streets.

Title: Goldman Sees Autonomous Vehicles Transforming Insurance World
Summary: Goldman Sachs predicts that autonomous vehicles will significantly transform the $400 billion US auto insurance industry, reducing accident frequency and claim costs, but also shifting liability concerns. Insurance costs per mile are projected to decline by over 50% in the next 15 years, while the liability for accidents will likely move from drivers to manufacturers and software providers, requiring insurers to adapt to new risk profiles like product liability and cyber coverage. Companies like Tesla, Alphabet, Aurora Innovation, Uber, Lyft, and Progressive Corp. are identified as potential beneficiaries or strong stocks in this transition.

Title: GraniteShares YieldBOOST TSLA ETF To Go Ex-Dividend On June 20th, 2025 With 0.29753 USD Dividend Per Share
Summary: The GraniteShares YieldBOOST TSLA ETF (NASDAQ: TSLP) is scheduled to go ex-dividend on June 20th, 2025. Shareholders will receive a cash dividend of 0.29753 USD per share. This information is crucial for investors tracking dividend payments from TSLP.

Title: ETF Spotlight: Assets Flee Wood's ARKK as Price Jumps
Summary: Despite a 45% gain over the past year, Cathie Wood’s ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) is experiencing significant outflows, with investors pulling $2.4 billion over the past year and $275 million in the past five days through June 17. The fund, known for its volatile performance, has seen its top holdings like Tesla and Roku surge, but concerns are rising due to Tesla's recent decline and increased short interest in ARKK. This paradox of rising price and fleeing assets highlights investor caution given ARKK's history of sharp drops after previous surges.

Title: Tesla inks first deal to build China's largest grid-scale battery power plant
Summary: Tesla has secured its first deal to construct a grid-scale battery power plant in China, which is projected to be the largest of its kind upon completion. This project, worth 4 billion yuan ($556 million), aims to serve as a "smart regulator" for urban electricity, addressing supply-demand imbalances exacerbated by intermittent renewable energy sources. The deal is noteworthy for Tesla, as it marks a significant step in the competitive Chinese battery market, where local companies like CATL and BYD are major players.

Title: Why Cathie Wood's Flagship Ark Innovation ETF Is Finally Booming Again.
Summary: Cathie Wood's flagship ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) has experienced a resurgence since last October, after struggling for years and missing out on the AI boom. This recent boom is attributed to holdings such as Circle, Robinhood, Palantir, and Tesla, indicating a shift in the ETF's performance drivers. The article highlights ARKK's underperformance compared to the S&P 500 in previous years despite the broader market's gains in AI and Nvidia.

Title: Is General Motors About to Overtake Tesla in EV Sales?
Summary: General Motors is rapidly gaining on Tesla in the US EV market, driven by a diverse range of EV models and a focus on affordability. GM's EV sales significantly increased in Q1 2025, while Tesla faces challenges including a drop in stock price and declining global deliveries. GM's advancements in battery technology and US-based production are also key factors in its growing competitiveness.

Title: Tesla stock soars following Austin AI robotaxi event
Summary: Tesla officially launched its AI robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, charging a $4.20 flat fee for initial rides. The debut caused Tesla's stock to jump over 10%, highlighting the long-awaited entry into the robotaxi market. The article also details the company's future plans, including the CyberCab sedan and expansion to other cities, and compares Tesla's new service with established players like Waymo and Zoox.

Title: Tesla Robotaxi videos show speeding, driving into wrong lane
Summary: Tesla's robotaxis reportedly violated traffic laws on their first day of paid operations, with videos showing a car driving into the wrong lane and others exceeding speed limits. Despite these incidents captured by customers and investors, Wall Street analysts offered broadly positive reports and Tesla's stock rose. The automaker had previously recalled vehicles for similar issues in 2023.

Title: Dow Futures Edge Lower As Iran Moves To Block Strait Of Hormuz: Exxon, Chevron, Occidental, Tesla Among Stocks In Focus
Summary: Dow Futures are trading lower following Iran's threats to block the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil transit choke point. This geopolitical tension is placing oil stocks like Exxon, Chevron, and Occidental Petroleum in focus. Tesla is also among the stocks being watched by investors.

Title: BlackRock launches Texas ETF as state draws investor interest
Summary: BlackRock has launched a Texas-focused exchange-traded fund called iShares Texas Equity ETF, aiming to capitalize on the state's growing economic activity. Texas's low taxes and business-friendly policies have attracted numerous companies, including Tesla, SpaceX, Oracle, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. BlackRock currently manages close to $380 billion in assets tied to public companies in Texas, solidifying its position as a major investor in the region.

Title: Tesla’s stock is giving back its robotaxi gains. Here’s what happened.
Summary: Tesla Inc. shares experienced a drop on Tuesday, giving back gains from the previous session's robotaxi launch. Despite an initial 8% surge due to the robotaxi rollout, which had been delayed, analysts noted chart resistance around $360 per share. This indicates that a long-term breakout might not be imminent for the stock.

Summary: BlackRock has launched the iShares Texas Equity ETF to capitalize on Texas's growth as a magnet for companies, capital, and jobs. The state’s low taxes, business-friendly policies, and burgeoning tech and energy sectors have attracted significant investment and company relocations, including Tesla, SpaceX, Oracle, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. This move comes as BlackRock navigates its complex relationship with Republican-leaning states over climate-focused investment policies, recently being removed from Texas's list of companies considered hostile to the energy sector after scaling back some climate commitments.

Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Tesla, eBay, PayPal and Alphabet
Summary: Zacks Investment Ideas spotlights Tesla, eBay, PayPal, and Alphabet, focusing on Tesla's robotaxi debut. The author advises caution, suggesting small position sizes and diversification for those considering this high-yield fund.

Title: 'Thank You, Elon:' Musk's Longtime Aide Reportedly Fired Days After Public Praise
Summary: Elon Musk's longtime aide, Omead Afshar, has reportedly been fired from Tesla Inc. just days after publicly praising Musk's robotaxi initiative. Afshar's departure coincides with a significant slump in Tesla's new vehicle sales in Europe and increasing turbulence within the EV industry. This news follows previous internal scrutiny and investigations involving Afshar in 2022 and 2023.

Title: Tesla fails to end Florida lawsuit over fatal Model S crash
Summary: A federal judge in Miami denied Tesla's attempt to dismiss a lawsuit over a fatal 2019 crash involving an Autopilot-equipped Model S. The ruling allows the estate of a woman killed in the incident and her injured boyfriend to pursue design defect and failure to warn claims, as well as punitive damages. A trial is scheduled for July 14, stemming from an incident where the driver, allegedly distracted, did not receive alerts before hitting a parked vehicle and victims, resulting in one death.

Title: 'Tesla Has The Robot And The Customer': Dave Mazza's HUMN ETF Makes A Calculated Bet On Optimus
Summary: Dave Mazza, CEO of Roundhill Investments, discusses how the Roundhill Humanoid Robotics ETF (HUMN) offers investors exposure to the burgeoning humanoid robotics market, which Morgan Stanley projects to reach $5 trillion by 2050. Mazza highlights the convergence of labor shortages, declining AI costs, and Robots-as-a-Service pricing as key drivers, making humanoid robotics an investable theme now. HUMN is an actively managed ETF that includes Tesla as its largest holding, aiming to navigate the fast-evolving frontier tech landscape and global robotics value chain.

Title: China EV insurance registrations for week ending Jun 29: Nio 3,790, Tesla 20,680, Xiaomi 9,090
Summary: Major electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers in China, including Nio, Tesla, Xpeng, and Xiaomi, largely experienced an increase in insurance registrations during the week of June 23-29, 2025, as deliveries typically rise towards month-end. Nio Inc (including Nio, Onvo, and Firefly brands) saw 6,300 registrations, while Tesla recorded 20,680, and Xiaomi hit a record 9,090 registrations. Li Auto and BYD, however, experienced slight decreases in registrations for the same period.

Title: Navitas Expands 200mm GaN Production: Major Push into AI Data Centers and EV Markets
Summary: Navitas Semiconductor announced a strategic partnership with Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC) to begin 200mm GaN-on-silicon technology production at Powerchip's Fab 8B in Taiwan. This collaboration aims to meet the growing demand for GaN in 48V infrastructure, AI data centers, and EVs, utilizing an improved 180nm CMOS process. Initial qualification is expected in Q4 2025, with 100V family production starting in the first half of 2026, and 650V devices transitioning from TSMC to Powerchip over the following 12-24 months.

Aeva is noted for its advanced 4D LiDAR system and significant stock growth, while Mobileye is recognized for its comprehensive driverless vehicle technology and strategic partnerships despite recent revenue declines.

Title: Enphase Energy Stock Slides After RBC Downgrade, But Retail Shrugs It Off
Summary: Enphase Energy (ENPH) shares dropped over 9% following an RBC Capital downgrade due to competitive pressures and projected slower growth, though retail investors remain bullish. RBC analyst Christopher Dendrinos lowered his rating to 'Sector Perform' and reduced the price target to $100, citing increased competition from third-party ownership systems benefiting from Inflation Reduction Act tax credits and potential market share loss to Tesla's Powerwall 3. Despite analyst concerns and a significant year-to-date stock decline, retail sentiment remains 'extremely bullish'.

Title: Elon Musk's $71 Billion Wealth Wipeout Dwarfs Next 7 Billionaire Decliners Combined
Summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla, has experienced a $71.2 billion decrease in his net worth in 2025, primarily due to the volatile performance of Tesla stock amidst his public disputes with President Donald Trump. This decline is greater than the combined wealth loss of the next seven billionaires on Bloomberg's list. The article highlights how political tensions and stock performance have significantly impacted Musk's financial standing and could continue to do so.

Title: Investment firm Azoria postpones Tesla ETF after Musk plans political party
Summary: Investment firm Azoria Partners has postponed the launch of its Azoria Tesla Convexity exchange-traded fund following CEO Elon Musk's announcement of forming a new U.S. political party, the "America Party." Azoria CEO James Fishback criticized Musk's political ambitions, questioning their compatibility with his role at Tesla, and expressed support for Donald Trump. This decision reportedly undermines shareholder confidence in Tesla's future.

Title: Azoria Delays Tesla ETF Launch Amid Musk’s Political Move
Summary: Azoria Partners has postponed the launch of its Tesla-focused ETF due to Elon Musk's entry into U.S. politics with the formation of the "America Party." The delay highlights how Musk's non-Tesla endeavors can influence financial markets and investor sentiment.

Title: A reignited Trump-Musk feud burns Tesla investors, shares of EV company tumble 8%
Summary: Tesla shares tumbled 7% after a public feud reignited between Elon Musk and Donald Trump, with investors concerned about potential government hurdles for Musk's companies. This comes amid a significant drop in Tesla's sales and increasing competition, following Musk's political alignment which analysts believe has negatively impacted the brand.

Summary: Cathie Wood, CEO of Ark Invest, has declared Elon Musk to be the "most productive human being on earth and in space in history," citing his role in AI, robotics, and energy storage breakthroughs. This endorsement comes as Ark Invest holds a significant stake in Tesla, Musk's company, across its ETFs. Despite a recent dip in Tesla’s stock, analysts like Dan Ives maintain an "Outperform" rating, valuing it as an undervalued AI play.

Summary: Cathie Wood of ARK Invest continues to support Tesla Inc. despite investor panic over Elon Musk's return to politics, reiterating her $2,600 price target, driven by Robotaxis and Optimus. Wood has also lauded Tesla as the "largest AI project on earth" and Musk as the "most productive human being," while Apple struggles with its AI race.

Title: Tesla Semi Generally Matches ArcBest’s Diesels, Pilot Finds
Summary: A recent three-week pilot test by ArcBest's ABF Freight division found that the Tesla Semi battery-electric tractor averaged 1.55 kWh per mile over 4,494 miles, matching claims by Tesla and outperforming some earlier pilot tests. The Semi performed well on various routes, including a significant climb, and drivers reported positive feedback regarding comfort and ease of use. ArcBest plans to continue assessing the long-term viability of Class 8 battery-electric tractors for its fleet.

Title: US stock market future slips as Trump’s 30% tariffs rattle global trade; Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq dip while Bo
Summary: US stock futures slipped after President Donald Trump announced 30% tariffs on imports from the EU and Mexico, beginning August 1st, stoking global trade tensions. Investors are also closely watching second-quarter earnings reports from major banks, upcoming inflation data, and the growing rift between Trump and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. Despite the market dip, Boeing saw gains while Apple and Tesla slid, and Bitcoin hit a new record high.

Title: Tesla to Face Jury Trial over Autopilot Defects Following 70-Page Summary Judgment Opinion
Summary: Tesla is set to face a jury trial over alleged Autopilot defects in the *Benavides v. Tesla* case, following a summary judgment opinion that largely rejected Tesla's defense. The case involves a fatal crash where a Tesla Model S, operating on Autopilot, ran a stop sign, killing a 22-year-old college student. The court found that a reasonable jury could conclude Autopilot was defectively designed because it could be activated on inappropriate roads and failed to adequately ensure driver attention, also allowing the claim for punitive damages to proceed.

Summary: Tech analyst Dan Ives has named Nvidia, Palantir, Microsoft, Meta, and Tesla as his top five stock picks for the second half of 2025, declaring the "golden age of tech is here with the AI Revolution." He anticipates an "explosion" in AI capital expenditure by companies, describing it as a "fourth industrial revolution" that will drive a bullish tech earnings season, and foresees Microsoft reaching a $5 trillion market cap in the next 18 months, aligning with Nvidia. Title: Tesla must pay $243 million over fatal Autopilot crash, jury decides
Summary: A jury in Miami has ordered Tesla to pay $243 million in a lawsuit stemming from a fatal 2019 Autopilot crash, marking the first significant court loss for the automaker related to its driver-assistance technology. The jury found Tesla to be 33% at fault for the collision that killed a woman and seriously injured her boyfriend, awarding $42.5 million in compensatory damages and $200 million in punitive damages, which Tesla expects to be reduced. The company plans to appeal the verdict, arguing that the driver was entirely at fault.

Title: Tesla's July China-made EV sales fall 8.4%
Summary: Tesla's sales of China-made electric vehicles, including exports, declined by 8.4% in July year-over-year, and 5.2% from June, amidst fierce competition and a price war in the Chinese auto market. This setback follows a brief recovery in June that ended an eight-month losing streak. The company is facing challenges from rival manufacturers like BYD and plans to introduce new models, including a longer-wheelbase Model Y and a longer-range Model 3, to boost sales in China.

Title: Georgia Power requests PSC permission to build and own 3GW of new battery storage projects
Summary: Georgia Power has formally requested certification from the Georgia Public Service Commission (PSC) to develop and own over 3 GW of new battery storage projects, which will primarily utilize Tesla Megapack technology. This initiative is part of a larger plan to add 9,900MW of new generation resources, including natural gas and solar-plus-storage, to meet an anticipated 8GW load growth by 2030. The utility asserts these company-owned battery energy storage systems (BESS) will be cost-effective and provide significant economic benefits to the state.

Title: Tesla, Elon Musk sued by shareholders over Robotaxi claims
Summary: Shareholders are suing Elon Musk and Tesla for securities fraud, claiming they concealed risks associated with the company's self-driving vehicles, including the Robotaxi. The lawsuit follows a public test where robotaxis exhibited dangerous driving behaviors, leading to a significant drop in Tesla's stock price and wiping out $68 billion in market value. This legal action comes after a Florida jury recently found Tesla partially responsible for a fatal crash involving its self-driving software.

Title: Ex-Tesla HR pros allege they were ‘penalized and pushed out’ for reporting bias

Summary: BYD Co. surpassed Tesla Inc. in electric vehicle sales in Germany and the UK last year, marking a significant expansion for the Chinese automaker. In Germany, BYD's vehicle registrations increased eightfold, while Tesla's almost halved. This performance contributes to BYD's global lead over Tesla in EV deliveries, even as growth in its domestic market faces pressure.

Title: Cathie Wood Beats S&P 500 in 2025 — This ARK ETF Delivered The Knockout With A 50% Gain
Summary: In 2025, Ark Invest's ETFs, led by Cathie Wood, significantly outperformed the S&P 500, with two funds, the Ark Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ) and the Ark Space & Defense Innovation ETF (ARKX), delivering gains nearing 50%. These top-performing ETFs, which had considerable overlap in their top holdings like Tesla, Kratos Defense, and Rocket Lab, benefited from strong trends in AI, robotics, and space. The article also highlights predictions for 2026, including a potential SpaceX IPO influencing ARKX.

Title: Why We Highly Rate JPMorgan Large Cap Growth
Summary: JPMorgan Large Cap Growth R6 (JLGMX) receives a Gold Morningstar Medalist Rating due to its highly experienced lead manager, Giri Devulapally, and a solid team of sector analysts. The fund's strategy combines robust fundamental research with a momentum component, enabling early identification and long-term holding of market-winning companies like NVIDIA and Tesla. Devulapally's tenure has resulted in impressive performance, consistently outperforming peers and the Russell 1000 Growth Index while effectively managing market volatility.

Title: ‘The Crash is Coming,’ Says Investor About Tesla Stock
Summary: An investor known as Cash Flow Venue predicts a crash for Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) stock in 2026, citing the company's declining EV deliveries, Elon Musk's unfulfilled promises, and intense competition from BYD. The investor views Tesla's high forward P/E multiple as excessively risky given these challenges, urging current investors to cash out or trim their positions. Despite this bearish outlook, Wall Street analysts maintain a consensus Hold rating on TSLA stock.

Title: Tesla Stock Falls on Rising Competition in Robo-Taxi Market
Summary: Tesla shares fell after Nvidia's CEO presented new self-driving technology at CES, raising concerns about increased competition in the robo-taxi market. Nvidia's Alpamayo system, which offers deep reasoning for autonomous vehicles, will be integrated into Mercedes' CLA models this year. Analysts still see significant long-term growth potential for Tesla's robo-taxi unit despite the rising competition.

Title: Tesla Stock Falls on Rising Competition in Robo-Taxi Market
Summary: Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) shares fell by 3% following comments at the Consumer Electronics Show by Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang about new self-driving developments, including their Alpamayo system. This technology, running on Nvidia's Thor self-driving computer, is being adopted by automakers like Mercedes-Benz, Lucid, and BYD, intensifying competition for Tesla and Alphabet's Waymo in the autonomous vehicle market. Despite this, analyst Edison Yu of Deutsche Bank maintains a Buy rating on Tesla with a $470 price target, projecting its robo-taxi unit could be worth $1.2 trillion by 2035.

Title: Senate hearing with Detroit 3 CEOs postponed after Ford raises concerns
Summary: A Senate hearing with the CEOs of the Detroit 3 automakers, scheduled for January 14, has been postponed after Ford raised concerns. Ford CEO Jim Farley cited existing commitments and expressed reservations about the hearing not including Tesla CEO Elon Musk. The hearing was intended to address rising car prices.

Title: If The US Beats China in EVs This ETF Is Going To Soar | DRIV
Summary: The Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF (DRIV) is positioned to benefit if the US maintains its lead in EV technology, especially in semiconductors and software, over Chinese manufacturers. The ETF's performance is heavily influenced by trade policy, such as tariffs and federal tax credits, and has a significant allocation to information technology rather than solely automakers. Investors should monitor trade policy announcements and DRIV's sector allocation for future performance indicators.

Title: Tesla: Shares Fall on Market Concerns About Autonomous Driving Competition from Nvidia
Summary: Tesla's shares fell by 5% following Nvidia's announcement at CES 2026 to develop and sell an autonomous driving system for personal vehicles and robotaxis. This new competition is seen as a threat to Tesla's growth in the autonomous driving software market, potentially impacting its future robotaxi service and overall market share. Morningstar maintains its $300 fair value estimate for Tesla, considering the stock overvalued at current prices.

Title: KraneShares AGIX ETF raises stake in Musk-backed xAI
Summary: The KraneShares Alternative Harvest ETF (AGIX) has reportedly increased its investment in xAI, an artificial intelligence company founded by Elon Musk. This move by AGIX suggests a growing interest in companies associated with the development of advanced AI technologies. The article from MSN provides this update on AGIX's portfolio changes.

Title: After Michael Burry, This Top Fund Manager Says Tesla Stock Is At Least 5X Overpriced, Pegs Fair Value At $80 A Share
Summary: Former fund manager George Noble argues that Tesla Inc.'s stock (NASDAQ: TSLA) is significantly overvalued, estimating its fair value at $80 per share, a stark contrast to its current trading price of $438.07. He bases this valuation on a "sum of the parts" analysis, comparing Tesla's robotics, robotaxi, core automotive, and energy businesses to comparable companies. This sentiment echoes Michael Burry's recent concerns about Tesla's overvaluation, especially after the company lost its position as the top EV maker to BYD.

Title: Tesla Has an Issue with Its Cybercab Trademark Thanks to a Comical Error from the Company
Summary: Tesla is facing a trademark dispute for its "Cybercab" name because it publicly announced the name before filing for the trademark. The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office suspended Tesla's application, and a French drinks company, UniBev, has since acquired the rights to "Cybercab." Tesla now faces the choice of either purchasing the trademark from UniBev or renaming its electric taxi.

Title: Tesla Earnings Preview: What to Expect
Summary: Tesla is set to announce its fiscal fourth-quarter 2025 earnings on January 28, with analysts expecting a profit of $0.34 per share, a 48.5% decrease year-over-year. The company's stock has underperformed the S&P 500 largely due to declining production, fierce competition from Chinese EV makers like BYD and XPeng, and margin pressures. Despite a "Hold" rating from analysts, some foresee an ambitious upside potential, with a Street-high price target of $600.

Title: Tesla Door Design Is Targeted by New US Automotive Safety Bill
Summary: A US lawmaker has introduced legislation to mandate manual door releases in new cars due to safety concerns with electrically powered handles, popularized by Tesla. The proposed SAFE Exit Act calls for clearly labeled mechanical latches and means for first responders to access vehicles when power is lost. This follows reports of severe injuries and deaths due to occupants being trapped in vehicles with inoperable electric doors.

Title: LCID Stock Crashed Last Year, But Will Robotaxis Save the Day for Lucid in 2026?
Summary: Lucid Group (LCID) experienced a significant stock crash in the past year, with its market capitalization falling below $4 billion due to slowing EV sales, production overcapacity, and high cash burn. Despite this, the company met its revised 2025 production guidance and recently partnered with Uber and Nuro to introduce robotaxis based on its Gravity SUV, integrating advanced autonomous driving systems. This robotaxi pivot could provide a crucial boost in sales volume and brand visibility for Lucid, although it primarily involves providing vehicles rather than a full robotaxi operation like Tesla.

Title: 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock to Buy Before It Soars 140% to Join Nvidia and Tesla as a Trillion-Dollar Company
Summary: Wedbush analyst Dan Ives predicts Palantir Technologies will become a trillion-dollar company, soaring 140% to join the ranks of Nvidia and Tesla, due to its leadership in AI decisioning software and accelerating revenue growth. However, the article highlights Palantir's extremely high price-to-sales ratio of 107, making it one of the most expensive software stocks historically, and warns that similar past high-valuation software stocks eventually fell significantly. While Palantir maintains strong analyst endorsements and robust growth in the AI sector, the author suggests its current valuation presents a high-risk-reward profile compared to historical market trends.

Title: Qualcomm in talks with Samsung for next-gen 2nm chips
Summary: Qualcomm is reportedly in discussions with Samsung Electronics for the production of its upcoming 2-nanometer (2nm) chips. This potential collaboration could significantly boost Samsung's foundry business, which has previously lagged behind TSMC. The move signals a shift as Samsung has made recent breakthroughs, including securing a substantial deal with Tesla for AI chips.

Title: Wedbush analyst Dan Ives upbeat on Tesla Inc. (TSLA) despite lower delivery numbers
Summary: Wedbush analyst Dan Ives maintains an Outperform rating and $300 price target on Tesla (TSLA) despite the company's Q4 delivery numbers falling below Wall Street expectations. Ives attributes the miss to production issues, especially around the Cybertruck, and remains optimistic about Tesla's potential given its market leadership and upcoming product launches. He forecasts a significant rebound for TSLA in 2024.

Title: JPMorgan's asset management will no longer use controversial proxy advisors for shareholder votes
Summary: JPMorgan's asset management division has ceased using controversial proxy advisors for shareholder votes, opting instead for an internal artificial intelligence tool called Proxy IQ. This move makes JPMorgan the first major investment firm to eliminate reliance on such companies, which have faced criticism from figures like Donald Trump and Elon Musk regarding their influence and recommendations. The AI tool will aggregate and analyze proxy data from 3,000 annual company meetings.

Title: Tesla CEO Musk brushes off Nvidia self-driving competition as 5 or 6 years away
Summary: Elon Musk believes Nvidia's self-driving technology, despite the newly announced Alpamayo models, is five to six years away from posing serious competition to Tesla's FSD. He noted that legacy car companies would take even longer to integrate such systems at scale. FSD remains central to Tesla's long-term strategy, including robotaxis and AI development.

Title: General Motors' Q4 US Sales Fall 7% Y/Y: Is EV Weakness the Reason?
Summary: General Motors reported a 7% year-over-year decline in Q4 2025 US sales, delivering 703,001 vehicles, with EV sales sharply dropping by 43%. Despite this quarterly dip, the company led the U.S. auto market for the full year, increasing sales by 6% and maintaining its leadership in full-size pickups and SUVs. This performance contrasts with rivals like Tesla and Ford, who showed mixed results in the same period.

Title: JPMorgan's asset management arm to end use of proxy advisers in US, memo shows
Summary: JPMorgan Chase's asset management division will cease using proxy advisers in the U.S., opting instead for its newly developed AI-powered in-house tool, Proxy IQ. This move, described as an industry first by the bank, comes amid growing complaints from conservatives and some business leaders, including Jamie Dimon and Elon Musk, who argue that proxy advisers unduly influence boardroom decisions and emphasize climate and social issues. The decision aligns with increased scrutiny on proxy advisory firms, with former President Donald Trump having signed an executive order to boost oversight of the industry.

Title: YieldMax Short TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF declares $0.2334 dividend
Summary: The YieldMax Short TSLA Option Income Strategy ETF (NYSEARCA:TSLY) has declared a dividend of $0.2334 per share. This dividend is payable on January 09, 2026, to shareholders of record as of January 08, 2026, with an ex-dividend date of January 07, 2026, and is an important piece of information for investors tracking income from this ETF.

Title: Ford enters race to offer eyes-off driving tech, starting with $30,000 EV in 2028
Summary: Ford Motor plans to introduce eyes-off driving technology in 2028, starting with an affordable $30,000 all-electric vehicle, intensifying competition with rivals like Tesla and General Motors. This strategy contrasts with the typical rollout of new automotive technology on pricier models. Additionally, Ford announced a new AI assistant and a vehicle software architecture at CES to enhance customer experience.

Title: Tesla ETF Rout Deepens As Nvidia Democratizes Self-Driving AI
Summary: Tesla-linked ETFs are experiencing a downturn, with the ProShares Ultra TSLA ETF down significantly from its December peak, due to growing scrutiny over the EV maker's long-term growth assumptions. Nvidia's introduction of open-source AI models for autonomous vehicles, Alpamayo, is intensifying competition for Tesla in self-driving AI, diluting its perceived dominance and increasing volatility for leveraged Tesla ETFs. Additionally, increasing competition in adjacent markets like autonomous driving and humanoid robotics, highlighted by Mobileye's acquisition, further pressures Tesla's future growth prospects and the valuations of related ETFs.

Title: New bill tackles safety concerns over Tesla's door handles
Summary: An Illinois lawmaker has introduced a bill, the SAFE Act, to mandate easily seen manual releases and external access for first responders in vehicles with electronic doors, like Teslas. This comes after over a dozen deaths have been linked to passengers being trapped in Teslas after crashes due to inoperable electronic door handles. Consumer Reports supports the bill, emphasizing the need for accessible manual releases even when power fails.

Title: Elon Musk Says Tesla Will Develop 2nm Chip Fab Amid AI Hardware Push
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that the automaker plans to develop its own 2nm chip fabrication facility, emphasizing "atomic level assembly" and unique cleanroom strategies for contamination control. This move comes as NVIDIA unveiled its new Vera Rubin chipset, which Musk believes will take over nine months to become fully operational. Tesla's focus on in-house chip production highlights its commitment to advancing its AI hardware capabilities.

Title: Wedbush Analyst Dan Ives Upbeat on Tesla Inc. (TSLA) Despite Lower Delivery Numbers
Summary: Wedbush analyst Dan Ives maintains an upbeat outlook on Tesla Inc. (TSLA) despite the company's lower-than-expected 2025 delivery numbers, viewing them as a step in the right direction. He forecasts a significant increase in Tesla's market cap, driven by advancements in robotics and autonomous driving, particularly highlighting CyberCab as a key valuation driver. Ives has a $600 price target and an Outperform rating for TSLA.

Title: Tesla Door Design Is Targeted by New US Automotive Safety Bill
Summary: A new US bill, the SAFE Exit Act, proposes requiring manual door releases in all new cars with electric door systems, directly targeting designs popularized by Tesla. The legislation, introduced by Representative Robin Kelly, aims to address safety concerns after incidents where occupants were trapped in vehicles due to electric door failures, including several reported fatalities involving Teslas. The bill follows regulatory probes by NHTSA into Tesla's door designs and Bloomberg News's extensive reporting on the safety risks.

Title: Jensen Huang Says Tesla FSD Is 'State-Of-The-Art,' Explains How Nvidia's Alpamayo Is Different
Summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang praised Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) system as "state-of-the-art" while discussing the differences with Nvidia's own Alpamayo self-driving technology. Huang noted that Alpamayo distinguishes itself by combining vision, radar, and LiDAR, though he considers its underlying technology "rather similar" to Tesla's FSD. The comments come amidst Tesla CEO Elon Musk's remarks on the automaker's AI4 chip investment and Nvidia's strategic investment in Musk's xAI venture.

Title: Elon Musk Teases Extreme Performance Tesla Roadster, Says Safety Is 'Not The Main Goal'
Summary: Elon Musk has stated that the upcoming Tesla Roadster will prioritize extreme performance over safety, likening it to Ferrari vehicles. He hinted that the Roadster could be one of the last human-driven cars before self-driving vehicles become widespread and remained cryptic about its rumored hovering capabilities. The Roadster has been a highly anticipated but elusive topic, with past issues like delayed refunds for reservations.

Title: Leo Michael cartoon: BYD dethrones Tesla for global EV crown
Summary: A cartoon by Leo Michael depicts BYD surpassing Tesla to become the top global electric vehicle seller. The article highlights this shift, emphasizing BYD's new position as the leader in the worldwide EV market.

Title: Qualcomm to provide infotainment tech for new Volkswagen platform
Summary: Volkswagen plans to enter a long-term supply deal with U.S. chip designer Qualcomm to power the infotainment system of its new software platform. The deal, outlined in a letter of intent, makes Qualcomm the primary tech provider for a platform Volkswagen is developing with Rivian, with cars featuring this technology expected to launch in 2027. This partnership is crucial for Volkswagen to compete with rivals like BYD and Tesla in the growing market for software-defined vehicles.

Title: Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X Shares Options Spot-On: On January 7th, 84,072 Contracts Were Traded, With 1.14 Million Open Interest
Summary: On January 7th, Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X Shares (TSLL.US) saw active options trading, with a total of 84,072 contracts traded. Call options represented 67.68% of transactions, while put options accounted for 32.32%. The open interest for TSLL reached approximately 1.14 million contracts, which is 93.02% of the average over the past 30 trading days.

Title: Cybercab spotted on Austin highway as Tesla moves into nighttime testing
Summary: A Tesla Cybercab prototype has been spotted testing on Austin's MoPac Expressway at night, indicating an aggressive push into nighttime highway travel for the autonomous vehicle. This advanced testing follows earlier sightings on busy South Austin streets and precedes a planned 2026 production timeline. The move to highway testing, especially at night, highlights the challenges of autonomous driving and Tesla's reliance on camera-only systems.

Title: US Stock ETF Tracker | Intel leads the tech sector rally, with the triple-leveraged semiconductor ETF surging over 8% and the double-leveraged INTC ETF skyrocketing more than 21%; Q2 revenue surged 250%, pushing the double-leveraged APLD ETF up 35
Summary: Intel's significant surge led a tech sector rally, with the triple-leveraged semiconductor ETF increasing over 8% and the double-leveraged INTC ETF soaring more than 21%.
