This investment follows a mixed reception from shareholders who previously voted against a similar proposal. The company also indicated it would convert part of its Fremont factory to produce Optimus robots, while canceling two EV models.

Title: Musk Says Tesla Needs to Build ‘TeraFab’ to Manufacture Chips
Summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla plans to build a "TeraFab" for manufacturing semiconductors, a move he says is necessary to avert a probable constraint in chip supply within three to four years. This large-scale facility will incorporate logic, memory, and packaging capabilities and signifies a significant expansion for Tesla beyond its traditional electric vehicle manufacturing. The project is expected to cost billions of dollars and will operate domestically.

Title: Amazing Abundance: Tesla's robot-fueled vision for the future (TSLA:NASDAQ)
Summary: Tesla is shifting its focus towards robotics, embodied by its "Amazing Abundance" mission and Optimus robots. This strategic pivot involves ending production of Model S and Model Y to reallocate resources to autonomy and advanced robotics, aiming to reshape economic output. Key risks include battery supply constraints and potential margin compression in the energy sector.

Title: Tesla profit falls again as sales and revenue decline, expenses pile up
Summary: Tesla's profit experienced a significant decline in the fourth quarter of 2025, with net income falling 61% and annual profit dropping 46%, marking the second consecutive year of decline. Despite the financial headwinds, CEO Elon Musk expressed optimism about the company's self-driving projects, including robotaxis and the Cybercab, and the development of the Optimus robot. The company is re-focusing on Full Self-Driving subscriptions while facing challenges like waning EV interest and increased competition.

Title: Tesla kills Model S sedan, Model X crossover to free factory space for Optimus humanoid robot
Summary: Tesla is discontinuing its Model S sedan and Model X crossover to make factory space available for the production of its Optimus humanoid robots. This move signifies a strategic shift by Tesla to prioritize autonomy, robotaxis, and the large-scale manufacturing of humanoid robots over traditional passenger vehicles. The change reflects CEO Elon Musk's vision for the company's future focus areas.

Title: Meta Guidance Lifts Shares 9%; Microsoft Drops 7%, Tesla Edges Up 2%
Summary: Meta Platforms' shares surged 9% in aftermarket trading after the company issued a bullish first-quarter sales forecast that significantly beat analyst expectations. In contrast, Microsoft's stock dropped 7% due to slowing cloud growth and higher-than-expected capital expenditures, raising concerns about its AI investment returns. Tesla also saw a modest 2% gain after beating Q4 earnings expectations, despite reporting its first-ever annual revenue decline.

Title: Tesla plans $20 billion capital spending spree in push beyond human-driven cars
Summary: Tesla plans to significantly increase its capital spending to over $20 billion this year, primarily focusing on ventures beyond traditional electric vehicles for human drivers. This investment targets autonomous vehicles like the Cybercab, humanoid robots, and battery/lithium production, reflecting a strategic shift towards AI-driven technologies. CEO Elon Musk emphasized this is a "very big capex year" for an "epic future," moving away from car production in some factories to prioritize these new business lines, which aim to justify the company's valuation akin to major tech firms rather than automotive manufacturers.

Title: Tesla profit plunges as AI expenses pile up and sales fall
Summary: Tesla's quarterly profit has plummeted by 61% to $840 million, with revenue down 3% and operating expenses soaring 39%, largely due to a slowdown in EV sales and significant investments in AI. Despite the current financial dip, the market remains focused on Tesla's future ventures, including a $2 billion investment in xAI, plans for humanoid robots by 2027, and expansion of self-driving car services, leading to a bump in shares post-announcement. The company is also expanding production infrastructure for Cybercab and Optimus robots.

Title: Tesla co-founder’s company gets Google as investor at $6 billion valuation
Summary: Google has invested in Redwood Materials Inc., a battery recycling and energy storage startup founded by Tesla co-founder JB Straubel, valuing the company at over $6 billion. This investment aligns with Google's strategy to secure more electricity for data centers as demand surges due to artificial intelligence, with Redwood Materials shifting some focus towards grid-scale energy storage.

Title: Direxion Daily TSLA Bear 1X Shares (NASDAQ:TSLS) Short Interest Up 199.3% in January
Summary: Short interest for Direxion Daily TSLA Bear 1X Shares (TSLS) significantly increased by 199.3% in January, totaling 4,696,117 shares. This surge reflects a rise in bearish sentiment towards Tesla, as TSLS is an inverse ETF providing -1x daily exposure to Tesla stock. The fund recently raised its quarterly dividend to $0.0495, indicating a 3.8% dividend yield.

Title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk to stop production of two models, S and X; convert Fremont, California factory to produce robots
Summary: Tesla's CEO Elon Musk announced plans to halt production of the Model S and X in the second quarter of the current year, converting its Fremont, California factory to produce Optimus robots instead. This decision comes as the company's annual profit plunged, losing its position as the largest EV maker, and amid boycotts affecting sales. Despite the financial downturn, Musk is shifting focus towards robotaxis and robotics, with investors showing some optimism due to improved gross profit margins and expansion plans for robotaxi services.

Title: Tesla shares up 1.8% in Frankfurt day after results
Summary: Tesla shares experienced a 1.8% increase in Frankfurt following the company's announcement to invest $2 billion in Elon Musk's AI company, xAI. Additionally, Tesla confirmed that production plans for its Cybercab robotaxi are on schedule for the current year. This rise was consistent with aftermarket trading of Tesla's U.S. shares, which had initially seen a larger gain before paring back.

Title: Tesla Earnings: Progress on Robotaxi and Optimus Shows Real World AI Growth
Summary: Tesla's latest earnings report highlighted significant advancements in its autonomous driving "robotaxi" service and plans for mass production of its Optimus humanoid robots by late 2026. These developments have led Morningstar to raise its fair value estimate for Tesla stock from $300 to $400, driven by increased valuation for robotaxis, autonomous driving subscription software, and the humanoid robot business. Despite this, Morningstar views Tesla shares as fairly valued around 10% above their current estimate, placing them in 3-star territory, acknowledging potential volatility as these new products progress.

Title: Tesla Rival Li Auto's Self-Driving Head Now Leads Robotics Division: Report
Summary: Li Auto's head of autonomous driving, Lang Xianpeng, will now lead the company's robotics research and development as part of a strategic shift. The move comes as Li Auto restructures its internal teams and follows a previously announced $836 million investment in AI. This development aligns with a broader trend among automakers and tech companies, including Tesla and Xpeng, to scale up robotics and autonomous driving efforts.

Title: Microsoft, Meta, Tesla, IBM, SAP, Apple, and More Stock Market Movers
Summary: This article lists some of the major stock market movers, including Microsoft, Meta, Tesla, IBM, SAP, Apple, and Las Vegas Sands. Stock futures were experiencing modest rises on Thursday. This movement occurred despite investors processing numerous Big Tech earnings reports and geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and Iran.

Title: These Stocks Are Today’s Movers: Microsoft, Meta, Tesla, IBM, SAP, Las Vegas Sands, Apple, and More
Summary: Stock futures showed an upward trend on Thursday as investors processed a wave of Big Tech earnings reports. This market movement occurred despite ongoing concerns about escalating tensions between the U.S. and Iran. The article highlights several key movers including Microsoft, Meta, Tesla, IBM, SAP, and Las Vegas Sands.

Title: Tesla to invest nearly $2B in Elon Musk's xAI
Summary: Tesla announced its plan to invest approximately $2 billion in xAI, Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company. This investment involves acquiring Series E Preferred Stock of xAI. The agreement was signed on January 16, 2026.

Title: Tesla Finally Announced the End of an Era
Summary: During its Q4 earnings report, Tesla announced it would stop production of the Model S and Model X cars to convert its Fremont factory to produce Optimus robots. While the company reported a decline in revenue and profits, its stock rose by two percent. This move marks the end of an era for the Model S, which was instrumental in establishing the viability of the electric vehicle market.

Title: Les warrants de Lemonade expireront le 9 février, la NYSE suspendra leur cotation le 5 février
Summary: Lemonade, Inc. (NYSE:LMND) a annoncé l'expiration de 7.846.646 warrants liés à l'acquisition de Metromile, fixée au 9 février 2026, à 17h00. La Bourse de New York suspendra leur négociation après la clôture du marché le 5 février 2026. L'action de Lemonade a affiché une forte performance, et la compagnie continue d'innover, notamment avec un nouveau produit d'assurance pour les véhicules Tesla équipés de la technologie Full Self-Driving.

Title: Tesla Stock Pops Despite Annual Sales Drop, Two Models Canceled
Summary: Despite a significant drop in fourth-quarter profits, revenue, and vehicle sales in 2025, Tesla's stock saw a modest pre-market pop. The company announced the discontinuation of its Model S and Model X vehicles to repurpose manufacturing space for Optimus robots, signaling a major pivot towards AI and robotics. This shift is solidified by a $2 billion investment in xAI, although challenges with market competition and the realization of ambitious AI projects remain.

Title: Numbers don’t lie. Why Tesla is trading S and X lines for Optimus
Summary: Tesla is shifting its focus from electric vehicles to AI and robotics, discontinuing the Model S and X to repurpose factory space for Optimus humanoid robot production. This strategic pivot is driven by the economic potential of robotics, with projections suggesting Optimus could generate significantly more revenue than the older EV models. William Blair maintains a Market Perform rating on Tesla, acknowledging the strategic shift but highlighting execution risks and increased capital intensity.

Title: Tesla reveals plans for $2 billion investment in Musk’s xAI
Summary: Tesla announced plans to invest $2 billion in xAI, the artificial intelligence startup founded by Elon Musk. This investment highlights Tesla's commitment to advancing AI capabilities, potentially integrating xAI's developments into its own autonomous driving and robotics projects. The move further solidifies the ties between Musk's various ventures in AI and technology.

Title: Lam Research stock hits all-time high at 245.17 USD
Summary: Lam Research stock has reached an all-time high of $245.17, marking a 221.72% increase over the past year. The company's market capitalization now stands at $300.92 billion, with its stock trading above its Fair Value and in overbought territory according to InvestingPro data. This surge is attributed to advancements in the semiconductor industry and strategic company initiatives, leading to a generally positive outlook from analysts despite a high P/E ratio.

Title: Elon Musk is pivoting Tesla to AI and robots. Wall Street analysts have their doubts
Summary: Tesla is shifting its focus from being a traditional automaker to an AI and robotics company, an investment many Wall Street analysts view as costly, risky, and slow to yield returns. Despite beating Q4 earnings, analysts are concerned about the "massive investment" and significantly increased capital expenditure planned for 2026, which could lead to significant cash burn. While some see this as a necessary step for Tesla's future growth in areas like robotaxis and Optimus robots, others believe it raises the company's risk profile and may put pressure on its valuation.

Title: First Solar drops 13% on risk of Tesla’s solar push
Summary: First Solar's stock dropped over 13% due to the potential threat of Tesla entering large-scale solar manufacturing. Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced plans for 100 gigawatts a year of solar cell production, which led BMO Capital Markets to downgrade First Solar's stock and cut its price target, citing concerns over long-term pricing and competitive positioning. This move by Tesla could introduce additional supply into the market, potentially pressuring module pricing or acting as an overhang on First Solar's shares.

Title: Stock market today: S&P 500, Nasdaq sink as Microsoft's post-earnings plunge drags tech down
Summary: US stocks, particularly the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, experienced a tech-driven selloff after Microsoft's earnings report spooked investors, causing its stock to plunge over 10%. Despite Meta's strong revenue outlook and subsequent stock gains, concerns about Microsoft's capital spending and slowing cloud sales, alongside Tesla's shift in strategy and first-ever annual revenue decline, contributed to the market dip. Geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran also caused gold and oil prices to rally.

Title: Tesla ending Model S, X production in Q2, CEO Elon Musk says
Summary: Tesla plans to end production of its Model S sedan and Model X SUV in the second quarter of this year, as announced by CEO Elon Musk. The Fremont factory, where these models are currently built, will be retooled for the mass production of Optimus humanoid robots. This decision marks a further shift in Tesla's focus towards autonomous driving, robotaxis, AI compute clusters, and energy storage, highlighting Musk's vision of transforming Tesla into an AI company.

Title: How Tesla's latest report impacts Austin: For one, big changes on Cybertruck
Summary: Tesla's latest earnings report, despite dismal financial results, outlines significant impacts for its Austin operations with a focus on autonomous vehicles and AI. Key takeaways include the expansion of "Robotaxi" services, the development of Cortex 2 supercomputer at Gigafactory Texas, and plans to transition the Cybertruck production line to fully autonomous for cargo delivery, alongside continued in-house cathode manufacturing. These initiatives underscore Tesla's strategic shift toward AI and automation, particularly within its Texas facilities.

Title: Sensor fusion in action: How cameras and LiDAR integrate with radar for safer driving
Summary: This article discusses how sensor fusion, integrating radar, cameras, and LiDAR with AI, is crucial for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous vehicles. It details the specific roles and advancements of cameras and LiDAR in enhancing perception, highlighting GlobalFoundries' contributions to improving their performance, integration, and efficiency through advanced semiconductor technologies. The piece emphasizes that while each sensor has its strengths, their combined operation is essential for safer and smarter driving.

Title: Big Tech Earnings Live: Apple Beats Wall Street Estimates; Meta Stock Surges, Microsoft Plunges After Results
Summary: Apple exceeded Wall Street's revenue and profit expectations, driven by strong iPhone sales, with its stock rising in after-hours trading. Conversely, Microsoft experienced a significant plunge due to concerns about cloud growth slowdown and AI spending, despite beating estimates. Meta Platforms saw its stock surge by over 10% as investors reacted positively to its rosy outlook and successful AI integration efforts, while Tesla shares declined.

Title: Tesla Stock Falls After Q4 Results: New Brand Value Ranking Shows The Worst May Not Be Over
Summary: Despite Tesla's better-than-expected Q4 2025 financial results, the company's full-year results showed a revenue decline and a second straight year of delivery decreases. A new report further indicates trouble ahead for Tesla, as its brand value has fallen 36% to $27.6 billion in 2026, marking the third consecutive year of declines. This brand erosion, coupled with a low recommendation score and competition from other automotive brands, suggests a challenging path forward for Tesla, focusing investor attention more on FSD, robotaxis, and the Optimus bot rather than traditional EV deliveries.

Title: Tesla Pulls Plug on Model S, Model X EVs
Summary: Tesla is discontinuing production of its Model S and Model X electric vehicles after more than a decade of sales. This decision comes as sales have dwindled due to aging designs, internal competition, a growing EV market, and CEO Elon Musk's public activities. The production capacity from the Fremont, California factory will be reallocated to manufacturing Optimus humanoid robots, with a goal of producing 1 million units annually.

Title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX, Tesla, and xAI in talks to merge, according to reports
Summary: Elon Musk's companies, SpaceX, Tesla, and xAI, are reportedly in early talks for a potential merger, with two main scenarios being considered: a merger between SpaceX and Tesla, or SpaceX and xAI. This consolidation could bring products like Grok, X, Starlink, and SpaceX rockets under one entity, potentially aligning with Musk's stated goal of placing xAI's data centers in space. The discussions are further suggested by the recent establishment of two new corporate entities in Nevada.

Title: The economics of Tesla the company are still all about cars. The economics of Tesla the stock are not.
Summary: Tesla's company economics remain car-centric, yet its stock's future is pivoting towards other ventures. The company saw its first annual revenue decline in 2025 due to decreased EV demand, but its Energy Generation and Storage segment grew significantly. Elon Musk plans to shift focus from some EV models to robotics, AI, energy, and self-driving technology, with significant capital expenditures planned for 2026.

Title: Elon Musk is betting Tesla’s future isn’t about cars at all
Summary: Elon Musk is shifting Tesla's focus from electric vehicles to humanoid robots, believing Optimus robots will define the company's future. Despite falling EV sales and increasing competition, Musk announced the discontinuation of Model S and Model X production to convert factories for Optimus manufacturing, projecting 1 million units annually. Critics, however, view this as a distraction from core business, highlighting intense competition in the robot market and Musk's history of overly ambitious timelines.

Title: Tesla beats Q4 expectations, gives upbeat outlook on robotaxi, Optimus - update (TSLA:NASDAQ)
Summary: Tesla exceeded Q4 earnings expectations, with its top and bottom lines beating forecasts, despite a decline in quarterly revenue. The company provided an optimistic outlook for its Cybercab and robotaxi initiatives, as well as its Optimus bot, which helped to overshadow the revenue dip. Analysts noted softening fundamentals but acknowledged that future growth from these new technologies could drive the stock higher.

Title: First Solar (FSLR) Is Down 6.5% After Tesla Details Massive Solar Manufacturing Push - What's Changed
Summary: First Solar's stock dropped over 10% in one day and 6.5% over seven days after Tesla announced plans for a large-scale, vertically integrated solar manufacturing base. This news led BMO Capital to downgrade First Solar to a neutral stance, raising concerns about future competitive intensity, pricing power, and contract wins. Investors are now closely watching First Solar's upcoming earnings report for commentary on module pricing and order visibility.

Title: Tesla Just Killed the Most Important Car of the 21st Century
Summary: Tesla is discontinuing its Model S and Model X vehicles to focus on AI and robotics, specifically the Optimus human robot. While the Model S was instrumental in proving the viability and desirability of electric vehicles, it has become less relevant compared to Tesla's newer, more affordable models. This move signals Tesla's strategic shift away from being primarily a car company towards becoming an AI company, despite the risks associated with unproven technologies like humanoid robots and fully autonomous vehicles.

Title: Insurance Gas Car Rental: Like a Time-Warp after Owning a Tesla Model 3 with FSD
Summary: The author, a Tesla Model 3 owner, recounts his experience renting a Genesis GV70 while his Tesla was in for repairs after hitting a deer. He highlights numerous shortcomings of the Genesis compared to his Tesla, especially regarding autonomous driving features, convenience, and fuel costs, calling the rental experience a "time-warp." The article emphasizes the significant advancements in Tesla's technology, particularly Full Self Driving (FSD), which made the gas-powered luxury rental feel outdated.

Title: Tesla’s energy storage business is growing faster than any other part of the company
Summary: Tesla's energy storage business significantly boosted its recent earnings report, growing faster than any other segment of the company. Despite a decline in EV sales and overall profit, record deployment of energy storage products like Megapack and Powerwall led to a 48% increase in gigawatt-hours deployed in 2025. This segment now contributes nearly a quarter of Tesla's gross profit, demonstrating higher profitability margins compared to vehicle sales, and is expected to continue growing with substantial deferred revenue from ongoing projects.

Title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX Said to Consider Merger With Tesla or xAI
Summary: SpaceX is reportedly considering a merger with either Tesla Inc. or Elon Musk's artificial intelligence firm, xAI, as part of a move to consolidate his various ventures. The company has discussed the feasibility of a tie-up with Tesla, pushed by some investors, and is also exploring a combination with xAI before a potential IPO. These discussions highlight Musk's interest in integrating his companies to leverage synergies, such as SpaceX providing computing capacity for xAI's AI efforts and Tesla's energy storage systems aiding SpaceX's space data centers.

Title: NVDA, MU Top Analog Devices Stock on Price & Potential
Summary: This article analyzes why NVIDIA (NVDA) and Micron Technology (MU) might be more attractive investments than Analog Devices (ADI). It compares key financial metrics like Price/Operating Income, revenue growth, and operating income growth for these semiconductor companies, highlighting that NVDA and MU have lower valuations relative to their performance compared to ADI. The analysis suggests a potential disconnect between ADI's valuation and its growth metrics, prompting investors to consider its peers.

Title: Tesla: Shares Rise on Media Report of Potential Merger With SpaceX
Summary: Tesla shares rose 3% after Bloomberg reported that SpaceX is considering a merger with either Tesla or xAI, potentially consolidating Elon Musk's companies. While such a merger could benefit both Tesla and SpaceX by integrating AI operations and connectivity, Morningstar maintains its $400 fair value estimate for Tesla, considering the stock fairly valued as no deal has been announced. The analysis emphasizes that Tesla's AI development pace, rather than a potential merger, remains the primary driver for its stock value.

Title: Tesla Trades on ‘Elon Musk’s Storytelling’ According to Cramer
Summary: Jim Cramer suggests that Tesla's stock performance is driven by "Elon Musk's storytelling" rather than its earnings, especially since the EV business is struggling. Tesla plans to discontinue its Model X and S lines, focusing on the more affordable Model 3 and Y, and invest $2 billion into xAI for developing robots and self-driving technology. Despite a 3% drop in 2025 revenue, the company is committing $20 billion to capital spending, double the previous year, to advance its self-driving cars and Optimus robot.

Title: Analysts Offer Insights on Consumer Cyclical Companies: Birkenstock Holding plc (BIRK), Tesla (TSLA) and WeRide (WRD)
Summary: This article highlights bullish sentiments from financial analysts on three consumer cyclical companies: Birkenstock Holding plc (BIRK), Tesla (TSLA), and WeRide (WRD). Analysts reiterated Buy ratings for Birkenstock and Tesla, and maintained a Buy rating for WeRide, providing specific price targets and an outlook on each company's potential upside or downside from current levels. The report details the analysts' individual ratings, success rates, and the overall consensus among experts for each stock.

Title: Analysts Offer Insights on Consumer Cyclical Companies: Birkenstock Holding plc (BIRK), Tesla (TSLA) and WeRide (WRD)
Summary: Three analysts have issued bullish sentiments on companies in the Consumer Cyclical sector: Birkenstock Holding plc (BIRK), Tesla (TSLA), and WeRide (WRD). Janine Stichter from BTIG reiterated a Buy rating on Birkenstock, Craig Irwin from Roth MKM reiterated a Buy rating on Tesla, and Tim Hsiao from Morgan Stanley maintained a Buy rating on WeRide, with all analysts providing price targets. The article details the analyst ratings, success rates, and consensus ratings for each company.

Title: Analysts Have Conflicting Sentiments on These Consumer Cyclical Companies: Tesla (TSLA), Greif Class A (GEF) and Starbucks (SBUX)
Summary: Analysts are presenting conflicting sentiments on several consumer cyclical companies. Tesla received a Buy rating from Canaccord Genuity but has an overall analyst consensus of Hold. Greif Class A (GEF) maintained a Hold rating from Wells Fargo, aligning with the general analyst consensus. Starbucks (SBUX) received a Buy rating from RBC Capital and has an overall Moderate Buy consensus.

Title: Tesla confirms that it finally solved its 4680 battery’s dry cathode process
Summary: Tesla has announced a major breakthrough in its 4680 battery production, confirming that it is now using a dry-electrode process for both the anode and cathode. This development addresses long-standing challenges and was highlighted by Tesla's VP of 4680 batteries. The company also revealed that it has started producing battery packs for certain Model Y vehicles using these in-house 4680 cells, providing greater supply chain flexibility for its US production.

Title: Semtech Corporation stock hits 52-week high at $84.00
Summary: Semtech Corporation's stock reached a 52-week high of $84.00, reflecting a 24.55% one-year change and strong investor confidence. The semiconductor company, valued at $7.7 billion, reported 20.6% revenue growth, although its high P/E ratio suggests it might be overvalued. Analysts have maintained mostly positive ratings, adjusting price targets upwards due to the company's focus on high-growth areas and strong fiscal third-quarter results.

Title: The End of the Model S Is the Start of a New Tesla
Summary: Tesla's decision to discontinue production of its Model S marks a significant shift for the company, signaling the end of an influential era for the electric vehicle. The Model S, known for its performance and high-tech features, is being phased out as Tesla pivots towards new priorities, specifically focusing on robots. This move indicates a new strategic direction for the automaker.

Title: Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) Shares Up 4.8% After Analyst Upgrade
Summary: Tesla shares rose 4.8% after UBS Group increased its price target to $352 from $307, while maintaining a "sell" rating. The company's Q4 earnings surpassed expectations, reporting $0.50 EPS against an estimated $0.45, and revenue of $24.90 billion, but also indicated significant planned capital expenditures for 2026, raising concerns about execution and margins. Recent insider selling by executives, including CFO Vaibhav Taneja and Kimbal Musk, also occurred, with insiders offloading 119,457 shares last quarter.

Title: Gigafactory Texas will see production of Tesla robot at 'much higher volume' than California
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has announced that while the Optimus 3 robot will be produced at a California plant, the next-generation Optimus 4 humanoid will be manufactured at Gigafactory Texas in Austin. Musk aims for "much higher volume" production of Optimus 4 in Texas, following the planned unveiling of Optimus 3 in a few months. He shared a goal of producing a million units annually from the California factory, highlighting the advanced capabilities of the robot.

Title: Gigafactory Texas will see production of Tesla robot at 'much higher volume' than California
Summary: Tesla announced that while its Optimus 3 robot will be produced at its California plant, the next-generation Optimus 4 will be built at Gigafactory Texas, with Elon Musk stating it will be at a "much higher volume." Musk aims for a million units annually from the California factory, and while the Model S and X production will end there, Tesla assures no job losses and potential headcount increases as Fremont becomes an "Optimus hub." The company plans to unveil Optimus 3 soon and begin tooling for Optimus 4 production in Texas, eyeing a 2027 start.

Title: Tesla is killing the Model S and Model X to build Optimus robots — and people have thoughts
Summary: Tesla is reportedly discontinuing production of its Model S and Model X luxury vehicles to focus on building Optimus humanoid robots, a shift that has generated significant online debate. This move signifies Tesla's pivot from being solely an electric vehicle manufacturer to a broader tech and automation company, focusing on artificial intelligence and robotics. The decision raises questions among the public and investors about the future of Tesla's automotive lineup, long-term support for existing owners, and the potential risks and rewards of betting on unproven robot technology.

Title: Tesla bulls and bears agree: This is not an auto stock
Summary: Tesla's recent plans to halt production of its higher-end Model S and X vehicles and focus on autonomous driving, robotics, and energy storage have led analysts, both bullish and bearish, to agree that Tesla is no longer just an auto stock. This shift is seen as a move towards "Physical AI" and robotics, despite automotive sales still contributing significantly to revenue and the company's valuation being much higher than traditional carmakers. Analysts express caution about the stock's high valuation and the projected increase in capital expenditures without a clear commitment to delivery growth.

Title: First Solar Shares Rebound As Wall Street Dismisses Tesla Competition Concerns
Summary: First Solar Inc. (FSLR) shares rebounded after Wall Street analysts dismissed concerns about Tesla's solar expansion plans significantly impacting First Solar's earnings through at least 2030 due to cost advantages and supply chain challenges. While Mizuho and Wells Fargo remain optimistic about First Solar, BMO Capital downgraded it to 'Market Perform' due to potential long-term overhang from Tesla's efforts to build a vertically integrated solar manufacturing base. Tesla CEO Elon Musk recently reiterated a target of 100 gigawatts of annual solar manufacturing within three years, causing FSLR shares to dip initially.

Title: Tesla persuades Delaware's top court to slash legal fees in director pay lawsuit
Summary: The Delaware Supreme Court has significantly reduced the legal fees Tesla must pay to shareholder lawyers in a successful lawsuit against the company's directors for overpaying themselves. The court slashed the fees by over $100 million, ordering Tesla to pay $70.9 million instead of the original $176.1 million awarded by a lower court. This decision was influenced by increasing criticism regarding legal fees in Delaware courts, with the Supreme Court stating that the original settlement value had been overstated.

Title: Analysts’ Opinions Are Mixed on These Consumer Cyclical Stocks: Birkenstock Holding plc (BIRK), Tesla (TSLA) and Amazon (AMZN)
Summary: This article summarizes analyst ratings for Birkenstock Holding plc (BIRK), Tesla (TSLA), and Amazon (AMZN), highlighting mixed sentiments in the Consumer Cyclical sector. Birkenstock received a Strong Buy consensus, Tesla a Hold, and Amazon a Strong Buy. The report details specific analyst price targets and success rates for each company.

Summary: This article examines analyst sentiments for Tesla (TSLA), Greif Class A (GEF), and Starbucks (SBUX) in the Consumer Cyclical sector. Summary: This article discusses Elon Musk's recent activities, including reports of a successful Neuralink trial and a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla, alongside Tesla's Q4 earnings. Title: Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X Shares (NASDAQ:TSLL) Sees Significant Increase in Short Interest
Summary: Short interest in Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X Shares (TSLL) rose significantly in January, increasing by 54% to over 30 million shares, representing approximately 9.2% of its outstanding stock. Despite this surge, the short-interest ratio remains low at 0.4 days, indicating quick turnover. The article also notes modest institutional investments, that TSLL recently paid a quarterly dividend of $0.1122, and its current trading price, market cap, and P/E ratio.

Title: NIO stock price slips into weekend as China PMI turns down; Monday’s data in focus
Summary: NIO stock closed lower on Friday, mirroring declines in other U.S.-listed Chinese EV companies, despite Tesla's rise. This downturn occurred as China's official factory survey, the Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), fell below the 50-point mark, indicating a contraction in manufacturing activity. Investors are now looking to early February delivery updates and Monday's upcoming private-sector PMI data for further direction.

Title: Jim Cramer Says Tesla’s Robots and Robotaxi Progress Are the Real Drivers Behind the Stock’s After-Hours Move
Summary: Jim Cramer highlighted Tesla's surprisingly strong fourth-quarter financial results, including beats on top and bottom lines and $1.4 billion in free cash flow, as a key factor in its after-hours stock surge. He emphasized that the anticipation of Tesla's robot and robotaxi introductions is the "real driver" behind investors' enthusiasm, overshadowing past expectations that production and delivery results fell short. Cramer noted that for Tesla, particularly at this time, the specific numbers often matter less than future innovations.

Title: Nvidia's CEO Says the "ChatGPT Moment" for Physical AI Is Here: 1 Move to Make
Summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang declared that a "ChatGPT moment" for physical AI has arrived, particularly with the company's new AI models for autonomous vehicles. Despite the projected $13.6 trillion market for physical AI, Wall Street remains somewhat skeptical due to past unfulfilled predictions for self-driving cars and intense competition from other tech giants like Alphabet and Tesla. Investors looking to capitalize on this trend without betting on a single company might consider a diversified ETF like the Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF (DRIV).

Title: Nio deliveries in January quadruple from a year ago, signaling a strong start to 2021
Summary: Chinese electric carmaker Nio reported a significant increase in January deliveries, quadrupling its volume from the previous year to 7,225 vehicles. This marks Nio's sixth consecutive month of record-high deliveries, although the company still has substantial ground to cover to match market leader Tesla's production. Rival Xpeng also reported a strong month, delivering 6,015 electric cars, for its third-straight record.

Title: First Solar stock (FSLR) steadies after Tesla solar talk jolts sentiment — what to watch next
Summary: First Solar (FSLR) stock steadied after Tesla's solar manufacturing ambitions caused a previous dip, with analysts divided on the long-term impact. Mizuho and Wells Fargo view competitive worries as "overdone" due to the high costs and time required for new U.S. solar supply chains, while BMO Capital Markets downgraded the stock more cautiously. Investors are now looking forward to First Solar's Q4 and full-year 2025 results and 2026 outlook release on February 24th for further clarity.

Title: Tesla already has a complete Robotaxi model, and it doesn’t depend on passenger count
Summary: Tesla has a comprehensive Robotaxi strategy that caters to various passenger counts by utilizing different vehicle types. The two-seater Cybercab will handle the majority of trips, while other Tesla models like the Model Y, Model Y L, and Robovan will serve larger groups. This approach mirrors current transportation methods, unifying diverse vehicles under a single autonomous software and fleet platform.

Title: Tesla: The Most Expensive Story Ever Told (NASDAQ:TSLA)
Summary: The article argues that Tesla (TSLA) stock is overvalued due to struggles in its core automotive business and reliance on declining regulatory credits. Intensifying competition, falling deliveries, and slow new model launches challenge its growth narrative. While energy and services show growth, they are too small to compensate for automotive declines, leading the author to reiterate a sell rating based on the stock's detachment from fundamentals.

Title: Elon Musk Says 'Saving The State' As Delaware Supreme Court Slashes Tesla Legal Fees By Over $100 Million
Summary: The Delaware Supreme Court significantly reduced the legal fees Tesla Inc. owed in a shareholder lawsuit from $176.1 million to $70.9 million, citing an overvalued settlement by a Chancery Court judge. Elon Musk commented on the decision, stating the Supreme Court was "saving the state." This ruling involved Tesla directors agreeing to return $277 million in cash and stock options, though Musk himself was not part of this specific settlement.

Title: Elon Musk is stressing robots over cars. Here are three humanoid parts suppliers that Morgan Stanley recommends
Summary: Elon Musk's increased focus on humanoid robots, marked by Tesla halting some car production to build Optimus robots, is fueling demand for specialized parts. Morgan Stanley identifies three Chinese suppliers—Leaderdrive, Inovance Technology, and Jiangsu Hengli Hydraulic—as key beneficiaries of this emerging market, expecting scalable production of components to precede widespread robot sales. The investment bank has doubled its forecast for China humanoid sales this year, signaling significant growth in the sector.

Title: Weekend Round-Up: GM Motors Earnings, Tesla Triumphs And Autonomous Vehicles Make Headlines
Summary: This automotive industry round-up highlights General Motors' strong Q4 earnings, surpassing analyst estimates, and Tesla's successful Q4 report which boosted its stock and revealed 1.1 million active FSD subscribers globally. Additionally, Pony AI expanded its Robotaxi operations through a new partnership, while Alphabet's Waymo experienced a Robotaxi crash during testing in Los Angeles.

Title: Bye-bye corporate conglomerates. Hello personal conglomerates.
Summary: The article explores the rise of "personal conglomerates" like Elon Musk, drawing parallels to historical figures like Jack Welch of General Electric and Gilded Age robber barons. It details how Musk's diverse ventures, spanning Tesla, SpaceX, xAI, Neuralink, and The Boring Company, mirror the sprawling empires of past industrialists. The author discusses the potential implications of such concentrated wealth and power, including regulatory challenges and the financial concept of a "conglomerate discount."

Title: Elon Musk Says 'Saving The State' As Delaware Supreme Court Slashes Tesla Legal Fees By Over $100 Million
Summary: The Delaware Supreme Court significantly reduced legal fees owed by Tesla Inc. in a shareholder lawsuit from $176.1 million to $70.9 million, prompting Elon Musk to comment that the court was "saving the state." The decision followed a ruling that a lower court had overvalued the settlement when determining attorney fees. Tesla directors had previously agreed to return about $277 million in cash and stock options, though Musk was not part of this settlement, having successfully defended his own compensation in a separate case.

Title: Palantir Billionaire Peter Thiel Sells Nvidia and Tesla, and Buys 2 AI Stocks That Now Account for 61% of His Portfolio
Summary: Billionaire Peter Thiel's hedge fund, Thiel Macro, made significant changes to its portfolio in the third quarter, selling shares of Nvidia and Tesla. Thiel Macro significantly increased its holdings in Apple and Microsoft, which now constitute 61% of the fund's assets, indicating high conviction in their AI potential despite Apple's high valuation and Microsoft's recent stock dip due to AI infrastructure costs. The article suggests cautious investment in Microsoft due to its reasonable valuation after a recent dip, while advising against Apple due to its high price relative to projected earnings.

Title: First Solar stock (FSLR) heads into Monday after Tesla’s 100‑GW solar talk jolts sentiment
Summary: First Solar (FSLR) stock is entering Monday with investor uncertainty after Tesla's announcement of plans for 100 gigawatts a year of solar cell production. While some analysts have downgraded First Solar due to concerns about pricing assumptions and increased competition, others dismiss Tesla's impact as overblown, citing the capital and time required for a U.S.-based solar supply chain. Investors are also anticipating First Solar's fourth-quarter and full-year results, and 2026 guidance, on February 24th.

Title: Elon Musk Fails to Deliver on His Cybercab and Optimus Promises—Again
Summary: Elon Musk has admitted that the early production of Tesla's Cybercab robotaxi and Optimus humanoid robot will be "agonizingly slow," despite previous ambitious promises for mass production and deployment. This admission contradicts his earlier targets for a 2026 Cybercab launch at an affordable price and Optimus robots working in Tesla factories by late 2025. Critics continue to highlight the significant gap between Tesla's self-driving technology and competitors like Waymo, with Tesla's Cybercabs still requiring supervision.

Title: Tesla Sales Slump to Three-Year Low in France, Plunge 88% in Norway
Summary: Tesla Inc. experienced a significant drop in European sales at the start of the new year, with registrations falling sharply in France and Norway. French sales decreased by 42% to a three-year low of 661 cars in January, according to the PFA. In Norway, where Tesla performed well last year, registrations plummeted by 88% during the same month.

Title: Inside Tesla's $20B Capex Plan: How TSLA Is Shaping Its Future
Summary: Tesla plans to significantly increase its capital expenditures to over $20 billion in 2026, up from $8.5 billion in 2025 and $11.3 billion in 2024, to invest heavily in AI, robotics, and autonomy. This spending will fund six new facilities, expand existing factories, and build AI compute infrastructure to support initiatives like full self-driving, robotaxis, and the Optimus robot. With over $44 billion in cash, Tesla is positioning itself as a technology and AI-driven company, a strategy mirrored by other tech giants like Meta Platforms and Nebius, which are also ramping up AI-related capital investments.

Title: Tesla Q4 Earnings: My CliffsNotes On 200+ P/E And Record CapEx (NASDAQ:TSLA)
Summary: Tesla's Q4 2025 earnings show a headline P/E ratio above 200x, but its owner’s earnings-based P/E is significantly lower due to strong underlying cash generation and aggressive growth CAPEX. The company's record $20B+ CAPEX for 2026 is viewed as a one-time, growth-oriented investment in AI, robotics, and new factories. Despite valuation concerns and uncertain returns on CAPEX, the long-term thesis is supported by TSLA’s secular and nonlinear growth potential.

Title: Tesla's Q4 Earnings Call Gave Us An Insight Into Elon Musk's Optimus Ambitions, As Well As Challenges
Summary: During Tesla's Q4 earnings call, Elon Musk announced the discontinuation of Model S and Model X production at the Fremont factory to convert it into an Optimus robot facility, aiming for a million units annually. He highlighted the upcoming third-generation Optimus, emphasizing its general-purpose AI and ability to learn via observation. Challenges include a significant $20 billion CapEx, the need for advanced AI5 chips and "TerraFab" for compute, and growing competition from Chinese robotics companies.

Title: ETFs in Spotlight as Tesla Tops Q4 Earnings, Dips on Revenue Miss
Summary: Tesla reported mixed Q4 2025 results, beating earnings per share estimates but missing revenue expectations and seeing a 3.4% slip in share price after initial gains. The company plans significant capital expenditures, especially in AI and new product development like Cybercab and Optimus, aiming for future growth despite current challenges in the EV market. Several ETFs with high Tesla weightings are highlighted as potential investment avenues for risk-averse investors to gain exposure while diversifying.

Title: China Is The First Country To Ban Tesla-Style Door Handles Over Safety
Summary: China has become the first country to ban Tesla-style, electronically-actuated door handles on EVs due to safety concerns and related incidents. This move, taking effect in 2027, requires mechanical release mechanisms for car doors. The article also covers a significant drop in Tesla sales in Norway, an NHTSA investigation into Ford F-150 transmission issues, and Hyundai's decision not to reacquire its former Russian plant.

Title: Tesla new car sales in Italy jump year-on-year in January, after 2025 drop
Summary: Tesla's new car registrations in Italy saw a significant 75% year-on-year increase in January, following an 18% drop throughout 2025. Despite the monthly volatility due to relatively low sales numbers in Italy, the company sold 713 cars last month, achieving a 0.5% market share. In 2025, Tesla sold 12,847 units in Italy, down from 15,650 in 2024.

Title: Tesla’s Next Move: Why Analysts See Either $500 or $350 Ahead
Summary: Tesla's (NASDAQ:TSLA) future is uncertain as CEO Elon Musk shifts focus from EVs to AI and robotics, leading to widely divergent analyst predictions ranging from $500 to $350 within 12 months. The company's Q4 2025 automotive revenue declined significantly, despite growth in other segments, contributing to a "show-me" narrative for investors as Tesla makes substantial capital investments in its new ventures. Wall Street analysts are sharply divided, with an average price target that actually suggests a decline, reflecting skepticism about Musk's changing priorities and the financial viability of these ambitious projects.

Title: What the Blockbuster SpaceX–xAI Merger Can Mean for Tesla Stock
Summary: Speculation about a potential merger between SpaceX and xAI, initiated by Elon Musk, is generating both optimism and concerns regarding the integration of AI across Musk's various companies, including Tesla. SpaceX recently announced its acquisition of xAI, an artificial intelligence company, in anticipation of a possible midyear IPO for SpaceX stock. The implications of this consolidation for Tesla's stock performance are a key point of discussion.

Title: 3 Cheap Stocks to Buy Now as Small Caps Heat Up
Summary: This article from Morningstar's "The Morning Filter" podcast discusses cheap stocks to buy as small caps heat up, analyzes recent tech earnings from Microsoft, Meta, Apple, and Tesla, and provides insights on other companies like Alphabet, Amazon, Pepsi, Mondelez, and Clorox. The hosts also address listener questions about Adobe and Amphenol, and conclude with three undervalued small-cap stock picks: Sensata Technologies (ST), Terex (TEX), and Mosaic (MOS).

Title: SpaceX bails out xAI in mega-deal — here’s what it means for Tesla
Summary: SpaceX has acquired Elon Musk's AI company, xAI, in a mega-deal reportedly valued at $1.25 trillion, creating a combined entity ahead of a planned IPO. This acquisition notably excludes Tesla, despite its recent $2 billion investment in xAI, which now translates to an indirect stake in the new combined company. The deal raises significant concerns for Tesla shareholders regarding Musk's priorities, the flow of cash, and potential conflicts of interest, as it appears to be a bailout for xAI.

Title: Lemonade Launches Tesla-Specific Insurance Plan
Summary: Lemonade introduced a Tesla-specific car insurance plan charging premiums per mile and halving fees when full self-driving is active, leading to a 21.9% stock surge in January 2026. This data-driven strategy uses Tesla's sensor system and is expected to expand to other self-driving brands, aiming to reduce accident rates, enhance financial performance, and solidify Lemonade's competitive position. Analysts have a mixed outlook on LMND, with an average 1-year price target of $77.60, as Privium Fund Management also increased its stake in the company.

Title: Tesla introduces new Model Y variant in US priced at $41,990
Summary: Tesla has launched a new all-wheel drive variant of its Model Y SUV in the U.S. for $41,990. This introduction comes as EV demand has softened and competition has increased, with Tesla having previously released cheaper versions of the Model Y and Model 3. CEO Elon Musk also recently announced that production of the Model S and X sedans would end to make space for humanoid robot manufacturing.

Title: Tesla introduces new Model Y variant in US priced at $41,990
Summary: Tesla has launched a new all-wheel-drive variant of its Model Y SUV in the U.S., priced at $41,990. This introduction follows Tesla's previous efforts in October to offer cheaper versions of the Model Y and Model 3 to maintain sales volumes after federal EV tax credits ended. CEO Elon Musk also recently announced that the company would cease production of its Model S and Model X sedans to reallocate manufacturing space for humanoid robots.
